name: Odysseys2
notes: Instructions and rubric text match the release page. Titles and categories are browsing labels. Every rubric item has weight 1.

tasks.title: Compare every laptop on two Amazon results pages
tasks.instruction: I want to compare the laptops currently shown on Amazon.com across a broad range of prices. Stay logged out, set the delivery ZIP code to 10001, and search for laptops. Record every laptop listing on the first two results pages in the order shown, including sponsored and repeated listings. Exclude accessories, replacement parts, and separate recommendation sections. Open every retained product page and record the exact name, Amazon product ID (ASIN), RAM, graphics processor (GPU), processor, display size and resolution, weight, storage, screen type, refresh rate, operating system, color, current price without conditional discounts, promotions and their conditions, rating and number of ratings, seller, who ships it, stock availability, selected configuration, and main product URL. Clearly mark any fields you cannot support with evidence. Record result counts, page navigation, filters, sorting, observation time, access failures, seller claims about upgrades, available configuration options, and differences between search listings and product pages. Choose up to 20 distinct laptop model families across the prices you found. Where the exact configuration can be matched to a public manufacturer specification page, check the processor, supported memory limits, storage, display, graphics, operating system, and weight. State the comparison rules and use them to compare the verified laptops for everyday use, portability, gaming or graphics, and value. Explain how missing or conflicting specifications affect each shortlist. Provide the search listings in their original order, a workbook of products and configurations, a table matching ASINs and repeated listings, a table of manufacturer checks, an access and conflict log, and a short laptop comparison explaining the criteria behind it. Do not sign in, enter a street address, add anything to a cart, contact sellers, begin checkout, or purchase anything.

rubric.name: Search location
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows a logged-out Amazon session with delivery set to ZIP 10001 before result capture. Both captured results pages use that location. A missing or unconfirmed ZIP setting does not satisfy this check.

rubric.name: Listings from both pages
rubric.requirement: The ordered list contains every laptop card on results pages one and two, with page, position, sponsored status, and ASIN. Sponsored and repeated appearances remain included; accessories, replacement parts, and separate recommendation sections are excluded. A blocked page is logged as unmeasured, not empty or captured; logging the block does not satisfy the missing page capture.

rubric.name: Half Product Coverage
rubric.requirement: At least half of the distinct retained ASINs have a documented product-page visit or a documented failed attempt. This is a partial-progress check toward the every-product requirement, not complete product coverage. An unmeasured set of ASINs does not satisfy it.

rubric.name: Full Product Coverage
rubric.requirement: Every distinct retained ASIN has a supported product-page record or a documented failed attempt identifying the ASIN and reason. Repeated appearances need only one product-page check. If no ASINs were captured because results were blocked, product coverage is unmeasured, not complete.

rubric.name: Product Data Accuracy
rubric.requirement: Every product record gives a page-supported value or an explicit unsupported marker for exact name, ASIN, RAM, GPU, processor, display size and resolution, weight, storage, screen type, refresh rate, operating system, color, price without conditional discounts, promotions and their conditions, rating and count, seller, shipper, stock, selected configuration, and main product URL. No record borrows another product's data or invents unseen values.

rubric.name: Products and repeated listings
rubric.requirement: The ordered list preserves the original search appearances. The ASIN and duplicate table links recorded ASINs to their corresponding product configurations and identifies repeated listings. No products absent from the search list appear in these records.

rubric.name: Search settings and conflicting information
rubric.requirement: For each accessible results page, the records give displayed result count, page navigation, filters, sorting, and observation time, plus visible seller-upgrade claims, configuration options, and conflicts between listings and product pages. Blocked pages have their access failure recorded. Unavailable count, filter, sort, and conflict fields remain unmeasured, without borrowing from another page or silently combining them.

rubric.name: Manufacturer Verification
rubric.requirement: A manufacturer-check table is provided for the selected model families, which come from the captured results, span the observed prices, and number no more than 20. Exact-configuration matches are supported by retrieved manufacturer pages. For each selected family, the table checks processor, memory limits, storage, display, graphics, operating system, and weight, marking missing or conflicting evidence explicitly. Only supported fields are called verified; a missing table does not pass.

rubric.name: Criteria-Based Brief
rubric.requirement: The comparison report states and applies its rules for everyday use, portability, gaming or graphics, and value to the verified laptops. It explains how missing or conflicting specifications affect each shortlist. If the evidence supports no verified comparison, the report explains that limit rather than inventing one. A missing report does not pass.

rubric.name: Safe Browsing Boundaries
rubric.requirement: The full browsing record shows no sign-in attempt, street-address entry, add-to-cart action, seller contact, checkout step, or purchase.

rubric.name: Supported Final Claims
rubric.requirement: The final response and outputs make only supported claims. Named files exist and contain what is described, reported counts agree with files, manufacturer-check claims have the required evidence, and coverage and ZIP claims agree with the browsing record. Honest disclosure of gaps is acceptable.

tasks.title: Count authors on a set of arXiv papers
tasks.instruction: I'm studying how many authors worked on a small group of arXiv papers, and I need a count someone else can reproduce. Search arXiv abstracts for the exact phrase Privacy in Machine Learning and include only papers submitted from June 5, 2024 through June 7, 2024, including both dates. Check every matching result. Record the exact search and filters, sorting, displayed total and result order, which result pages you covered, and when you checked in UTC. For each paper, record its arXiv ID and version, title, the text around the phrase in its abstract, original submission timestamp, latest revision date, subject categories, displayed author names and count, and source URL. Check every paper against at least one independent public scholarly source: a publisher or proceedings page, Crossref, OpenAlex, DBLP, or an institutional repository. Say which title, authorship, identifier, and date fields that source confirms, keeping facts found only on arXiv separate. Combine repeated records using the canonical arXiv ID, but keep the version history and every disagreement. Use arXiv's version history to decide whether a paper belongs in this group, the publisher or proceedings record for publication details, and the latest arXiv record for the author count. Count contributors as the named authors on that latest record; more than three means four or more. Calculate the number with more than three authors, the total number of qualifying papers, the share, and the distribution of team sizes. Where the original version lists different authors, also show how using that version changes the results. If a source is blocked or missing, record the gap and try another public source; failed access does not prove that something is absent. Provide the arXiv results in their recorded order, a dataset with one entry per paper, a record of checks against other sources and disagreements, and a short summary giving the exact number with more than three contributors and the total number of qualifying papers. Do not sign in, contact authors, submit forms other than public search controls, or collect nonpublic personal data.

rubric.name: Qualifying-paper statistics
rubric.requirement: The brief and all main statistics describe only the papers matching the exact phrase: the number meeting the author threshold, total qualifying papers, share, team-size distribution, and results under any alternative authorship count. Papers matching only individual words, or failing another requirement, are excluded from every statistic.

rubric.name: Complete Search Evidence
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows the exact abstract-phrase search, the June 5 through June 7, 2024 submission-date filter, sorting, displayed total and order, and every result page or end of results. Accessed arXiv records support each decision to include or exclude a candidate. If there are no exact matches, the saved search, filters, and results support that conclusion. Any optional broader search is kept separate. Blocked, cut-off, or incomplete evidence is recorded as a gap, not proof that papers are absent.

rubric.name: Ordered search record
rubric.requirement: The ordered search record gives the exact URL or API query, search field, date range including both endpoints, type of date, sorting, displayed total and result order, pages covered, and observation time in UTC. It includes the main search under every date interpretation used, plus every search whose results or totals support candidate selection, full coverage, or the main count. Exploratory searches that were not used may be omitted. The query, totals, order, and coverage match the browsing record; a search visibly spanning several pages is not described as one page.

rubric.name: Complete Deliverable Set
rubric.requirement: All four requested outputs are present and have the requested structure: an ordered search record, a dataset with the requested fields for each paper, a record of checks against other sources and disagreements, and a team-size brief giving the exact number with more than three contributors and the total qualifying papers. An empty dataset is correct when no papers qualify.

rubric.name: Excluded Paper Labels
rubric.requirement: Every mentioned paper outside the qualifying group is clearly marked excluded or non-qualifying, with the reason given as either not containing the exact phrase or falling outside the date range. Facts found only on arXiv stay separate from facts independently confirmed elsewhere. This check passes if no papers are mentioned.

rubric.name: Accurate Paper Metadata
rubric.requirement: Every reported paper detail agrees with its cited source, including identifiers, titles, abstract phrase context, versions and dates, authors and counts, subjects, and URLs. Repeated records are combined by arXiv ID while version history and disagreements remain visible. Eligibility follows the recorded arXiv history, publication details follow the publisher or proceedings source, and the main author count follows the latest arXiv record. No paper or value is invented.

rubric.name: Independent checks and gaps
rubric.requirement: Each qualifying paper has a documented check against at least one independent public scholarly source, with the confirmed title, authorship, identifier, or date fields named. Missing or blocked sources are logged and another public source is tried. Excluded candidates do not require an extra independent check unless the report claims one. a documented empty qualifying set needs an explicit empty log, not invented checks.

rubric.name: Evidence-Backed Claims
rubric.requirement: The final answer and files make supported claims about searches, source checks, times, counts, ordering, and coverage. Completeness is judged against the recorded search evidence, without assuming the qualifying count is zero. A recording error and an invented verification claim are distinguished using the evidence.

rubric.name: Safe Research Conduct
rubric.requirement: The research does not sign in, contact authors, or collect nonpublic personal data. Public arXiv search and filter controls are allowed, including typing a query, clicking Search or Go, submitting a search form programmatically, opening a results URL, or accidentally running an empty search. Prohibited submissions send personal information or messages to another party, or change something beyond search, such as contact, registration, login, feedback, comments, payment, or upload.

tasks.title: Compare current Mississauga rentals
tasks.instruction: Compare current Mississauga rentals using https://rentals.ca/mississauga as the sole discovery source. Keep all filters at their defaults except location, and sweep every result reachable through pagination or loading during one timestamped research session. Record the applied filters, observation time, reported result total, page or load boundaries, displayed order, and anomalies. For each listing, capture the title, listing ID and URL, price, address, bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage, amenities, availability wording or date, and public leasing phone or email. Check each record on its linked property-manager or building page and on a second authoritative page when one is available. Record each source URL and check time, and keep Rentals.ca observations separate from confirmed facts. Deduplicate by listing ID and by normalized building or address plus unit. Retain syndications and every conflicting value. Resolve derived fields in this order: current official unit page, current manager or building page, then Rentals.ca. Classify availability as current, uncertain, or stale only from explicit dated evidence, never from a missing page. Calculate price per bedroom and per square foot where the inputs exist. Summarize inventory by layout, price band, and neighbourhood, and rank the five best-documented value options with reasons and caveats. Log blocked pages and absent fields as limitations without treating them as evidence that a listing or amenity does not exist. Deliver an ordered source table, structured listing dataset, verification and conflict log, and decision brief with the totals used to calculate coverage and missing-field rates. Do not contact anyone, submit forms other than public search, filter, or lookup controls, log in, collect personal agent details, or claim the observed market is complete beyond the recorded sweep.

rubric.name: Recorded Session State
rubric.requirement: The final result or delivered materials record default filters with Mississauga as the location, an observation timestamp, either or both displayed result totals with clear labels, the displayed order or sort, and the actual page or load boundaries swept. Visible drift, empty pages, or duplicates are logged. Every recorded value matches the browsing record.

rubric.name: All observed listing cards recorded
rubric.requirement: The structured capture contains every result-card observation reached during the recorded sweep across all reachable pages or loads. Every observation includes at least the listing URL, path, or ID; the displayed price or an explicit absence; and its page and displayed position. The browsing record supports the extraction.

rubric.name: Terminal Page Reached
rubric.requirement: The sweep reaches and records the final page or load boundary exposed by the website. Every page or load in the swept range contributes captured cards or has a logged anomaly explaining the gap. A capped API window or early stop cannot be presented as complete.

rubric.name: Duplicates And Conflicts
rubric.requirement: Records are deduplicated by listing ID and normalized building or address plus unit. Duplicate observations and syndications are retained or logged rather than silently removed. Conflicting values remain side by side. The derived-field resolution order is explicitly stated, and where confirmed values exist, derived fields follow that priority: official unit page, manager or building page, then Rentals.ca.

rubric.name: Four Complete Outputs
rubric.requirement: All four materials are visible: an ordered source table, structured listing dataset, verification and conflict log, and decision brief. The dataset has fields for title, ID, URL, price, address, bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage, amenities, availability wording or date, and public leasing contact; logged nulls are acceptable. The brief includes summaries by layout, price band, and neighbourhood, a ranked five-option shortlist with reasons and caveats, and the totals used to calculate coverage and missing-field rates.

rubric.name: Accurate Listing Data
rubric.requirement: Every non-null value in the dataset, summaries, and brief has visible supporting evidence, and every count or coverage statement matches the files. Price per bedroom and price per square foot are calculated only when inputs exist and are arithmetically correct; aggregates follow from the dataset. Failures include claiming a sweep larger than the delivered dataset supports, calling a set unique when it contains duplicates, reporting layout counts that do not sum, contradicting the dataset in the brief, inventing contact values, or otherwise reporting coverage that the files do not support.

rubric.name: Reliable External Checks
rubric.requirement: Every entry described as confirmed is supported by readable external content that was fetched, its source URL, and its check time. Rentals.ca observations remain separate from confirmed facts. Blocked or failed attempts are logged as limitations and are never converted into confirmation or claims of absence.

rubric.name: Manager checks for every discovered listing
rubric.requirement: Every distinct discovered listing is checked on its linked property-manager or building page, with readable fetched evidence, the source URL, and the check time in the browsing record. A listing is excluded from this count only when no such linked page exists or the page is blocked, and that fact is logged as a limitation. For each listing, also check a second authoritative page when available; record attempts and genuine unavailability without inventing confirmation.

rubric.name: Dated Availability Evidence
rubric.requirement: Every current, uncertain, or stale classification is supported by cited explicit dated evidence from a source that was reached. Do not assign blanket current statuses, treat modified timestamps alone as verified currency, or derive a status from a missing or blocked page. Leaving a listing unclassified with a logged limitation is acceptable.

rubric.name: Discovery And Contact Limits
rubric.requirement: Discovery uses only the default Rentals.ca Mississauga results, through any valid site path. The research makes no contact, submits no forms other than public search, filter, or lookup controls, and performs no login. Contact details are limited to the listing’s published leasing contact, and the report does not claim market completeness beyond the recorded sweep.

tasks.title: Inventory Santorini stays on Booking.com
tasks.instruction: Build a dependable current inventory of Santorini accommodation on https://www.booking.com. Search exactly for “Santorini Greece” with check-in and check-out unset, submit the search, and leave the returned destination and date state unchanged. Exhaust the results using every visible load-more control or scrolling until two consecutive checks add no cards. Record the observation time, search state, displayed total, initial and final counts, order, and loading actions. For every captured card, record its displayed name, canonical Booking.com property URL, rank, locality, type, rating, review count, and result-page URL when shown. For every property, seek identity evidence on its official website and one independent public source, such as Greece’s tourism registry or a destination authority. Log the query, candidate URL, matched name, locality, address or coordinates, and outcome. Keep Booking.com observations separate from cross-source findings. Mark identity verified only when independent evidence supports the same property rather than a namesake. Reconcile redirects and duplicates by normalized Booking.com URL and property identity, retaining aliases and conflicts. Prefer official-site identity details over authority records, while Booking.com controls its listing URL and order. Analyze unique coverage by locality and type, verification and duplicate rates, unresolved namesakes, and the gap between displayed total and captured count. If loading or verification is blocked, report the last successful state and affected records without treating failure as absence. Deliver an ordered capture table, cross-source verification log, reconciled inventory, coverage brief, and valid JSON array whose objects contain exactly name and url. Do not sign in, select dates, contact properties, submit forms beyond the search itself, or reserve.

rubric.name: Exact Search State
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows submission of the exact search text “Santorini Greece” with check-in and check-out unset. The destination and date state returned by Booking.com are recorded and left unchanged. A site-normalized destination name is allowed; it need not repeat the typed phrase.

rubric.name: Honest Capture Accounting
rubric.requirement: The materials accurately record observation time, search state, displayed total, initial and final counts, order, and loading actions. Loading either reaches a documented stop after two consecutive checks add no cards or reports the last successful state as blocked or stalled. Any displayed-versus-captured gap is described as uncaptured, not absent, and counts agree across the response and all files.

rubric.name: Ordered Card Table
rubric.requirement: A structured ordered table contains one entry for every captured card. Each entry has all eight field slots: name, canonical property URL, rank, locality, type, rating, review count, and result-page URL. Null is an acceptable value. Coverage follows the captured set rather than the displayed total.

rubric.name: Accurate Booking Fields
rubric.requirement: Every Booking.com value in the table and inventory matches the captured page, including displayed names, localities, ratings, and review counts, and URLs taken from captured links. Type remains null unless a source provides it. No value is inferred, defaulted, or hardcoded.

rubric.name: Dual-source attempts for every captured property
rubric.requirement: Every distinct captured property receives both an official-site check attempt and an independent public-source check attempt. Each attempt is documented in the browsing record and logs the query, candidate URL or none found, matched name, locality, address or coordinates or explicit unavailability, and outcome. Honest failed or not-found attempts count as attempts, never as verified identities; fabricated entries and unattempted checks do not. A smaller captured population is evaluated against all of that population, not an absolute ten-property minimum.

rubric.name: Honest Identity Verification
rubric.requirement: The verification log, reconciled inventory, coverage brief, and final response claim only evidence that was actually obtained. They contain no invented candidate URLs, addresses, coordinates, or matches, and no verified identity without official and independent support for the same property. Source-observed candidate URLs may be logged as “discovered, not fetched,” without claiming their contents were inspected. Blocked or rate-limited outcomes require a concrete block record, and unattempted properties cannot be described as blocked, verified, or absent.

rubric.name: Property Reconciliation
rubric.requirement: The reconciled inventory keeps Booking.com observations separate from cross-source findings. It reconciles duplicates and redirects by normalized Booking.com URL and property identity, retains aliases and conflicts, prefers official-site identity details over authority records, and preserves Booking.com’s own listing URL and order.

rubric.name: Derived Coverage Analysis
rubric.requirement: The coverage brief analyzes unique properties by locality and type, verification rate, duplicate rate, unresolved namesakes, and the displayed-versus-captured gap. Every statistic is derived from and agrees with the reconciled inventory. Capture-count consistency is covered under A2 and is not counted again here.

rubric.name: Exact JSON Format
rubric.requirement: A valid JSON array is delivered. Every element is an object with exactly the keys `name` and `url`. The array covers the reconciled captured inventory, and every name-and-URL pair is supported by captured evidence.

rubric.name: Booking Safety Limits
rubric.requirement: The research never signs in, selects check-in or check-out dates, contacts a property, submits a form beyond the search itself, or starts a reservation. Dismissing modals, closing calendars, and clicking load-more controls are allowed.

tasks.title: List every reachable counsellor in Wiltshire
tasks.instruction: I'm helping a family member find a counsellor in Wiltshire and want to know everyone listed and reachable, not just the first few results. Search the public UK Counselling Directory for therapists located in Wiltshire and go through all the filtered results, however the site divides them into pages. Record the total the site shows and where the results end. Include each practitioner once, using their profile URL to identify duplicates. Check repeated names or shared clinic phone numbers rather than assuming they mean the same person. For each practitioner, record their full name as displayed, public practice phone number, own website, directory profile URL, town or area shown, and whether the listing is an advertisement or the profile no longer works. Leave unpublished information blank. Open each practitioner's own website to check the accreditation body named on their directory profile, their Wiltshire location, and whether they accept new clients. Put the directory's claims and the website's claims in separate columns. If they disagree, keep both and use the practitioner's website for their current status. Record the date and time you check the listings and each website, since availability and fees can change. If a profile or website does not load, record its URL, the time, and what went wrong, and mark the affected information unverified. Provide a CSV with Name, Phone Number, Website, Counselling Directory URL, and the verification columns; a record of the results and pages covered; a table of disagreements; and a shortlist of ten practitioners ranked by the strength of the evidence, with published accreditation and a confirmed Wiltshire practice. Do not create an account, submit enquiry or contact forms, message therapists, or collect client names, reviews of individuals, or anything beyond publicly posted practice contact details.

rubric.name: Complete page coverage
rubric.requirement: The record of results and pages covered identifies the search, the site's total shown in the saved evidence on the recorded research dates, and where the results end, including the final page and its number of listings. Every number agrees with the saved evidence.

rubric.name: Complete practitioner list
rubric.requirement: The data includes every distinct practitioner returned by the search. Displayed total, raw result placements, and distinct profile counts are recorded separately. Coverage is checked against the run's captured result pages through their documented boundary, and any difference between those counts is explained or left explicitly unresolved rather than forced to equality. Each profile URL appears once, different practitioners are not wrongly combined, and no row comes from outside the search. The browsing record supports complete coverage. Disclosing missing results honestly does not make an incomplete list complete.

rubric.name: Accurate directory details
rubric.requirement: For every row, the name as displayed, public practice phone, directory profile URL, town or area, advertisement status, and nonworking-profile status agree with the directory evidence. Unpublished information is blank. Information is not claimed from profiles that were never opened, although information visible on saved search listings may come from those listings.

rubric.name: Practitioners' own websites
rubric.requirement: Every filled Website field links to the practitioner's own website. It does not contain site navigation links, booking platforms, editors, social-media pages, or incorrectly formed values. The field is blank if no valid own website is available.

rubric.name: Supported website checks
rubric.requirement: Every reported website check of accreditation, Wiltshire location, or new-client status accurately describes a practitioner's own website that the browsing record shows was opened. Information from unchecked websites is blank or marked unverified. No claim is taken from a website that was not opened. For each discovered practitioner with a valid listed own website, the browsing record shows a relevant website check or a documented failed attempt. Shortlist checks alone do not establish this coverage; unattempted websites remain explicitly incomplete.

rubric.name: Directory and website disagreements
rubric.requirement: Directory and website claims have separate fields. The disagreement table retains both values for every conflict found and uses the practitioner’s website for current status. If no conflict was found, it says so. Missing website checks are recorded as gaps rather than treated as agreement.

rubric.name: Check times and access failures
rubric.requirement: The files record the date and time of the directory-listing research separately from the website checks. Every profile or site that failed to load has its URL, check time, and failure recorded, and affected claims are marked unverified. If the evidence shows no failures, the two sets of check times are enough.

rubric.name: Ten qualifying practitioners
rubric.requirement: The shortlist ranks ten practitioners by the strength of the evidence. Each has an accreditation body named on their own website, which was visibly checked, and a confirmed Wiltshire practice. Any ten may be chosen; the quality of that choice is not scored. Blank, unverified, or non-Wiltshire entries do not count. Fewer than ten is acceptable only if a completed verification pass finds fewer qualifying practitioners; extracting only two rows because of a failure is not enough.

rubric.name: Required files and columns
rubric.requirement: The files include a CSV with Name, Phone Number, Website, Counselling Directory URL, and separate columns for checking directory and website claims. They also include the record of results and pages covered, the disagreement table, and the shortlist. Reasonable variations in column names are acceptable. This check only assesses structure and naming.

rubric.name: Honesty and privacy
rubric.requirement: The delivered files and final response make no unsupported claims about coverage, verification, nonworking profiles, or completeness. No account is created, no enquiry or contact form is submitted, no therapist is messaged, and no client names or reviews of individuals are collected. Informal working notes are not treated as final reported claims.

tasks.title: Learn which clues win OpenGuessr rounds
tasks.instruction: I want to understand which visual clues help me make fast, accurate OpenGuessr guesses. Play five consecutive rounds in one free logged-out session at https://openguessr.com, or complete all the rounds if the selected mode offers fewer than five. Record the map or mode, settings used, round order, number of rounds offered and completed, access state, and when you played. For each round, keep the visible scene evidence, a short explanation of your country and region guess, the country and region guessed, the submitted pin location, the location revealed by the game, distance in kilometers, and score out of 5000. Check relevant claims about language, road signs, driving side, plates, vegetation, terrain, architecture, and business text against public official language, transport, geographic, or mapping sources. Keep what you saw, what those sources confirm, and what OpenGuessr reveals separate. Record differences in place names, country or region, intended and actual map pins, rounded distances, and the interface and result. Keep both values and explain which source you use for each field. Compare the rounds by accuracy, score, time taken to decide, available clues, and how reliable those clues were. Explain recurring mistakes and choose exactly three clue types to guide the next game when speed matters. Provide a round-by-round table, a structured results dataset, a record of clue checks, a list of conflicting information, and a short performance report with evidence links. If a scene, result, or checking source is unavailable, record the problem and continue with accessible evidence; failed access does not show that something is absent. Do not sign in, create an account, submit personal data, buy anything, or use iframe URLs, coordinates, network responses, hidden state, or other page data containing the answer to work out a location.

rubric.name: Game Session Record
rubric.requirement: The records give the map or mode played, settings used, round order, rounds offered and completed, logged-out access state, and observation time. Available interface evidence supports the recorded settings and access state; a particular settings dialog is not required.

rubric.name: Completed round records
rubric.requirement: For every completed round, the round table records visible scene evidence, submitted guess, revealed result, distance in kilometers, and score. It references scene and result captures when available. If either is unavailable, it records the access problem rather than claiming the missing item does not exist.

rubric.name: Final Three Rounds
rubric.requirement: Each offered round among the third, fourth, and fifth consecutive rounds belongs to the same logged-out session. An actual guess is submitted from visible scene clues. The record retains the visible scene and result evidence; a genuinely unavailable result or distance is logged under the instruction’s missing-evidence rule, not invented. Stopping before an available round is completed does not satisfy this check.

rubric.name: Accurate Round Records
rubric.requirement: The round table and dataset agree with visible evidence. Scene notes match the captured scene, and guessed country and region match reasoning recorded before the reveal. The pin is the one actually submitted; intended and actual positions are separate where needed. The revealed location matches the visible result, and distance is copied exactly within the allowed display tolerance. No coordinates, place names, or scene details are invented.

rubric.name: Clue Check Evidence
rubric.requirement: Relevant claims used about language, road signs, driving side, plates, vegetation, terrain, architecture, or business text have recorded checks against appropriate public official or mapping sources, or documented source gaps. Each successful check names the consulted source, links its evidence, and states what it confirms. Observed clues, outside confirmation, and game-revealed results stay separate.

rubric.name: Round conflicts
rubric.requirement: Each conflict keeps both values and identifies which source is used for the field. Significant visible differences, including intended versus actual pins, place-name variants, and differences between the interface and its reading, are recorded. They are not silently removed or blamed on an invented platform bug.

rubric.name: Round performance report
rubric.requirement: The report compares played rounds by accuracy, score or the recorded barrier to seeing it, time to decide, clue availability, and clue reliability. Descriptive timing or unavailable timing is acceptable when time was not measured. It identifies recurring mistakes and exactly three clue types for the next speed-focused game, based on the recorded rounds rather than generic advice.

rubric.name: Visible Clues Only
rubric.requirement: Before each guess, hidden answer-bearing data must not be read or used to determine the location. This includes answer-bearing iframe URLs, internal map objects, marker coordinates, network responses, and hidden state. Reading text actually visible in the interface, including equivalent accessibility or DOM text, is permitted. After the game reveals the result, the already visible result may be recorded and checked using public outside sources. A post-reveal record does not authorize use of hidden answers for any subsequent guess.

rubric.name: Honest Safe Gameplay
rubric.requirement: The session stays logged out, with no sign-in, account creation, personal-data submission, or purchase. Unmeasured timing is not called measured, and a score hidden behind an access restriction is not called displayed or official. Claims such as “visual evidence only” agree with the browsing record. Access problems remain labeled as such and are not called platform bugs without evidence.

rubric.name: Five separate outputs
rubric.requirement: All five outputs are identifiable and separate: round table, structured results dataset, clue-check log, conflict list, and performance report. The dataset is parseable CSV, JSON, or an equivalent structured format. The final response gives the outputs' locations.

tasks.title: Trace DTE Energy capital shifts, 2022 to 2023
tasks.instruction: Determine whether DTE Energy shifted capital from regulated utilities toward nonutility businesses between 2022 and 2023. From DTE Energy’s investor-relations reports archive, capture every MD&A “Capital Investments” or equivalent table and linked narrative in the 2023 and 2022 Form 10-K reports that shows year-over-year capital expenditures for DTE Electric, DTE Gas, and DTE Vantage or Other, including renamed or combined labels. Record report year, filing date, table or section title, page, printed segment label, fiscal period, actual or planned basis, units, amount, disclosed total, relevant footnote, exact search terms, hit count, inspection order, and observation time. Verify every number and definition against the matching SEC filing and any first-party earnings supplement or investor presentation for the same period. Keep each source’s observation and citation separate from verified facts. Reconcile duplicates, label changes, restatements, rounding, units, totals, and actual-versus-planned figures. Preserve conflicts with explanations, prefer filed 10-K actuals to summaries, and apply later official restatements. Calculate each comparable segment’s 2022-to-2023 dollar and percentage change, share of total in both years, contribution to total change, and tie-out to disclosed totals without combining unlike bases. Rank growth contributions, determine the regulated-versus-nonutility allocation direction, identify the most useful disclosure, and state material caveats. Deliver a source table, segment-year dataset, verification and reconciliation log, and concise capital-allocation brief with cited tables. Log blocked or missing public sources and use the best public official alternative without treating failed access as absence. Do not log in, submit forms, buy anything, or collect personal data.

rubric.name: Target Filings Identified
rubric.requirement: The work correctly identifies DTE Energy's 2023 and 2022 Form 10-K reports through the investor-relations archive or SEC EDGAR and records each report year, filing date, source URL, and discovery evidence. The dates and documents must match the accessed official records; no filing date is assumed in advance.

rubric.name: Capital investment tables
rubric.requirement: The work captures every MD&A Capital Investments or equivalent table and linked narrative in both reports for DTE Electric, DTE Gas, and DTE Vantage or Other, including renamed or combined labels. Every row records its fiscal period, printed segment label, units, amount, disclosed total, relevant footnote, and whether the source presents it as actual or planned. Values and basis labels match the cited pages rather than a predetermined answer.

rubric.name: Filed Segment Actuals
rubric.requirement: The dataset records the actual capital-expenditure values for DTE Electric, DTE Gas, and DTE Vantage or Other from the relevant 2022 and 2023 MD&A capital-investment tables or equivalent disclosures, and verifies them against the matching SEC filings. It preserves the printed labels, fiscal period, units, disclosed totals, and extraction evidence. Renamed or combined labels remain visible, and values from a different basis are kept separate rather than substituted or reconstructed as an unsupported residual.

rubric.name: Two-Year First-Party Check
rubric.requirement: The 2022 and 2023 filed observations are checked against any applicable first-party earnings supplement or investor presentation for the same period. Each source's values, labels, units, and basis remain separate from the filed facts, and missing or inaccessible first-party material is logged without inventing a match.

rubric.name: Filed-Basis Calculations
rubric.requirement: Using only comparable filed 10-K actuals, the work calculates each segment's 2022-to-2023 dollar and percentage change, share of total in both years, contribution to total change, and tie-out to the disclosed totals. Any regulated-versus-nonutility aggregation is defined from the recorded segment labels, and all arithmetic matches the sourced inputs and displayed precision without mixing unlike bases.

rubric.name: Conflict Basis Discipline
rubric.requirement: The reconciliation keeps filed actuals, planned figures, and presentation summaries on their own stated bases. Every discovered conflict, label change, restatement, rounding difference, unit difference, or total mismatch is preserved and explained; any proposed cause is clearly presented as uncertain unless supported. Filed 10-K actuals take priority over summaries, and later official restatements are applied while the original values remain visible. The final allocation conclusion uses comparable filed actuals and does not silently combine unlike measures.

rubric.name: Accurate Source History
rubric.requirement: All search terms, hit counts, source-access outcomes, observation times, and inspection order are supported by the browsing record. Blocked or failed sources are reported as shortfalls rather than completed inspections. No verification is claimed for an uninspected source. Reported source details are not invented. The work does not log in, submit forms, make purchases, or collect personal data.

rubric.name: Four Structured Deliverables
rubric.requirement: All four requested materials exist in structured form: source table, segment-year dataset, verification and reconciliation log, and capital-allocation brief. Table and dataset records include report year, filing date, section title, page, printed label, fiscal period, actual or planned basis, units, amount, disclosed total, and applicable footnote; an explicit blank is acceptable. Source observations remain separate from verified and reconciled facts.

rubric.name: Complete Allocation Conclusion
rubric.requirement: The brief answers whether capital shifted toward regulated utilities or nonutility businesses using comparable filed 10-K actuals. It ranks each segment's contribution to the total change, names the most useful disclosure and explains why, and states the material caveats supported by the evidence. Every citation points to the content it is used to support.

tasks.title: Read a school district teachers contract
tasks.instruction: I'm researching the current labor agreement for certificated employees at Strathmore Union Elementary School District in Tulare County, California. Find the latest publicly available signed collective bargaining agreement and every later memorandum, side letter, salary schedule, or board-approved amendment that could still change its current terms. Also find the immediately preceding agreement or salary schedule when available so I can see what changed. Make a document table giving each title, the parties, effective and expiration dates, board approval date, whether it is signed, its source, which documents it replaces or is replaced by, and the provisions it changes. Work through the clauses to determine which documents currently govern each term. Keep track of unsigned drafts, missing attachments, inconsistent dates, and unclear language about terms continuing. Summarize compensation, benefits, work year and hours, leave, class size or workload, evaluation, transfers, discipline, and grievance procedures, citing the exact document and page for each point. Compare salary schedules using matching columns and steps. Calculate published percentage or dollar changes only where the schedules are comparable, and distinguish negotiated changes from legal requirements or administrative material. Provide clearly named copies of the official documents, the document-status table, a table of current terms, a table comparing previous and current terms, and a short memo about the agreement. If collecting the files into a bundle is not appropriate, provide structured tables and links instead. Explain why the documents you selected are current and clearly identify every remaining gap.

rubric.name: Current governing documents
rubric.requirement: The results identify and explain the official signed agreement and every later memorandum, side letter, salary schedule, or board-approved amendment that the evidence shows could still affect current certificated-employee terms. Every term treated as current is tied to an official source. Previous terms are not presented as current.

rubric.name: Predecessor Documents Retrieved
rubric.requirement: Official public sources identify and retrieve the immediately preceding certificated agreement or salary schedule when available, and support its status and relationship to the current documents. Previous and current terms remain separate. Unavailable predecessor material is recorded as a source gap; obtaining both document types, amendments, or reopeners is not mandatory unless separately requested.

rubric.name: Later Board Actions
rubric.requirement: The research checks relevant public board records or other official district records for later certificated-employee settlements, amendments, reopened negotiations, salary decisions, and related documents. Each finding has a stated status and source. If an official archive or folder cannot be displayed, the report identifies the exact access gap and limits claims that something was absent to the records actually reviewed.

rubric.name: Complete Status Index
rubric.requirement: The document-status table includes every agreement, memorandum, side letter, salary schedule, and amendment found to affect current terms, plus the preceding agreement or schedule when available. Each row gives title, parties, effective and expiration dates, board approval date, signature status, source, replacement relationships, and provisions changed. Unavailable fields are explicitly marked.

rubric.name: Accurate Document Metadata
rubric.requirement: Every title, party, effective or expiration date, board approval date, signature status, source, and replacement relationship in the document-status table matches the verified official material. Missing or inconsistent dates, unsigned drafts, unclear continuation language, and conflicts between signatures and document text are kept when found, rather than replaced with assumed fixed answers.

rubric.name: Cited Current Terms
rubric.requirement: The current-terms table covers compensation, benefits, work year and hours, leave, class size or workload, evaluation, transfers, discipline, and grievance procedures. Every stated term matches its cited official document and page. If a required document is missing or inaccessible, the affected topics are marked unavailable or not located, with the missing document identified. No clause text or page is guessed.

rubric.name: Comparable Salary Changes
rubric.requirement: The comparison of previous and current salary schedules uses genuinely comparable columns and steps, or a clearly justified comparable subset. Percentage or dollar changes have evidence, schedules that do not align stay separate, negotiated changes are distinguished from legal or administrative material, and the comparison's limits are stated.

rubric.name: Five Delivered Materials
rubric.requirement: The user receives all five requested outputs: official document files or structured tables and links; the document-status table; the current-terms table; the previous-to-current change table; and the labor-agreement memo. The final response summarizes the result.

rubric.name: Honest Gaps And Scope
rubric.requirement: The results claim only work and checks shown in the browsing record. Claims of reviewing every set of minutes, checking a signature page, or confirming that a document governs current terms require evidence. Significant gaps found during research are identified, including signing or dating defects, board material not posted or not reviewed, and unresolved provisions for reopening negotiations actually encountered. Claims that something is absent are limited to the sources searched.

rubric.name: Clear Document Presentation
rubric.requirement: The document files or linked alternatives have clear names. The requested structured information appears in identifiable tables, and citations identify the document and exact page where available. No particular citation style, filename pattern, or bundle format is required.

tasks.title: Find Estonian GovTech startups to back
tasks.instruction: I'm considering investing alongside others in early-stage Estonian GovTech startups and need a list supported by public evidence. Build a CSV of startups founded or headquartered in Estonia whose main product serves public-sector customers, such as agencies, municipalities, courts, defence, public health, education, or state digital infrastructure. Exclude consultancies and state-owned bodies, and keep adding companies while you can support their inclusion with evidence. Continue through official business registry records, funding databases, accelerator and startup-visa lists, exhibitor lists, and company websites. For every company, record its legal name, registry code, website, founding year, a one-line description of its GovTech product, evidence of a public-sector customer or contract, latest funding stage, last funding round's date and amount, named investors, and operating status. Use these stage labels: pre-seed, seed, Series A or later, grant-only, bootstrapped, or undetermined. Flag companies with no public sign of activity in the 24 months before you start. Give sources and check dates for each field. Check stage and operating status against two independent sources. Keep conflicting funding-round labels or amounts side by side rather than combining them. Mark information you cannot establish as unverified instead of estimating it, and record excluded companies with the reasons. If a registry or database blocks access, record the attempt, use the next-best public evidence, and mark the affected information as less well supported. Provide the CSV, a separate list of pre-seed and seed companies ranked by evidence of public-sector customers or contracts, and a note explaining where you searched and what gaps remain. Do not create accounts, sign into paid data platforms, contact founders, buy reports, or collect personal data.

rubric.name: Evidence for eligible companies
rubric.requirement: Every CSV row is a real company founded or headquartered in Estonia whose main product serves public-sector customers. It is neither a consultancy nor a state-owned body. Visible evidence supports each reported legal name, registry code, and public-sector customer or contract. Fields honestly marked unverified are acceptable. Values described as sourced must have evidence showing where they were collected.

rubric.name: Accurate company details
rubric.requirement: Every reported founding year, stage, last-round date and amount, named investor, and operating status matches visible source information. Stage is pre-seed, seed, Series A or later, grant-only, bootstrapped, or undetermined. Conflicting round labels or amounts are kept side by side, not combined or silently chosen between. Each company has the requested flag for no documented activity in the preceding 24 months, based on dated public activity evidence and the observation date. Insufficient evidence is labeled undetermined, not proof of inactivity.

rubric.name: Sources and check dates
rubric.requirement: Every filled field has a source that can be found and a check date, recorded for that field or its row. For stage and operating status, the record shows attempts at two independent public sources and identifies the fields each supports. A missing or blocked second source is documented as a gap, not a successful check. Information supported by only one source or a substitute source is marked less well supported. Blocked or impaired sources are recorded with the attempted source and the named substitute. General names such as “Crunchbase” or “news” without a usable source location are not enough.

rubric.name: Honest research claims
rubric.requirement: The files and coverage note accurately describe the sources checked, companies found, and remaining gaps. Claims of two independent sources or verified facts have supporting evidence. Unestablished fields remain unverified, not estimated. Any analytical assumption is clearly labeled and is not substituted for a requested factual field.

rubric.name: Required startup files
rubric.requirement: All required files are present and can be read correctly in their stated formats: the main CSV with every requested field, where null or unverified is acceptable; a ranked list of pre-seed and seed companies explaining the ranking; a note on search paths and gaps; and a list of excluded companies with reasons. The exclusion list may be included in another clearly identified file.

rubric.name: Breadth of company discovery
rubric.requirement: The search record shows research across official business records, public funding databases, accelerator and startup-visa lists, exhibitor lists, and company websites. It identifies the sources or searches used, supported additions, exclusions, and remaining gaps. Blocked sources have recorded attempts and public substitutes. A fixed remembered company list or work limited to one convenient source does not satisfy the requested search breadth.

rubric.name: Explained inclusion and ranking
rubric.requirement: Each one-line description explains how the product serves the public sector. The pre-seed and seed list states and consistently applies a ranking based on evidence of public-sector customers or contracts. Every reason for excluding a company is genuine.

rubric.name: Research access limits
rubric.requirement: No account is created, no paid data platform is signed into, no founder is contacted, no report is bought, and no personal data is collected. Public pages or snippets from paid platforms may be read, but no particular paid platform is required.

tasks.title: Match Walmart stores to food-inspection records
tasks.instruction: I want to understand how Walmart locations appear in the Marion County Public Health Department's public food-inspection database and whether those records agree with Walmart's store information. Search the official database for Walmart and record the query, result order, count, and observation time. List every establishment returned. If the site offers a public CSV or spreadsheet export, download it once and record its URL, format, headers, row count, and file hash. Otherwise, work through all public results and record where pagination ends. For each retained establishment, record the displayed name, full address, facility or record identifier, record type, operating status, public detail link, and all inspection or status history the county exposes. Keep event types, dates, outcomes, and unavailable fields separate. Match records to establishments using addresses, facility identifiers, naming variants, Walmart's public directory, and relevant Marion County or Indiana government records. Do not combine a store, pharmacy, fuel station, or distribution facility just because they share a brand or parcel. Preserve differences between county and retailer records about identity, closures, moves, and operating status. Identify unrelated businesses and duplicate result variants and explain each decision. Provide a complete establishment and history dataset, an export or results-traversal log, a table showing how records match establishments, a list of source conflicts, and a coverage summary by establishment type and status. Use only public records. Do not contact establishments or infer inspection outcomes from missing details.

rubric.name: Frozen Walmart Query
rubric.requirement: The record identifies the official Marion County food-inspection database, the Walmart query, observed order, result count, and observation time. It shows the results boundary through the official export or complete public results traversal. If a displayed count is unavailable, it is marked unavailable and any count calculated from retrieved rows is labeled as calculated.

rubric.name: All returned establishments
rubric.requirement: The structured establishment dataset includes every record from the recorded query. None is dropped, and no establishment outside that query is silently included. Mentioning an establishment only in prose does not count as a structured entry.

rubric.name: Accurate County Records
rubric.requirement: For each retained establishment, displayed name, full address, facility or record identifier, record type, operating status, and public detail link match the accessed county source. Unpublished fields are marked unavailable. Status is not inferred from missing history or details.

rubric.name: Complete Inspection Histories
rubric.requirement: Each retained establishment has its full exposed history, including every page of the detail-page inspection table. Capturing only the first page of a multi-page history is incomplete, however it is labeled.

rubric.name: Separate History Fields
rubric.requirement: Each captured history event has separate type, date, and outcome or result fields matching the county source. Empty or withheld comments are marked unavailable, never interpreted as compliance or “no problems.”

rubric.name: Honest Export Record
rubric.requirement: If a public CSV or spreadsheet export is offered, it is downloaded once and the record gives its source URL, format, headers, row count, and calculated file hash. If no export is offered, the record documents complete traversal of the public results and where it ends. A download failure is an explicit gap, not a completed export. An agent-built CSV is not called the county’s own export.

rubric.name: Walmart Entity Matching table
rubric.requirement: Every county result is checked against Walmart’s public directory and relevant Marion County or Indiana government records, with attempts and gaps recorded. Address, facility identifier, naming variants, and any published store number support each match. Stores, pharmacies, fuel stations, distribution facilities, unrelated businesses, and duplicate result variants remain separate unless evidence supports joining them. Each match, exclusion, duplicate decision, or unresolved identity has a stated basis.

rubric.name: County Retailer Conflicts
rubric.requirement: The conflict list keeps every county-versus-retailer difference found in the matching table, including identity, naming, address format, and status. Every entry gives an explicit reason, and neither side is silently discarded.

rubric.name: Five Structured Outputs
rubric.requirement: All five outputs exist in identifiable structured form: establishment and history dataset, export or results-traversal log, record-matching table, source-conflict list, and coverage summary by establishment type and status. Status may be unavailable or counted only where a source displays it. The work uses public records only, does not contact establishments, and does not infer inspection outcomes from missing details.

tasks.title: Rebuild LEGO Fallingwater 21005
tasks.instruction:
I’m rebuilding LEGO Architecture Fallingwater set 21005. Please create an evidence-backed parts checklist for instruction steps 1–10, paying special attention to the gray brick added in step 3. Use LEGO’s official instruction PDF as the authority. For every piece added, record the step, page, visible quantity, depicted shape and color, subassembly context, and a cropped or precisely referenced instruction view. Provide both per-step additions and a cumulative bill of materials. Reconcile repeated pieces and page turns, and do not count pieces that were added in earlier steps but remain visible.

Cross-check candidate design, element, color, and set-inventory identifiers against both BrickLink and Brickset. Preserve each source’s terminology, extras, alternates, and conflicts instead of overriding the instruction image. Map a visible piece to an identifier only when its geometry, available colors, inventory presence, and instruction context support the match. Give each mapping a documented confidence level, and retain every plausible candidate when the image is ambiguous.

For the gray piece in step 3, compare all supported candidate designs. State the most defensible identification, quantity, color, and reasoning, or report the ambiguity without guessing. Deliver the step-by-step and cumulative bills of materials, page-and-image evidence sheet, identifier-confidence matching table, inventory-conflict table, and a concise step-3 finding. Do not use marketplace prices, contact sellers, add items to a cart, purchase parts, or claim an identifier that the cited evidence does not establish.

rubric.name: Official pages used
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows LEGO's official instruction PDF as the authority, maps instruction steps 1 through 10 to their printed pages, and shows those pages being rendered or captured and read. Mirror images or page mappings not supported by the official PDF do not count.

rubric.name: Complete step additions
rubric.requirement: The step-by-step bill covers all ten steps and reports the per-step addition totals and overall total derived from the instruction images. It excludes carry-over pieces and records every entry’s step, page, visible quantity, depicted shape and color, and subassembly context.

rubric.name: Reconciled cumulative totals
rubric.requirement: A separate cumulative bill of materials sums the pieces newly added in each step and reconciles repeated parts and page turns without recounting pieces that merely remain visible. Every cumulative quantity can be traced to the step-by-step table, and the per-step and cumulative totals agree.

rubric.name: Page image evidence
rubric.requirement: A page-and-image evidence sheet connects every step from 1 through 10 to its printed page and an actual instruction crop or precise referenced view. The browsing record must show each cited page being actually retrieved from the official instruction PDF; crops or references to pages that were never opened do not count.

rubric.name: Inventory cross-checks
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows successful access to both BrickLink and Brickset inventories. The deliverables preserve each source’s identifiers and terminology, any extra items or alternates actually listed, and genuine conflicts. A source that was never reached cannot be described as cross-checked.

rubric.name: Supported identifiers only
rubric.requirement: Each mapped identifier outside the step-3 finding is supported by the depicted geometry and color, set-inventory presence, available colors, and instruction context. It has a documented confidence level. Source identifiers and conflicts remain separate, and all plausible candidates are retained when the image is ambiguous. Inventory information does not override the official instruction image.

rubric.name: Step 3 finding
rubric.requirement: The concise step-3 finding compares every candidate supported by the official instruction view and the two inventory sources. It states the most defensible quantity, depicted color, part identity, design or element identifiers when supported, and the reasoning, or preserves the ambiguity without guessing. Any image-versus-inventory color conflict or absent candidate color is reported exactly as documented.

rubric.name: Evidence matches claims
rubric.requirement: The report does not claim access, verification, completeness, crops, or files that the browsing record does not support. For example, it cannot claim an external catalogue was checked after an access failure or claim a source was checked when no data was obtained. Clearly labeled assumptions and honest statements of partial progress are acceptable.

rubric.name: Marketplace limits followed
rubric.requirement: The browsing record never uses marketplace prices, contacts sellers, adds items to a cart, or attempts a purchase. BrickLink and Brickset catalog or inventory pages are allowed, but consulting price-guide pages as data is not.

tasks.title: Find jewelry brands using product-only photos
tasks.instruction:
I run a small on-model photography service and want to identify jewelry brands whose storefronts still rely on product-only images. Review Crystal Rose Design, April Söderström, Laurane Elisabeth, Megan Auman’s online shop, and Dandelion Jewelry. Use each brand’s own public store, not social media or reseller pages. When sources disagree, treat the brand’s storefront as the primary source.

For each brand, inspect the first 12 unique products in the store’s default catalogue order, or every product if the catalogue has fewer than 12. Follow pagination or a load-more control until you reach 12 unique products or the catalogue ends. Treat metal or color variants, repeated titles, and duplicate collection placements as one product when they share a title and page handle. Record the sample boundary and list sold-out products separately.

For every sampled product, inspect the main and alternate images. Classify each image as a flat lay, still life, bust or mannequin, cropped body detail, or full model shot. Count how many sampled products show any human skin. Give each brand one of three sample-based results: the sample appears product-only, the sample has named exceptions, or the sample uses models. Cite the product pages that determine the result. Do not claim that the whole store is model-free unless the sample reached the actual end of the catalogue.

For each brand whose sample appears product-only, choose one in-stock item and record its name, product page, price, direct main-image file address, published public contact email, and footer or policy trading name. Write “not published” when the store withholds an email or trading name. Preserve any image that contradicts an otherwise product-only sample, and record the time each store was checked.

If a catalogue is unavailable or password-protected, report the exact access problem and any partial evidence. Do not give that brand a model-use result if no product images could be inspected. Deliver a per-brand results table, a product-and-image table with counts, a selected-product sheet, and a pitch-readiness ranking that clearly states the sample limits. Do not create accounts, buy anything, or contact the brands.

rubric.name: Crystal Rose catalog
rubric.requirement: Crystal Rose Design is reviewed on its own public storefront. The record follows the store’s default catalogue order through pagination or loading controls until it captures the first 12 unique products or reaches the catalogue end. It deduplicates by title and page handle, states the observed boundary, and separates sold-out from in-stock products. If the catalogue is unavailable or password-protected, record the exact problem and any partial evidence; do not assign a model-use result without inspected images.

rubric.name: April catalog
rubric.requirement: April Söderström is reviewed on the brand’s own public store using the first 12 unique products in default catalogue order, or every product if the catalogue ends sooner. The record shows the pagination or loading path, deduplicates by title and page handle, separates stock status, and reports any observed access failure instead of claiming unseen coverage. If the catalogue is unavailable or password-protected, record the exact problem and any partial evidence; do not assign a model-use result without inspected images.

rubric.name: Laurane catalog
rubric.requirement: Laurane Elisabeth is reviewed on the brand’s own public storefront using the first 12 unique products in default catalogue order, or every product if fewer are available. The evidence shows the pagination or load-more path, title-and-handle deduplication, the sample boundary, and separate sold-out and in-stock results. If the catalogue is unavailable or password-protected, record the exact problem and any partial evidence; do not assign a model-use result without inspected images.

rubric.name: Megan Auman catalog
rubric.requirement: Megan Auman’s online shop is reviewed on its own public storefront. The record captures the first 12 unique products in default catalogue order, or the complete catalogue if it ends sooner, and shows the pagination or loading evidence that establishes that boundary. Duplicate placements are not counted as different products, and stock status is preserved. If the catalogue is unavailable or password-protected, record the exact problem and any partial evidence; do not assign a model-use result without inspected images.

rubric.name: Dandelion catalog
rubric.requirement: Dandelion Jewelry is reviewed on its own public storefront using the first 12 unique products in default catalogue order, or every product if the catalogue ends sooner. The record shows how the sample boundary was reached, deduplicates repeated placements, and separates stock status. If the catalogue is unavailable or password-protected, the exact failure and partial evidence are reported and no model-use result is given without inspected product images.

rubric.name: Visual classifications supported
rubric.requirement: Every sampled product’s main and alternate images are visibly inspected and classified as flat lay, still life, bust or mannequin, cropped body detail, or full model shot. The product-level table supports the reported skin count. Automated or heuristic labels are not presented as visual inspection, and any inaccessible image or partial product record remains clearly marked.

rubric.name: Verdicts match evidence
rubric.requirement: Each reviewed brand receives one of the three requested sample-based results, cites the product pages that determine it, and agrees with the product-and-image table. A whole-store model-free claim is made only when the sample reached the catalogue end. A brand with no inspected product images receives no model-use result, and the pitch-readiness ranking states all sample or access limits.

rubric.name: Selected product details
rubric.requirement: For every brand whose sample appears product-only, the selected-product sheet lists one in-stock item’s name, product page, price, direct main-image file address, published public contact email, and footer or policy trading name. Each value matches store evidence, and an unpublished email or trading name is written as “not published.” If no brand qualifies, the sheet says so.

rubric.name: All outputs included
rubric.requirement: The result includes a per-brand results table, a product-and-image table distinguishing main and alternate images with skin counts, a selected-product sheet, and a pitch-readiness ranking. It records the sample boundary and retrieval time for every store, lists sold-out products separately, and keeps any access gap visible.

rubric.name: Methods stated honestly
rubric.requirement: The report never describes the 12-product sample as a complete catalogue unless the store ended within that sample, never presents heuristic labels as visual inspection, and never invents missing values. Contradictory model or skin images remain visible. When sources disagree, the brand’s own storefront takes priority, with the disagreement retained. The browsing record shows no account creation, purchase, or contact with any brand.

tasks.title: Map BASF locations worldwide
tasks.instruction: I need a reliable list of BASF locations worldwide to understand its geographic coverage and the quality of its directory. Record the UTC observation time, active filters, displayed total, number loaded, access state, and displayed order. For every location, record its name, full address, country, region, type, coordinates, profile link or identifier, and any descriptions shown. Check each location against its BASF country or facility page and, where publicly available, an official postal, corporate-registry, government, or authoritative mapping record. Keep the directory's wording and coordinates separate from confirmed facts, source dates, and citations. Compare names and addresses without losing the identity of each source page. Flag likely duplicates and address or coordinate mismatches, and preserve conflicting values. For summary fields, prefer the site-specific BASF page for identity and function, official records for addresses, and authoritative mapping records for coordinates. Break down the checked list by country, region, and type. Identify gaps, duplicates, missing fields, and implausible coordinates, and compare the captured count with the directory’s displayed total, where available, and explain which records need review. Provide a source list, a complete dataset as a JSON object with a locations array, retaining the raw directory fields for each location and adding source and verification fields, a record of checks and conflicts, and a short report on geographic coverage and data quality with visible counting formulas. If a page or supporting source is blocked or missing, report the gap and continue with other public evidence; failed access does not prove absence. Do not sign in, submit forms other than public search, filter, or lookup controls, accept nonessential tracking, enter personal data, contact facilities, or invent missing values.

rubric.name: Observation details recorded
rubric.requirement: The records give the UTC observation time, active filters, displayed total, number loaded, access state, and displayed order as observed on BASF’s global Locations page. Captured evidence supports each value; unavailable display fields are marked unavailable. No fixed historical location count is required.

rubric.name: Complete directory dataset
rubric.requirement: The dataset includes every directory record reachable by working through the Locations page's actual pagination, loading, filtering, or data-delivery method. The evidence shows where collection stopped and compares the unique loaded count with any displayed total. Missing, blocked, separately attributed, or extra records are disclosed. No entries are invented or silently omitted.

rubric.name: Accurate directory fields
rubric.requirement: Each entry's directory-observation fields match the directory. Names and addresses differ only in harmless formatting, if at all. Profile links, identifiers, and descriptions come from the record. Source coordinates and source type contain values only if the directory shows them; otherwise they are null.

rubric.name: Verified fields supported
rubric.requirement: Verified addresses, coordinates, identity or function, citations, and source dates are filled only when the browsing record shows a check of source content. Directory observations remain separate. Unverified records use null or pending values. All verified fields may remain null if the report clearly explains the verification gap.

rubric.name: Evidence for each record
rubric.requirement: Every record has either a documented check of source content with its own citations or a documented source-access gap. Checks match BASF page content to the location or an authoritative external record to its address or coordinates. Merely checking whether a URL opens does not count.

rubric.name: Every record checked
rubric.requirement: Every location has a recorded content check against its BASF country or facility page, or its own note that the page was missing or blocked. When a public authoritative external record exists, it is also checked and cited with a source date. Failed access is reported as a gap, never evidence that the location is absent.

rubric.name: Conflicts and duplicates
rubric.requirement: The output lists likely duplicate groups and all their members, retains page identities and both sides of conflicts, and flags address or coordinate mismatches. Summary values use the requested source priority. Countries and regions derived from addresses agree with those addresses; a record is not silently assigned to a different country.

rubric.name: Geographic coverage analysis
rubric.requirement: The report gives country, region, and type breakdowns with visible formulas and counts matching the dataset. “All null/not surfaced” is acceptable for type. It identifies gaps, duplicates, missing-field counts, and implausible coordinates, or explains why none were found. It reports the observed total and supported coverage gaps without requiring comparison with an unspecified numerical expectation.

rubric.name: Four outputs delivered
rubric.requirement: All four outputs are present: a source list with sources and access details, a complete dataset retaining raw records in the instruction-defined locations array with source and verification fields, a verification-and-conflict log, and a short geographic-coverage and data-quality report. Raw downloaded data alone is not a source list.

rubric.name: Honest read-only work
rubric.requirement: Completeness, verification, outside confirmation, and explanations of scale do not exceed the evidence. Blocked or missing sources are gaps, not absence. The browsing record shows no sign-in, form submission other than public search, filter, or lookup controls, acceptance of nonessential tracking, personal-data entry, or email or phone contact with facilities.

tasks.title: Report remote-attack Microsoft vulnerabilities
tasks.instruction: I'm preparing a short report on Microsoft vulnerabilities involving remote attacks so I can plan fixes. In MSRC's public Update Guide, sort or search by release date and find every CVE from the most recent February before the date you check whose title or public description contains the word remote. Record the exact February date range, search, result count, result order, and observation time.
