For each qualifying CVE, record its identifier, title, release and revision dates, affected products, vulnerability type, CVSS version, vector and base score, severity, exploitability assessment, public disclosure and exploitation status, required privileges, user interaction, attack vector, and official link for fixes or other remedies. Open every official CVE detail page. Keep revised entries and differences in scores between products separate, and explain how they relate. Mark unavailable fields and record result-page or API limits. If you cannot reproduce the exact February set, provide an access report. Check every retained CVE against CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue. Record whether Microsoft provides a patch, mitigation, or workaround, including source and update dates. Group the findings by affected product and vulnerability class. State the rule you use to rank which issues to address first, using only disclosed evidence about severity, exploitation, exposure, and available remedies, and summarize the exposure patterns the evidence supports. Provide the complete February CVE list, a table matching products to their scores, MSRC revision history, a table of CISA KEV results and remedies, a priority spreadsheet with visible formulas, an access log, and a short defensive report. Do not test systems, download or link exploits, give exploitation steps, infer that an organization has a vulnerability, or treat severity alone as proof of current exploitation.

rubric.name: Exact CVE population
rubric.requirement: The list includes every CVE from the most recent February before the observation date whose public title or description contains the word 'remote', without assuming a fixed count. It excludes entries outside that month or with the word in neither field, explains the search limits, and keeps any secondary comparison group separate.

rubric.name: Accurate CVE fields
rubric.requirement: Every recorded value matches MSRC: identifier, title, release and revision dates, affected products, vulnerability type, CVSS version, vector, base score, severity, exploitability, disclosure and exploitation status, required privileges, user interaction, attack vector, and remediation link. Fields not provided by MSRC are explicitly marked unavailable.

rubric.name: Reproducible February query
rubric.requirement: The access record gives the February start and end dates and timezone convention, exact URL, parameters or visible search used, a count from that search, sorting rule, full observation timestamp, and every result-page or API boundary encountered. This includes nextLink, $top/$skip paging, rejected filters, and blocked inputs. If the search cannot be reproduced, an access report is required.

rubric.name: Details and revisions
rubric.requirement: The browsing record contains official details for every retained CVE. Revisions found during the research, including those after February, remain separate entries rather than being combined or left out.

rubric.name: Per-product score rows
rubric.requirement: The product-and-score table has rows for each product, not just one summary row per CVE. It keeps any observed score differences between products and does not invent differences.

rubric.name: KEV and fixes
rubric.requirement: Every retained CVE has a recorded CISA KEV check and Microsoft patch, mitigation, or workaround findings, with source and update dates. A successful KEV lookup supports present or absent status; an inaccessible or incomplete lookup is marked unknown, not absent. Unavailable remediation information is explicitly marked rather than invented.

rubric.name: Executable priority formula
rubric.requirement: The priority spreadsheet states and applies a rule using the available disclosed evidence about severity, exploitation, exposure, and remedies. Visible formulas and row inputs reproduce the ranking, and missing inputs are explicitly handled. Severity alone is not treated as proof of exploitation. No particular formula, weighting, or software is required beyond the requested visible calculation.

rubric.name: Consistent groups and brief
rubric.requirement: Results are grouped by affected product and vulnerability class. Counts agree with the listed members, and no CVE is assigned to a class that conflicts with MSRC's stated impact. The defensive report's account of attack vectors and exploitation matches the retained MSRC records.

rubric.name: Claims match browsing
rubric.requirement: The report does not claim without evidence that the interface or complete result set was reproduced, all details were opened, a source was accessed, or the work was complete or verified. Clearly marked assumptions and limitations are acceptable when consistent with the browsing record.

rubric.name: Defensive safety limits
rubric.requirement: The work does not test systems, download or link exploit code, give exploitation steps, infer vulnerabilities in an organization, or treat severity as proof of current exploitation. A KEV listing or MSRC's “Exploitation Detected” status may be cited as evidence of exploitation.

tasks.title: Assemble an OpenAI vendor-security packet
tasks.instruction:
I’m assembling the vendor-security packet needed before adopting OpenAI’s enterprise API. The address I received, https://openai.com/index/trustbank/, resolves but is not the trust portal; report exactly what it returns now and do not treat it as an document source. Locate OpenAI's actual public trust portal yourself and start there. Build the inventory from OpenAI’s live public trust portal and the security and privacy pages it links to. Cover every compliance document, audit report, certificate, questionnaire, and policy exposed without authentication.

Work through the whole public surface, including tabs, filters, accordions, expandable rows, cards, tables, and modals. Re-read sections after interacting because some items load late. Capture everything the portal lists, not only the first screen, and avoid padded duplicate rows. For every document, record its printed title, source view, type using my eight categories—SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, security questionnaire, terms of service, privacy policy, security policy, or penetration test report—or the site’s label when none fits. Also record the shown version, year or audit period, and whether it is openly readable, gated by an access request or NDA, or only mentioned. Keep separate editions as separate rows.

Reconcile which of the eight types are evidenced, asserted only in prose, or missing. Mark gaps clearly and preserve conflicts between portal listings and policy pages. Deliver a timestamped document register keyed by source view, an eight-type coverage table with gate status, the misrouted address's current response, and a short explanation of what a reviewer can obtain today without signing anything. Stay logged out and read-only: do not click download buttons, submit access-request or NDA forms, enter email or account details, or contact sales.

rubric.name: Supplied address response
rubric.requirement: The result reports exactly what the supplied address currently returns, identified by title or an unmistakable description, and never uses it as an document source. An observed HTTP status may be included, and any status must be labeled as a fetch result. The account must match what the browsing record actually showed.

rubric.name: Public portal inventory
rubric.requirement: The document register includes every document-bearing item exposed by the actual OpenAI public trust portal located during the research within the requested categories, attributed to its source view. All observed items are retained, including gated listings whose contents cannot be read. No fixed document roster or count is required.

rubric.name: Portal controls and late-loading items
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows the available public tabs, filters, accordions, expandable rows, cards, tables, and modals checked through their visible boundaries. Sections are re-read after interactions to capture late-loading items. A control that does not exist is not required; an unvisited or blocked section is identified as a gap.

rubric.name: Editions and repeated references
rubric.requirement: Separate editions of an document remain separate register entries. Repeated references to the same edition are linked to their source views without padded duplicate rows. The inventory distinguishes an actual listing from a mention in prose, and does not assume that a listed gated item was read.

rubric.name: Linked policies covered
rubric.requirement: The register covers the security and privacy pages linked from the public trust portal and the requested document types they expose. Each page has an access status and evidence of inspection or a documented access gap. Unrelated pages are not required unless directly exposed within the requested scope.

rubric.name: Faithful register fields
rubric.requirement: Every present row preserves the printed title, allowing only harmless case or punctuation differences. It uses the correct source view and gate status. Versions, years, and periods appear only when a cited source shows them. Unavailable fields are marked blank, none, or not shown rather than guessed.

rubric.name: Eight-type coverage
rubric.requirement: The coverage table addresses exactly SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, security questionnaire, terms of service, privacy policy, security policy, and penetration test report. For each type it reports, from the accessed public evidence, whether the type is documented by an document, asserted only in prose, or missing, together with its observed open, request- or NDA-gated, or mention-only state. Conflicts between portal and policy pages remain visible.

rubric.name: Reasonable type mapping
rubric.requirement: Each document uses one of the eight requested categories when the evidence supports it. When none fits, it retains the site’s own label. No document is forced into an unsupported category or assigned an invented type instead of an available site label.

rubric.name: Required outputs present
rubric.requirement: The result contains a source-view-keyed document register, the eight-type coverage table, the supplied address’s observed response, and a short explanation of what can be obtained without signing anything. The register includes an observation timestamp, keeps separate editions as separate rows or explicit file entries, and does not repeat the same document, view, and file merely to pad the inventory.

rubric.name: Only observed work claimed
rubric.requirement: The report does not claim complete extraction, exhaustive interaction, filter or modal use, re-reading, HTTP statuses, or source content that the browsing record does not show. Every register row has visible source support. Honest gap statements, such as an uninspected private tab or a timeout before a section loaded, are acceptable.

rubric.name: Read-only boundary
rubric.requirement: The complete browsing record stays logged out and read-only. It shows no login, access-request, NDA, subscription, or bulk-download submission; no click on download buttons; no entry into email or account fields; and no contact with sales.

tasks.title: Buy a WORX Landroid WR346 for Phoenix
tasks.instruction:
I’m trying to buy the WORX Landroid Vision Cloud 4WD mower for up to 1.5 acres, exact model WR346, for delivery to ZIP 85001. Check the WORX, Amazon, Walmart, and Lowe’s pages. Confirm whether each offer is the exact model and compare the publicly shown price, seller or fulfiller, stock, delivery timing and charge, pickup options, and included components. Keep different sellers and bundles separate. Exclude other models and acreage variants, and clearly identify retailers where no exact public offer can be confirmed.

Use WORX as the product-identity authority, but also search for other public U.S. sellers offering the exact WR346. Retain up to 20 distinct seller-and-bundle offers, or the complete smaller public population. For every offer, record the model evidence, seller, fulfiller, included components, warranty source, returns, stock, ZIP 85001 delivery or pickup evidence, and every disclosed charge at one observation time. Deduplicate identical marketplace offers without merging materially different bundles, and preserve conflicts between retailer and manufacturer information.

Rank confirmed offers by total disclosed cost, then delivery speed, then information quality. Do not infer unavailable destination charges. Deliver an exact-WR346 offer table, seller-and-bundle matching table, disclosed-cost comparison, and concise purchase-channel brief. Do not sign in, provide a street address, join a membership, add the mower to a cart, or place an order.

rubric.name: WORX authority record
rubric.requirement: An official WORX product page establishes the mower's model identity and advertised acreage class. The record captures every displayed manufacturer price, stock state, included components, warranty, and return information requested by the task at the observation time. Every non-null value is supported by accessed manufacturer content, and conflicts with retailer information remain visible.

rubric.name: Amazon exact-model check
rubric.requirement: If an exact WR346 Amazon offer is publicly accessible, the table records its exact-model evidence, price, seller or fulfiller, stock, delivery state, included components, and observation time. If no exact WR346 Amazon offer can be publicly confirmed, the table clearly identifies Amazon as having no confirmed exact public offer; no value from another model or invented offer is imported. A recorded public Amazon lookup attempt supports either an exact offer or the stated confirmation gap; an unattempted search does not establish that no offer was confirmed.

rubric.name: Walmart exact-model check
rubric.requirement: If an exact WR346 Walmart offer is publicly accessible, the table records its exact-model evidence, publicly visible price, and stock state at observation. If no exact WR346 Walmart offer can be publicly confirmed, the table records that outcome and its evidence without importing a value from another model. A shown price cannot be reported as hidden or blank. Seller or fulfiller values appear only with page evidence. Other acreage variants are excluded. A recorded public Walmart lookup attempt supports either an exact offer or the stated confirmation gap; an unattempted search does not establish that no offer was confirmed.

rubric.name: Lowe’s exact-model check
rubric.requirement: If an exact WR346 Lowe’s offer is publicly accessible, the table records its exact-model evidence, public price, stock state, and yard-size wording as displayed at the observation time; Lowe’s wording is not normalized to 1.5 acres. If no exact WR346 Lowe’s offer can be publicly confirmed because access fails or the listing is unavailable, the report records the evidence and says confirmation was impossible. A recorded public Lowe’s lookup attempt supports either an exact offer or the stated confirmation gap; an unattempted search does not establish that no offer was confirmed.

rubric.name: Valid extra sellers
rubric.requirement: The record shows a search for additional public U.S. sellers of the exact WR346. Every selected offer has model evidence, and the full retained set has no more than 20 distinct seller-and-bundle offers. Identical marketplace offers are combined with evidence; materially different bundles remain separate. Any claim that a smaller set is the complete public population is supported by the recorded search, not assumed from stopping early.

rubric.name: Destination claims supported
rubric.requirement: ZIP 85001 delivery charges, dated arrival estimates, pickup availability, and destination-specific stock appear only when the browsing record shows the page set to ZIP 85001. Generic free-shipping banners remain labeled as banners and are not converted into a $0 charge or confirmed delivery to 85001. Taxes, fees, and delivery dates are never estimated. “Not publicly disclosed” is acceptable.

rubric.name: Other fields supported
rubric.requirement: Every retained offer has fields for seller, fulfiller, included components, warranty source, returns, stock, destination delivery or pickup, disclosed charges, and check time. Values have matching source evidence; unavailable values are explicitly marked. The record does not transfer facts between sellers, bundles, or configurations. This check covers field completeness and facts not already assessed under the retailer and destination checks.

rubric.name: Four usable outputs
rubric.requirement: All four requested outputs are present and usable: a timestamped exact-WR346 offer table with structured per-offer fields, a seller-and-bundle matching table, a disclosed-cost comparison, and a concise purchase-channel brief. Sellers and materially different bundles remain separate. Confirmed offers are ranked by disclosed cost, delivery speed, and information quality, with consistent results across sections.

rubric.name: Purchase actions avoided
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in or account creation, street-address entry, membership enrollment, add-to-cart action, or order placement on any site. Entering ZIP 85001 by itself is allowed.

tasks.title: Check a Rough Country cover fits a Ram
tasks.instruction: I'm checking whether a Rough Country hard flip-up tonneau cover is currently offered for a 6-foot-4-inch bed on a 2009–2018 Ram 1500 or a 2010–2025 Ram 2500. Go through every accessible Rough Country tonneau-cover result on Summit Racing. Identify every listing or selectable vehicle option that could match the cover type, truck series, model-year ranges, and stated bed length. Keep the results in their displayed order and record the title, part number, selected vehicle option, displayed price, stock or availability, whether the purchase button is enabled, and URL. Find the relevant Rough Country part numbers and related documents. Use current public Rough Country pages and manuals to check model year, body style, actual bed measurement versus the stated bed size, factory features, bed-liner restrictions, exclusions, any drilling or modifications, and required hardware. Keep Summit's price and availability information separate from Rough Country's evidence that the cover fits. Record every search, filter, page, duplicate, similar listing you excluded, check time, access failure, and disagreement. Do not apply a Ram 1500 rule to a Ram 2500 configuration unless a source explicitly supports it. For each exact part number supported by the manufacturer evidence, compare up to ten additional public offers from authorized or established sellers when available. Record the time, price, seller, stock wording, shipping conditions, and whether the purchase button is enabled. A marketplace listing does not prove the cover fits. Mark each Summit listing and each requested vehicle range as documented, unsupported, conflicting, or unclear. State whether you found an exact product, with its supported price, availability, and enabled Add to Cart or equivalent button status. Provide the complete Summit results list, a table showing fit by year and vehicle platform, a list of manufacturer documents, a comparison of seller offers, a record of disagreements, and a checklist of what to verify before purchase. Do not enter vehicle or personal information beyond public vehicle-fit selectors, add anything to a cart, contact sellers, recommend a purchase, or claim a cover fits when the cited documents do not say so.

rubric.name: Exact Summit listing
rubric.requirement: Each matching Summit listing has a title, part number, price displayed at the check time, availability wording, enabled or disabled Add-to-Cart status, and URL supported by summitracing.com. If Summit could not be accessed, an explicit access-failure record marked unclear or access-failed also meets this requirement.

rubric.name: All accessible Summit results
rubric.requirement: The Summit results list covers every accessible Rough Country tonneau-cover result and records how the pages end or where access stops. It keeps displayed order and each title, part number, selected vehicle fit or description, price, stock or availability, enabled or disabled purchase-button status, and URL. Possible matches and similar excluded listings have reasons. Any displayed result count is recorded; no particular total is required.

rubric.name: Accurate Summit details
rubric.requirement: Every value attributed to Summit agrees with saved Summit evidence. No rows, prices, availability wording, shipping dates, purchase-button states, or vehicle-fit claims are invented. In particular, vehicle-fit claims do not go beyond what the cited Summit page says. This check assesses the reported entries separately from the completeness check in A2.

rubric.name: Relevant manufacturer documents
rubric.requirement: The manufacturer-document list identifies every relevant Rough Country part number established in the research. It connects each number to its public product page, fitment table, and installation manual or other relevant documents when available. The cited documents are opened and checked. Missing, inaccessible, or conflicting documents are explicitly recorded rather than replaced with unsupported claims that the cover fits.

rubric.name: Accurate manufacturer fit information
rubric.requirement: Every Rough Country fit or installation claim agrees with the cited manufacturer page or manual. Where the source addresses them, this includes model year, body style, actual versus stated bed length, factory features, bed-liner restrictions, exclusions, drilling or modifications, and required hardware. Anything the public documents do not establish is marked unsupported or unclear, not assumed to apply across truck series.

rubric.name: Vehicle ranges assessed
rubric.requirement: Every observed Summit candidate and both requested vehicle ranges are marked documented, unsupported, conflicting, or unclear using cited evidence. Ram 1500 rules are not applied to Ram 2500 without explicit support. The result states whether an exact product was established and gives only supported prices, availability, and purchase-button status. An inaccessible listing is recorded as an access failure and marked unclear, not treated as evidence that no product exists.

rubric.name: Supported seller offers
rubric.requirement: For each exact supported part number, the comparison includes up to ten additional public offers from authorized or established sellers when available. Each has the seller, check time, price, stock wording, shipping conditions, and enabled or disabled purchase-button status from a saved seller page. A smaller selected set is permitted; neither ten offers nor proof of scarcity is required. Marketplace stock never counts as proof of fit.

rubric.name: Six required outputs
rubric.requirement: There are six clearly separate structured outputs: the Summit results list, fit-by-year-and-platform table, manufacturer-document list, seller-offer comparison, disagreement log, and pre-purchase checklist. Searches, filters, pages, duplicates, similar excluded listings, check times, access failures, and disagreements are also recorded. This check assesses output structure only. Field accuracy is assessed under A3, A5, and A7.

rubric.name: Honest coverage claims
rubric.requirement: Claims of completeness and verification agree with the saved work. Blocked sources are marked access failures rather than results, and recorded disagreements remain visible. A claim about fit or restrictions that the cited documents do not address is clearly marked as an assumption or undocumented. Values assessed under A3, A5, or A7 are not scored again here. This check covers unsupported claims of coverage or verification and claims that the cited sources do not address.

rubric.name: Purchase and contact limits
rubric.requirement: No vehicle or personal information is entered beyond public vehicle-fit selectors. Nothing is added to a cart, no seller is contacted, and no purchase recommendation is made. Observing whether a cart button exists or is enabled is allowed.

tasks.title: Compare offers for a WORX Landroid WR320.1
tasks.instruction: I want to compare offers for the exact WORX Landroid Vision Cloud 2WD mower for one-half acre, model WR320.1, for delivery to ZIP 10001. Use WORX documentation to establish the model's identity and any documented difference from WR320; do not treat them as equivalent unless WORX says they are. Check WORX, Walmart, Home Depot, Lowe's, and Amazon, then any other useful public U.S. retailer or marketplace sources, for up to 20 distinct offers for the exact model, or all offers if fewer exist. For each seller and bundle, record the public price, seller or fulfiller, stock, delivery timing and charge, pickup options, included components and accessories, warranty source, returns, ZIP 10001 delivery or pickup evidence, and other disclosed charges. Record when you checked every value that can change. Keep different marketplace sellers and bundles separate. Combine repeated appearances of the same seller's offer on search and detail pages without combining materially different bundles. Rank confirmed exact-model offers by total disclosed cost, then delivery speed, then how clearly the terms are disclosed. Clearly identify retailers where no exact public offer can be established. Provide a table of exact-WR320.1 offers, a table matching models and bundles, a table of delivery and pickup information disclosed for ZIP 10001, and a short recommendation of where to buy based on comparable disclosed cost, delivery, returns, and evidence quality. Do not sign in, provide a street address, join a membership, add anything to a cart, or purchase.

rubric.name: WR320.1 identity
rubric.requirement: WR320.1's identity is established from WORX product-page, manual, or specification content actually captured. WR320 is treated as different unless WORX establishes equivalence. Any claimed difference is tied to matching WORX documentation. A limited statement that no equivalence information was found is acceptable; invented differences are not.

rubric.name: Exact offers only
rubric.requirement: The retained set contains no more than 20 distinct offers. Every confirmed offer in the table or ranking has captured evidence of the exact WR320.1 model in its title, model field, or matching UPC/GTIN. WR320, related mowers, accessories, and unrelated bundles are excluded or clearly separated. Different bundles remain separate. The same seller offer appearing on results and detail pages appears only once.

rubric.name: Source fields accurate
rubric.requirement: Each reported price, seller or fulfiller, stock status, delivery timing and charge, pickup option, component, warranty source, return term, and timestamp matches visible evidence from that same source. Unavailable fields are explicitly marked; there are no invented placeholders, remembered values presented as observations, values borrowed from elsewhere, or prices from another variant. ZIP-specific claims are checked separately under A4.

rubric.name: ZIP evidence labeled
rubric.requirement: Delivery, charges, and pickup for ZIP 10001 are claimed only when browsing shows the site set to ZIP 10001 or an explicit sitewide statement that unambiguously applies to that destination and offer. Observations under another default or proxy ZIP retain that ZIP or are marked not ZIP-verified. If a street address is required, the report says the information could not be established.

rubric.name: Five retailers resolved
rubric.requirement: WORX, Walmart, Home Depot, Lowe's, and Amazon each have either an exact confirmed offer with captured evidence or a “no exact public offer can be established” outcome with the observed reason, such as only a similar model or an access or location restriction. The record also shows research on other useful public U.S. seller sources. Claims of no offer or a complete smaller population have supporting search evidence and do not contradict captured results.

rubric.name: Four structured outputs
rubric.requirement: All four outputs are present: exact-WR320.1 offer table, model-and-bundle matching table, ZIP-10001 disclosure table, and retailer recommendation. Offer rows are structured and use not-disclosed or null values as appropriate. Every changeable field has a timestamp, and all files or tables are readable and parseable.

rubric.name: Consistent offer ranking
rubric.requirement: Only confirmed exact-model offers are ranked, first by total disclosed cost, then delivery speed, then transparency. The order agrees with the recorded values. The retailer recommendation follows the recorded cost, delivery, returns, and evidence quality, without unsupported assumptions about current prices.

rubric.name: Transaction limits followed
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in, street-address entry, membership enrollment, add-to-cart action, or purchase. Entering ZIP 10001 and opening public pages are allowed.

tasks.title: Export the Bett UK exhibitor directory
tasks.instruction:
I’m shortlisting edtech vendors to meet at Bett UK and need a verified export from its public solution-providers directory at https://uk.bettshow.com/solution-providers. Exhaust populated listing pages 4 through 8 at one recorded UTC observation time. This is the nearest live five-page replacement for the superseded pages 16 through 20. Preserve every page number, card position, card count, displayed total, and any visible ordering or filters. Do not assume an unlabeled sort.

In a separate boundary note, identify pages 16–20 as the original window and record their live access and population state. Do not treat an out-of-range shell as proof that the directory has no exhibitors. If numbered pages are unavailable, treat consecutive default-order card batches as pages, using the site’s per-fetch batch size, cover batches 4–8, and state the observed pagination model.

For every exhibitor in the window, record the exact company name, website URL, directory profile URL, stand number, country, product categories, and a short profile summary. Mark unlisted values as unavailable. Preserve the raw page populations before deduplicating by stable profile identity rather than name, and log every merge. Verify every retained website and trading name against the destination site or official business records. Preserve conflicts and flag redirects, parked domains, and dead links.

Summarize the deduplicated set by country, sector, and field completeness with the number of records used to calculate each missing-field rate. Shortlist exactly ten exhibitors using published, formula-visible criteria based only on collected fields. Return the complete JSON array of exhibitor objects, each containing at least name and website, directly in the response, plus the pagination and boundary table, deduplication and conflict logs, verification matching table, and meeting brief. Report blocked or missing sources, retain the best available public alternative evidence, and lower confidence rather than guessing. Do not sign in, register, request a badge, contact exhibitors, collect personal contact details, or substitute a remembered roster.

rubric.name: Pages 4–8 logged
rubric.requirement: A table covers pages 4–8 and records each page number, card count, and card positions at one UTC observation time. If numbered pages are unavailable, batches 4–8 use the site’s observed per-fetch size in default order. The record states the observed pagination model, actual visible filter state, and displayed total when independently visible. It does not claim an unlabeled sort order.

rubric.name: Old window checked
rubric.requirement: A separate note identifies pages 16–20 as the original superseded window and reports their live access and population state from actual probes shown in the browsing record. Empty or out-of-range shells are not treated as proof that the overall directory has no exhibitors.

rubric.name: Complete raw window
rubric.requirement: The raw, pre-deduplication population contains every live card in the canonical window: the complete population observed at the recorded UTC observation time, with the observed card count preserved for each of pages 4–8. Every card retains its page and position and is supported by live extraction. No entries are imported from memory, other pages, filters, or reordered views.

rubric.name: Accurate exhibitor fields
rubric.requirement: Every retained record contains name, website URL, directory profile URL, stand, country, product categories, and short summary. Values match the directory card or profile. The name is the displayed company, not the Bett UK banner; the website is the profile’s published destination. Missing values are explicit.

rubric.name: Identity-based deduplication
rubric.requirement: The raw population remains separate from the deduplicated population. Deduplication uses a stable identity observed on the page, such as the profile slug or URL, never the company name alone. Every merge is logged, or a zero-merge result explicitly states the key used.

rubric.name: Identity verification through either permitted source
rubric.requirement: Every retained exhibitor has a documented website-and-trading-identity verification attempt using its destination website or official business records, with field-level sources and outcomes. Either permitted source route can establish identity; checking only a shortlist is insufficient. A website access attempt is required for a claimed redirect, parked-site, or dead-site status, not as a universal additional identity-verification gate.

rubric.name: Verification statuses honest
rubric.requirement: Every matching table status and confidence level agrees with the captured evidence. Blocks, CAPTCHAs, challenges, and maintenance pages are reported as such and lower confidence, with the best available public alternative evidence retained. Redirects, parked domains, and dead links are flagged. Trading-name conflicts preserve both the directory value and destination or official-record value rather than silently normalizing them.

rubric.name: Summaries show denominators
rubric.requirement: Country, sector, and field-completeness summaries are calculated over the deduplicated population. Each summary gives the total number of records used and the number with missing values, and all totals agree with the delivered records.

rubric.name: Formula-based top ten
rubric.requirement: The shortlist contains exactly ten exhibitors. Its selection formula is visible and uses only collected fields. Every score is actually computed and can be reproduced by spot-checking its inputs. Null or absent scores are not presented as calculated results, and unsupported scores are excluded.

rubric.name: Complete inline JSON
rubric.requirement: The final response itself includes a parseable JSON array with one object for every retained exhibitor. Each object contains at least the exhibitor name and website or an explicit missing-value marker. The array must be complete; a separate file cannot replace it.

rubric.name: Interaction limits followed
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in, registration, badge request, exhibitor contact, or collection of personal contact details. The delivered population contains no exhibitors inserted from a remembered list of prominent brands.

tasks.title: Find where PayPal appears for AirPods on Target
tasks.instruction:
I’m deciding whether AirPods can be paid for with PayPal on Target.com and need to know where that option appears or disappears. While logged out, use Target’s own search for the exact query “AirPods” and sweep the complete result set, not only the first screen. Keep every distinct AirPods-family product, deduplicated by TCIN, and record its TCIN, title, generation, price, sold-by label, shipping and pickup availability, and source page.

Choose several in-stock, Target-sold candidates across different generations and price tiers. Advance each through the shortest guest path to the furthest cart or checkout state available before an account or payment credential is required. At every step, record each offered payment method’s on-screen label, placement, eligibility note, and disabled state. Screenshot every payment surface with the clock time observed. Stop immediately at a sign-in wall, PayPal credential screen, or technical block. Do not type anything into that blocked or credential-gated screen, and do not place an order.

Separately collect Target’s public help and payment-page statements about accepted methods, including any exclusions for marketplace sellers, gift cards, subscriptions, or pickup. Reconcile the published claims with each candidate’s observed options. Preserve disagreements. Classify each candidate as PayPal absent, present but conditioned, or undetermined when its path ends early.

Finish with a plain verdict about PayPal availability for AirPods, its conditions, and the strength of the evidence. For every unfinished path, preserve the partial table and identify the specific blocker; a wall does not show whether PayPal exists. Deliver the deduplicated inventory, per-candidate step table with screenshot index, published-versus-observed payment matching table, and blocked-path log. Do not sign in, create an account, enter payment or personal information, or submit an order.

rubric.name: Complete Target sweep
rubric.requirement: While logged out, Target’s own AirPods search is swept through every page or offset covered by the result count shown in the browsing record. The report states how the sweep ended, harvests only the result grid rather than carousels, and deduplicates by TCIN. A first-screen or partially paginated extraction is not complete.

rubric.name: Accurate AirPods inventory
rubric.requirement: Every inventory row is an AirPods-family product. Its TCIN, title, generation, price, Target sold-by label, shipping and pickup state, and source page are supported by captured evidence or marked not shown. There are no invented defaults, duplicate TCINs, or variants counted more than once.

rubric.name: Varied candidate paths
rubric.requirement: Several in-stock, Target-sold AirPods candidates from the captured inventory are selected across different generations and price tiers, and each is advanced along the shortest available guest path. The record identifies the candidates, their generation and price differences, and any availability limits. It does not impose a separate fixed three-candidate or two-price-point quota.

rubric.name: Complete step tables
rubric.requirement: For every advanced candidate, a structured table records each step, all payment methods shown, their exact on-screen labels and placement, and every eligibility note or disabled state. A step without payment options records that none were shown. Each table names the furthest guest state reached, and every entry is supported by the browsing record.

rubric.name: Payment screenshots indexed
rubric.requirement: Every observed payment surface on each candidate path has a saved screenshot and an index entry with the observed clock time. The files and index agree. A screenshot that could not be captured is recorded as a gap, not replaced by an invented capture or omitted from the record.

rubric.name: Stops before credentials
rubric.requirement: Every candidate path stops without typing into sign-in, account, personal-information, or payment-credential fields. No account is created, no order is placed or submitted, and no direct checkout URL or checkout API is used to bypass a wall.

rubric.name: Target policies retrieved
rubric.requirement: Target’s own public help or payment pages are directly retrieved; search snippets and third-party summaries do not count. The report records their claims about PayPal and addresses marketplace sellers, gift cards, subscriptions, and pickup.

rubric.name: Candidate payment matching table
rubric.requirement: The published-versus-observed matching table reconciles policy claims separately for every candidate rather than giving one general comparison. It preserves disagreements as conflicts and assigns each candidate exactly one status: PayPal absent, present-but-conditioned, or undetermined. Any path stopped by a wall is classified undetermined.

rubric.name: Observations stated honestly
rubric.requirement: The deliverables do not claim an exhaustive sweep after partial extraction, more tested candidates than were actually advanced, or payment and availability observations absent from the browsing record. A blocked or wall-ended path is never treated as evidence that PayPal is present or absent. All coverage statements match the captured work.

rubric.name: Verdict and blockers
rubric.requirement: The deliverable ends with a plain verdict on PayPal availability for AirPods on Target.com, states any relied-upon conditions from Target’s public pages, and describes the evidence strength. It also contains a structured blocked-path log naming the specific stopper for every unfinished candidate path.

tasks.title: Survey Scientific Reports 2012 conference papers
tasks.instruction: I'm studying research from conferences that Scientific Reports published in 2012. Make a complete, sourced list of that year's items that Nature explicitly identifies as conference proceedings or as part of a named conference collection. For each qualifying item, record the title, authors, publication date, article type, conference or collection name, subject area, DOI, and public article link. Check the publication details for every retained DOI through Crossref and at least one scholarly index, and explain differences in dates, type labels, or conference association. Use the journal's complete 2012 archive, every relevant Nature collection or proceedings index, and conference statements in individual articles to establish what belongs in the list. Record how each candidate was found. Keep membership in a collection separate from an article's explicit statement that it came from a conference. Define a consistent set of topic categories from titles and abstracts before calculating totals, explain how to apply them, and allow an item to have more than one topic. Report counts by topic and conference. Identify any items listed in a collection index but missing from the journal's 2012 archive. Clearly mark inaccessible abstracts or publication details rather than guessing them, and report how inaccessible abstracts or publication details change the number of items used in the analysis. Provide the complete dataset in a machine-readable format, a graph connecting conferences to items and their supporting sources, a table comparing collection entries with the archive, a table of conflicting publication details, the topic definitions and counts, and a short account of what the evidence suggests about the journal's conference-related subject coverage that year.

rubric.name: Complete corpus
rubric.requirement: The dataset has a structured entry for every qualifying item, and the browsing record supports why each belongs. It has no missing, invented, or out-of-scope items and is more than a prose list.

rubric.name: Accurate corpus fields
rubric.requirement: Each retained entry gives the title, complete author list, publication date, article type, conference or collection name, subject area, DOI, and public article link. Values match the consulted evidence, allowing harmless changes to capitalization, punctuation, or diacritics. Missing or inaccessible publication details are explicitly marked, and the effect on analysis coverage is recorded. These accuracy requirements apply to the values actually reported.

rubric.name: Full archive review
rubric.requirement: The browsing record establishes coverage of the complete Scientific Reports 2012 archive, including its boundaries and relevant article-type labels. A complete listing or another documented method covering that archive is acceptable. A proceedings-filter page alone does not establish review of the whole archive.

rubric.name: Collection and archive comparison
rubric.requirement: Every relevant Nature conference collection or proceedings index found during review is listed and linked to its items. The comparison identifies which indexed items appear in the complete 2012 archive and which, if any, are missing. Conclusions come from accessed evidence, not an assumed collection or count.

rubric.name: All collections screened
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows a systematic method able to find every Nature conference collection or proceedings index linked to the 2012 volume, including the complete archive, relevant index links, and conference statements in individual articles. Reasons are given for including or excluding candidates. A page sample or single search is not described as exhaustive.

rubric.name: Every DOI verified
rubric.requirement: Each retained DOI has recorded checks through Crossref and at least one scholarly index. Retrieved records support the confirmed publication fields, and observed differences in dates, type labels, authorship, or conference association are kept and explained. An inaccessible record is marked as a gap, not a successful match, and its effect on the analysis is stated.

rubric.name: Consistent topic analysis
rubric.requirement: Topic categories and rules are defined from titles and accessible abstracts before calculating totals. They allow multiple topics per item and are applied consistently to every retained record. Item assignments, topic and conference counts, and the written account agree. The abstract-based analysis uses the actual number of accessible abstracts and explicitly reports every reduction due to missing or blocked abstracts.

rubric.name: Six required outputs
rubric.requirement: All six readable outputs are present: a machine-readable dataset, a record linking conferences to items and sources, an archive comparison table, a publication-details conflict table, topic definitions with counts, and a short subject-coverage account. The source record separates collection membership from article-level origin, and the dataset or archive comparison records how each retained candidate was found. This check assesses output structure only; A2 assesses values, A7 counts, and A9 coverage claims.

rubric.name: Evidence-bound reporting
rubric.requirement: All claims match the browsing record. A partial page or failed collection attempt is not called complete coverage; verification sources are named only if queried; missing search results are not reported as publication details; article-level conference statements are not invented; and no claim of zero missing collection items is made without listing the collection. Inaccessible sources are identified. Clearly marked assumptions supported by cited evidence are acceptable.

tasks.title: Compare Dutch retailer delivery info
tasks.instruction: I'm moving within the Netherlands and want to compare how much delivery information Dutch retailers show before I sign in, using postcode 1234 AB to check. Start with Amazon's Dutch storefront, then check bol, Coolblue, MediaMarkt Netherlands, and Wehkamp. Find every logged-out place that accepts a postcode, including header delivery-location controls, product-page delivery estimates, pickup-point and store finders, and shipping calculators that work without a cart. Explain in plain words how to reach each one. Enter 1234 AB no more than once in each place. Record the field label, exactly what you entered, whether it changes to 1234AB or a place name, the exact validation or confirmation message, the resulting header or panel, and whether that setting remains after one ordinary page navigation. Separately use PostNL's public postcode lookup and Dutch address or municipality records to establish whether 1234 AB covers a real address range and which place it belongs to. This checks the postcode itself, not whether a retailer delivers there. If a retailer gives a different place from the authoritative records, or two parts of its own site disagree, keep both results. Mark information you cannot see as unavailable and explain what blocked access. An access block says nothing about whether the postcode is valid. Record the clock time for each retailer's observations, since these panels can change. Rank all five retailers by how early and fully they show delivery timing, cost, and pickup options before requiring an account or street address, and explain which is most useful for someone moving. Provide a record for each place checked, a table comparing the postcode with authoritative records, a record of disagreements, a list of access blocks, and the ranking. Do not sign in, register, enter a street address or personal information, add anything to a cart, or order.

rubric.name: Authoritative postcode check
rubric.requirement: The postcode table records independent check attempts for 1234 AB through both PostNL and Dutch address or municipality records such as PDOK/BAG Locatieserver or BAG Viewer. The query and result are visible in the browsing record. It reports whether those records show a registered address range and which locality they show, keeping the actual result. It separates postcode validity from retailer acceptance and delivery availability. A retailer's or another non-authoritative source's place name is not treated as authoritative. A source's extra input requirement may be recorded as a limitation alongside a successful check of authoritative address records.

rubric.name: Amazon pages and controls
rubric.requirement: Amazon.nl is checked while logged out. The record covers its accessible postcode-entry locations, including header delivery controls, product delivery estimates, pickup-point or store finders, and no-cart shipping calculators where offered. It explains how to reach each location and records the observed result of entering 1234 AB at most once there. Missing controls and actual access blocks are distinguished from an invalid postcode; unseen content is not invented.

rubric.name: Bol pages and controls
rubric.requirement: bol is checked while logged out. The record covers its accessible postcode-entry locations, including header delivery controls, product delivery estimates, pickup-point or store finders, and no-cart shipping calculators where offered. It explains how to reach each location and records the observed result of entering 1234 AB at most once there. Missing controls and actual access blocks are distinguished from an invalid postcode; unseen content is not invented.

rubric.name: Coolblue pages and controls
rubric.requirement: Coolblue is checked while logged out. The record covers its accessible postcode-entry locations, including header delivery controls, product delivery estimates, pickup-point or store finders, and no-cart shipping calculators where offered. It explains how to reach each location and records the observed result of entering 1234 AB at most once there. Missing controls and actual access blocks are distinguished from an invalid postcode; unseen content is not invented.

rubric.name: MediaMarkt pages and controls
rubric.requirement: MediaMarkt Netherlands is checked while logged out. The record covers its accessible postcode-entry locations, including header delivery controls, product delivery estimates, pickup-point or store finders, and no-cart shipping calculators where offered. It explains how to reach each location and records the observed result of entering 1234 AB at most once there. Missing controls and actual access blocks are distinguished from an invalid postcode; unseen content is not invented.

rubric.name: Wehkamp pages and controls
rubric.requirement: Wehkamp is checked while logged out. The record covers its accessible postcode-entry locations, including header delivery controls, product delivery estimates, pickup-point or store finders, and no-cart shipping calculators where offered. It explains how to reach each location and records the observed result of entering 1234 AB at most once there. Missing controls and actual access blocks are distinguished from an invalid postcode; unseen content is not invented.

rubric.name: Complete postcode-entry records
rubric.requirement: Every tested postcode-entry location records the field label, exact entered text, whether and how it was reformatted, the returned validation or confirmation message or state, and whether it remained after one ordinary navigation. Evidence shows both the submission and the navigation used to test this. Unseen fields are marked unavailable and the blocker is named. Persistence is not claimed without evidence of both steps.

rubric.name: Recorded check times
rubric.requirement: Each retailer's observations include a clock time supported by the browsing record. Times are not invented or added later without evidence.

rubric.name: Five-retailer ranking
rubric.requirement: All five retailers are ranked by how early and fully they show delivery timing, cost, and pickup options before requiring an account or street address. The explanation uses only recorded, supported observations and identifies the best option for someone moving. A blocked retailer may be placed last or marked unrankable if the block is stated.

rubric.name: Required outputs and browsing limits
rubric.requirement: The five outputs can be identified: the record for each page or control checked, the table comparing the postcode with authoritative records, the disagreement log, the access-block list, and the ranking. An empty disagreement log is acceptable when it states that no disagreements were found in the observed evidence. The browsing record shows no sign-in, registration, street-address or personal-information entry, cart addition, or order. 1234 AB is entered at most once per page or control.

tasks.title: Map YC Winter 2025 B2B companies
tasks.instruction: I’m mapping the Winter 2025 B2B group in Y Combinator’s public company directory. Capture every company currently returned by the W25 and B2B filters. Preserve the directory’s count, order, pagination or loading boundary, observation time, YC profile identity, company name, one-line description, B2B subcategory tags, status, and location. For every company, record the active founders publicly listed by YC, YC profile URL, external company website, and any explicitly stated product category, target customer, and pricing model. Use not listed for unsupported fields. Reconcile the final row count with the filtered directory and deduplicate by YC profile identity. Preserve conflicting batch, tag, status, and location evidence. Keep company, operating, remote, and founder locations in separate fields. Visit every listed external site to confirm that it represents the same company. Record redirects, final URLs, inaccessible sites, and missing information. Code product category, target customer, and pricing model only when the company site states them explicitly. Recalculate counts from the delivered rows by status, B2B subcategory, country or remote location, and business model. Explain multiple-category counting and show the total number of records used in each calculation. Deliver the saved directory capture, complete company-profile dataset, founder and company identity matching table, external-site verification table, classification table, and concise group brief. Do not sign in, contact founders or companies, collect personal contact information, or infer private funding, employment, or operating status.

rubric.name: Complete directory capture
rubric.requirement: The saved directory capture contains every company returned by the W25 and B2B filters as structured rows, in directory order, with no unrelated companies. Rows are deduplicated by YC profile identity, and the final row count is reconciled with the filtered directory.

rubric.name: Capture details
rubric.requirement: The delivered capture records the directory-reported count, an observation time, the pagination or loading boundary actually encountered, and an explicit reconciliation between the final row count and the directory count.

rubric.name: Accurate directory fields
rubric.requirement: For every delivered row, the company name, one-line description, B2B subcategory tags, status, and location match the YC directory. A missing directory location is recorded as missing or not listed rather than inferred.

rubric.name: All company profile fields
rubric.requirement: Every captured company includes the active founders publicly listed by YC, its YC profile URL, and its external company website. Founder names are intact and not malformed by nearby page text. A profile that lists no founders or no external site counts when recorded as not listed.

rubric.name: Full profile coverage
rubric.requirement: Every captured company records any product category, target customer, and pricing model explicitly stated by its external company website. Genuine omissions are recorded as not listed, and unsupported values are not inferred.

rubric.name: Truthful site verification
rubric.requirement: The external-site verification table covers every company with a listed website. Each row records whether the site was reachable, redirected with a final URL, or inaccessible; provides evidence that it represents the same company; and records missing information. A site is not claimed as verified unless it was visited successfully.

rubric.name: Evidence-based coding
rubric.requirement: Every populated product-category, target-customer, and pricing-model value is explicitly stated on the company's own site; otherwise it is recorded as not listed. Search snippets, generic labels, calls to action such as Book a demo, and the mere existence of a pricing page are not treated as substantive values.

rubric.name: Recomputed group counts
rubric.requirement: Counts by status, B2B subcategory, country or remote location, and business model are recalculated from the delivered rows. The total number of records used in each calculation is stated, multiple-category counting is explained, and totals remain internally consistent across every output and the group brief.

rubric.name: Six distinct outputs
rubric.requirement: All six distinct outputs are delivered: saved directory capture, company-profile dataset, founder and company identity matching table, external-site verification table, classification table, and group brief. The dataset separates company, operating, remote, and founder locations and preserves conflicting batch, tag, status, or location evidence. Missing values may be null or not listed.

rubric.name: Privacy boundaries
rubric.requirement: The browsing record and deliverables contain no sign-in attempts, outreach to founders or companies, or collected personal contact information such as email addresses or phone numbers. Public founder names and roles requested by the task are allowed. No private funding, employment, or operating status is inferred.

rubric.name: Honest final report
rubric.requirement: The group brief and final report agree with the delivered records on counts, coverage, and verification. YC status labels are not presented as independently verified operating status. Inaccessible sites and other shortfalls are disclosed. A missing required brief does not satisfy this check.

tasks.title: Track Wisconsin Surplus auctions
tasks.instruction: I’m tracking current Wisconsin Surplus auction opportunities for budgeting without participating. Record one UTC observation time and capture the complete accessible population of Wisconsin Surplus lots closing within the next 30 days. Then allocate up to 60 lots across vehicles, heavy equipment, tools, electronics, and office or institutional assets. Target 12 per category, filling shortfalls by close time and then lot number. For every retained lot, record the lot number, title, agency, category, location, close time, current bid, number of bids, next minimum bid, buyer premium, taxes and fees, inspection, pickup, condition, image count and image URLs, documents, status, and canonical lot link. Preserve the full eligible population and raw category assignments before creating the up-to-60 analysis view. Also preserve duplicates, withdrawn, closed, inaccessible, practice or header, and beyond-window records; allocation arithmetic; pagination or loading boundary; bid timestamp; and unavailable fields. For up to 15 lots chosen under a published category-spread rule, record public reference prices or specifications from an authoritative or established public source when exact identity is supportable. Keep reference values separate from auction condition and fees. Summarize current bids, next-bid increments, premium and fee exposure, close-time concentration, and category values without treating current bids as final cost or recommending a bid. Deliver the complete table, allocation workbook, image manifest, reference matching table, formula-visible fee scenarios, access log, and concise budgeting brief. Do not register, sign in, bid, contact sellers, download image binaries, begin payment, or infer final price, condition, or availability.

rubric.name: Frozen time and access
rubric.requirement: One UTC observation timestamp is fixed, recorded in the deliverables, and supported by contemporaneous browsing evidence. The 30-day window is calculated from it. The access log records public URLs or endpoints used and the pagination or loading boundary, including any site-reported total and pages traversed. An unsupported rounded timestamp is insufficient.

rubric.name: Complete population table
rubric.requirement: The lot-level table covers the complete accessible population, preserves raw categories, and contains no synthetic or padded rows. It preserves all observed duplicate, withdrawn, closed, inaccessible, practice or header, and beyond-window records with their class or reason. Auction-level rows alone are insufficient. Use the end time displayed by the consulted source; an auction-level time may be copied unless captured per-lot evidence contradicts it. Zero-occurrence classes need no explicit record. Every population count stated in the deliverables matches the extraction documented in the browsing record.

rubric.name: Reproducible lot allocation
rubric.requirement: The analysis view contains up to 60 genuine eligible lots and excludes practice, header, placeholder, and synthetic rows. It targets 12 lots in each of the five named categories, using the recorded raw assignments, and fills shortfalls by close time and then lot number. The allocation arithmetic is preserved and reproducible from the population table.

rubric.name: Complete lot fields
rubric.requirement: Every analysis-view lot contains all nineteen requested fields: lot number, title, agency, category, location, close time, current bid, bid count, next minimum bid, buyer premium, taxes and fees, inspection, pickup, condition, image count, image URLs, documents, status, and canonical link. Values match captured sources, and genuinely absent fields are explicitly marked unavailable.

rubric.name: Accurate image manifest
rubric.requirement: The image manifest maps retained lots to extraction-supported source image URLs and image counts. Lots with no images may be marked honestly as zero. The manifest is not empty when lot images were exposed, and ordinary site assets are not counted as lot images.

rubric.name: Supported reference values
rubric.requirement: The reference matching table covers up to 15 retained lots chosen under a published category-spread rule. Every populated reference price or specification is supported by visible access to the named public source and an exact, defensible identity match. Auction condition and fees remain separate. A not supportable result is acceptable; an unevidenced reference value is not.

rubric.name: Correct fee formulas
rubric.requirement: The fee scenarios expose their formulas and inputs. They use the buyer premium, taxes, and fees published for each applicable lot or auction page. Invented rates are not used.

rubric.name: Evidence-based budget brief
rubric.requirement: The budgeting brief and supporting tables cover current bids, next-bid increments, premium and fee exposure, close-time concentration, and category values, with figures consistent with the delivered data. They do not treat current bid as final cost, recommend a bid, or infer final price, condition, or availability beyond the sources.

rubric.name: Defensible categories
rubric.requirement: Allocated and reference-selected lots are defensibly mapped to the five named categories. The category-spread rule used for the reference matching table is explicitly published in the deliverables. All seven requested outputs are identifiable: complete table, allocation workbook, image manifest, reference matching table, fee scenarios with formulas, access log, and budgeting brief.

rubric.name: Read-only conduct
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no registration, sign-in, bidding, seller contact, image-binary download, or payment attempt. Any statements about following these limits agree with the record. Reading public auction pages, terms, and reference sites is allowed.

tasks.title: List every restaurant in East Hartford, CT
tasks.instruction: I'm preparing a catering pitch to independent restaurants in East Hartford, CT, and need a complete local restaurant list. Use Yelp's restaurant results and work through all the filtered results, however Yelp divides them into pages. For every distinct restaurant returned, record its name, full street address, listed phone, Yelp page link, cuisine categories, price tier, rating, review count, claimed status, and any business website, ordering details, hours, or other business contact information Yelp shows. Mark missing fields "not shown." List businesses with addresses outside East Hartford separately. Combine repeated listings only when the name plus address or phone agree, and keep separate locations of one brand as separate rows. Check each retained restaurant against its own website, Connecticut business registration records, a mapping profile, or town health-inspection records. Name the source and keep conflicts in phone, address, trading name, or operating status visible. For conflicting current contact or status information, prefer official business sites or government records over mapping profiles. Flag likely closures or moves using the strongest public evidence, and name restaurants with no outside confirmation. Record the date and clock time of the Yelp observations. If Yelp blocks access, state which pages you saw and where access stopped, and describe the unseen results as unmeasured. Provide the restaurant table, a record of out-of-area businesses and duplicates, a list of Yelp-versus-outside-source conflicts, and a ranked non-chain shortlist with its ranking rule. Do not sign in, contact a business, place an order, or gather personal details about owners or staff.

rubric.name: Valid restaurant entries
rubric.requirement: Every restaurant row is supported by a Yelp observation. The main local list contains East Hartford addresses; businesses with other addresses are kept in the separate out-of-area record. A business found only through an outside source is not inserted into the Yelp population.

rubric.name: Accurate Yelp fields
rubric.requirement: For retained and out-of-area entries, every Yelp value matches captured evidence: name, street address, phone, Yelp link, categories, price tier, rating, review count, claimed status, website, ordering, hours, and other contact details. Missing fields say not shown. Outside-source additions name their source, and one business's values are never assigned to another.

rubric.name: All Yelp pages checked
rubric.requirement: All accessible Yelp restaurant-results pages are visited through the last page offered, and every distinct returned restaurant is captured in the local table or separate out-of-area record. The record includes retrieval date and clock time, page order, and where results end. If access is blocked, it names the pages observed and stopping point and calls the unseen remainder unmeasured, not empty or complete.

rubric.name: Out-of-area and duplicate records
rubric.requirement: Businesses with addresses outside East Hartford are listed separately. Repeats are combined only when the name plus address or phone agree. Separate locations of the same brand remain separate rows. This check applies to the entries present.

rubric.name: Outside confirmation coverage
rubric.requirement: Every retained restaurant has a documented relevant outside-source check attempt using its own website, Connecticut business records, a mapping profile, or town health-inspection records. Each attempt has a source or query, visible browsing evidence, and its outcome. A no-confirmation entry counts only with a documented attempt or concrete access limitation. Not-found and inaccessible outcomes are not confirmation; unattempted rows, geocoding alone, and invented confirmations do not satisfy attempt coverage.

rubric.name: Conflicts and status
rubric.requirement: The conflict list keeps both values for every phone, address, trading-name, or operating-status disagreement found. Official business sites and government records take priority over mapping profiles for current contact or status. Closure or move flags cite their supporting evidence. No outside confirmation and no observed conflict are distinguished from checks that were never attempted.

rubric.name: Yelp access record
rubric.requirement: The report records the Yelp observation date and clock time. When access stops, it gives the pages observed and boundary reached and calls the unseen remainder unmeasured, never zero. Completeness claims do not go beyond that boundary.

rubric.name: Four structured outputs
rubric.requirement: All four structured outputs exist: restaurant table, out-of-area and duplicate record, Yelp-versus-outside conflict list, and non-chain shortlist with a stated ranking rule. Missing fields use not shown. Tables with headers only are acceptable if Yelp was fully blocked before any results appeared.

rubric.name: Valid non-chain shortlist
rubric.requirement: The shortlist includes only non-chain restaurants in the retained table and follows its stated ranking rule. If no restaurants were retained, this check does not apply.

rubric.name: Honesty and conduct
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in, business contact, order placement, or collection of personal details about owners or staff. Claims in the final report, README, block note, or methodology files about counts, completion, outside-check coverage, labels, sources of information, and sources consulted are materially accurate. Notes from an interrupted run count as its report. Field errors are checked elsewhere; honest descriptions of documented blocks are acceptable.

tasks.title: Inventory GMX bounty repositories
tasks.instruction: I'm documenting the public GitHub repositories linked by GMX’s Immunefi bounty and comparing its linked deployment-folder inventories. Open https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/gmx/ and inspect the Information, Scope, and Resources sections. Record the GitHub links directly exposed in the program’s content, with their original URL, source section, label, displayed order, access result, and UTC check time. Exclude general navigation and do not follow blockchain-explorer links or inspect contract code. Identify each link as a repository, folder, file, or organization, and map repository-related links to the current owner, repository name, and main repository URL. Preserve duplicate references, redirects, renames, and ambiguous links. For each distinct linked repository, use its public page or public GitHub API to record its exact identity, default branch, archive status, and the latest commit on its default branch, including the commit identifier and date. Keep the branch written in a source link separate from the repository’s default branch. For the Arbitrum and Avalanche deployment folders linked by the bounty, record the commit identifier currently reached by the linked branch and use that same commit for both folder inventories. List every file and subfolder directly inside each folder, including hidden names, but do not descend into subfolders. Record each entry’s name, full path, file-or-folder type, byte size when supplied, Git object identifier, and public page URL; mark unavailable fields explicitly. Use only directory metadata, not file contents or code downloads. Match files across the two folders by filename, and report names found in both, names found in only one, and whether same-name files have equal or different Git object identifiers. Give per-folder file and subfolder counts and supported size totals, keeping unknown sizes distinct from zero. State which repository or path claims the bounty explicitly supports, and keep mere links, organization membership, and folder contents separate from proof of bounty scope. Provide the original-link table, deduplicated repository table, two folder inventories, filename comparison, scope-evidence table, access log, and a short coverage note explaining the counts and any unresolved differences. Record genuine access failures and source changes without treating them as empty repositories or complete inventories. Do not sign in, contact maintainers, submit reports, test systems, search for vulnerabilities or exploits, download or execute code, or draw security conclusions.

rubric.name: Public bounty links
rubric.requirement: The Information, Scope, and Resources sections are inspected. The original-link table records each direct GitHub link in the program content with source section, label, displayed order, access result, and UTC check time. General navigation is excluded. No fixed count or remembered link list replaces the observed links.

rubric.name: Repository identity and versions
rubric.requirement: Each distinct linked repository has public-source evidence for owner, name, main URL, default branch, archive status, and latest default-branch commit identifier and date. The branch in an original source URL remains separate from the default branch. An unavailable field is explicitly marked, not guessed.

rubric.name: Complete folder inventories
rubric.requirement: The Arbitrum and Avalanche deployment folders linked by the bounty are both inventoried at the same recorded commit reached from the linked branch. Every direct child, including hidden files and subfolders, is retained. Subfolders are not recursively expanded. Partial or truncated responses are not called complete.

rubric.name: Folder metadata accuracy
rubric.requirement: Each folder entry has its name, full path, file-or-folder type, byte size when supplied, Git object identifier, and public page URL. Values agree with public directory metadata at the recorded commit. Missing sizes are explicit and are not changed to zero.

rubric.name: Cross-folder file comparison
rubric.requirement: The comparison matches files by filename and correctly separates shared names from names found in only one folder. For each shared filename, equal or different Git object identifiers are recorded from the two inventories. A name match alone is not called identical file content.

rubric.name: Scope claims kept separate
rubric.requirement: The scope-evidence table identifies the program wording supporting each repository or path claim. A mere link, organization membership, or presence in a folder is not independently treated as proof of bounty scope. Ambiguous claims remain explicit and no security conclusion is drawn.

rubric.name: Complete output package
rubric.requirement: The original-link table, repository table, both folder inventories, filename comparison, scope-evidence table, access log, and short coverage note are all provided as identifiable structured files or sections. A missing required output does not pass.

rubric.name: Read-only metadata research
rubric.requirement: The record contains only public bounty pages, repository information, and directory metadata. It shows no blockchain-explorer traversal, contract-code inspection, code download or execution, sign-in, maintainer contact, report submission, system testing, vulnerability or exploit search, or security conclusion.

rubric.name: Traceable links and access results
rubric.requirement: Original links remain traceable to their current repository or path. Duplicates, redirects, renames, ambiguities, access failures, and source changes are recorded without inventing observations or confusing an inaccessible source with an empty one. Claimed public checks and UTC times have supporting evidence.

rubric.name: Consistent counts and explanation
rubric.requirement: The coverage note gives file and subfolder counts for each folder and size totals from supported file sizes, with unknown sizes separate. It explains the filename comparison and unresolved differences. All counts and totals can be recalculated from the delivered inventories and agree across the outputs.

tasks.title: Audit Flying Tiger Turkey mobile product pages
tasks.instruction: Audit mobile product-detail-page problems on Flying Tiger Turkey. At one timestamp, use https://www.flyingtiger.com.tr/ while logged out at 390×844 CSS pixels. For every top-level category, select its first purchasable product and its first distinct product that visibly has variants. If no public variant-bearing product is found after exhaustion, record the shortfall and continue. Preserve the category, filters, sort, displayed count, rank, exclusions, URL, SKU, price, promotion, stock, and time. Replace duplicate SKUs or SKU-less URLs with the next item. Capture each PDP before scrolling. Test one available variant when possible and perform a guest-cart add and remove. Answer every code for every PDP using only yes, no, partially, or na, with evidence: 5.1 above-fold product and price; 5.2 discount; 5.3 urgency; 5.4 favorites; 5.5 payments or installments; 5.6 breadcrumbs; 5.7 gallery quality; 5.8 zoom; 5.9 thumbnails; 5.10 arrows or swipe; 5.11 video or 360; 5.12 customer images; 5.13 variant visibility; 5.14 variant selection; 5.15 variant price; 5.16 variant stock; 5.17 guest add-to-cart; 5.18 cart feedback and remove; 5.19 mobile information controls; 5.20 specifications; 5.21 description; 5.22 warranty; 5.23 delivery; 5.24 shipping cost; 5.25 campaign or free shipping; 5.26 returns or exchanges; 5.27 store stock; 5.28 restock control; 5.29 rating summary; 5.30 reviews; 5.31 recommendations; 5.32 relevance; 5.33 personalization; 5.34 product identity; 5.35 purchase readiness. Verify store terms through official Turkish help or policy pages and product facts through official brand or manufacturer pages when available. Separate observations from verified facts and preserve conflicts and timestamps. Prefer the PDP for interface state, official Turkish policy pages for store terms, and official brand or manufacturer sources for product facts. Compare groups, identify systemic failures, and rank exactly five fixes by reach, purchase impact, severity, and confidence. Return one valid JSON list containing a source table, PDP records, verification log, code answers, conflict notes, and prioritized brief. Log evidence gaps and continue publicly; access failure does not prove absence. Do not log in, create accounts, enter personal or payment data, submit checkout, contact anyone, or buy.

rubric.name: Verified mobile state
