rubric.requirement: The entire browsing record contains no sign-in, records request, fee payment, or form submission other than public property searches and map-layer queries. The output contains no owner or occupant identity or contact details. This applies even if no report was produced.

tasks.title: List standard features of a Cavco modular home
tasks.instruction: I'm comparing modular homes before signing with a retailer and need the complete standard features for Cavco's Westlake Modular 24603A. Open https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-homes/cavcodotcom/standard/us/596-westlake-modular-24603a, expand every collapsed 'Show More' area, and record every standard feature in displayed order, with its exact wording, visible category heading, and observation time in UTC. Also record the published square footage, bedrooms, baths, dimensions, section count, and series. Keep the builder's stated values separate from any calculations you make. Check as many recorded features as possible against other official materials for the model and independent retailer listings for the same 24603A plan. Mark each feature confirmed standard, contradicted, described as optional or upgrade, or unverified, and keep conflicting wording separate. Repeat the same collection for every other Westlake Modular plan the builder publicly lists, combine duplicate plans by model number, and report how far you reached rather than filling gaps with assumptions. Compare the records to show which standard features are shared across the Westlake line, which are unique to 24603A, and which differ in scope or brand. Mark unavailable values as unavailable. A blocked page or failed expansion is an access problem, not evidence that a feature does not exist. First provide the 24603A features as a two-column table separated by pipe characters, with the exact header 'Category | Standard Feature' and wrapped in triple backticks. Then provide the specification sheet, a verification record for each feature, a table of shared and unique features, and notes on access problems and conflicts. Do not sign in, request a quote, contact a retailer, submit any form, or share personal contact details.

rubric.name: Format feature table
rubric.requirement: The 24603A output includes a two-column table separated by pipes, with the exact header `Category | Standard Feature`, wrapped in triple backticks. Clearly separate sections provide specifications, per-feature checks, shared-versus-unique comparisons, and access and conflict notes. An optional language tag on the opening code fence is allowed, but the exact header remains a table row inside the fenced block.

rubric.name: Capture all features
rubric.requirement: Every standard-feature item shown on the page appears as a row in displayed order under its visible category heading. Repeated source items remain wherever they appear. The capture has an observation time in UTC. The browsing record shows every collapsed Show More area expanded and its revealed items extracted, or a documented failed expansion. A failed expansion is not complete capture of its unseen contents. No source item is omitted, added, reordered, or incorrectly combined as a duplicate.

rubric.name: Preserve exact wording
rubric.requirement: Every feature and category heading uses the source wording. Headings are not abbreviated, and all words, digits, and asterisks are kept. Harmless formatting differences are allowed.

rubric.name: Record model specifications
rubric.requirement: The specification sheet accurately reports the builder's displayed square footage, bedrooms, baths, series, and model name. Dimensions and section count follow the displayed source. Dimensions, section count, or area calculations not published by the builder are labeled third-party information, arithmetic, or inference.

rubric.name: Classify every feature
rubric.requirement: Every captured feature is individually named and assigned exactly one explicit status: confirmed standard, contradicted, described as optional or upgrade, or unverified. Grouped unnamed entries such as “all Interior rows” or “remaining rows” are insufficient. Unverified is acceptable if the consulted sources do not cover that feature.

rubric.name: Support verification claims
rubric.requirement: Every positive status and quoted comparison has a source shown in the browsing record, with conflicting wording kept side by side. If a cited source group or step has several URLs, at least one opened source contains the quote. “Unverified” makes no positive claim. An opened official floor-plan drawing can support a specific optional label when its relevant label is readable in the inspected evidence. Optional configurations outside the captured rows do not contradict a statement limited to those rows. Any unsupported positive claim fails this check.

rubric.name: Cover the full roster
rubric.requirement: The work lists every publicly listed Westlake Modular plan reachable during review, combining duplicates by model number. For each plan it repeats the standard-feature and specification collection requested for 24603A, preserving order, wording, headings, and observation time. It records checked pages or endpoints and where the search stopped. Blocked or inaccessible remaining plans are reported as an access gap. A subset is never called the complete public list.

rubric.name: Compare plan features
rubric.requirement: The shared-versus-unique table follows the plan data actually collected. Claims of shared features, unique features, or differences in scope or brand are backed by the compared records and limited to checked plans. If all checked plans show the same feature block, saying all captured features are shared and none unique is acceptable. Differences in overall specifications are not mislabeled as feature differences.

rubric.name: Describe access accurately
rubric.requirement: The outputs accurately record each feature's observation time in UTC and describe relevant expansion attempts, timeouts, blocks, and CAPTCHAs in the access and conflict notes. Failed access never proves a value or feature absent, and unavailable values are not guessed. Describing a collapsed or CSS-clipped panel as hidden, not visible, not rendered, or missing from the rendered view is acceptable when true.

rubric.name: Avoid prohibited actions
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in, quote request, retailer contact, form submission, or sharing of personal contact details, and the output does not claim otherwise. Viewing public retailer or dealer listings is allowed and is not contact.

tasks.title: Find jobs across Western Sydney
tasks.instruction: I'm helping a candidate decide where to apply for jobs across Western Sydney. On Seek.com.au and Indeed's Australian site, use the location controls to search Western Sydney Area, sort by newest postings, and collect the ten newest listings on each site, or all listings if there are fewer than ten, in displayed order. For each listing, record the job title, company name as displayed, full public job description, main listing URL, suburb, work type, salary wording, posted-date wording, advertiser type (direct employer, agency, or undisclosed), source site, and check time. Use not listed for missing fields. Compare listings across the two sites for duplicates using company, title, location, and description matches. Keep both source rows for duplicates and flag the earlier posting rather than combining them. Verify as many retained roles as possible against the employer's own careers page or official applicant-tracking listing, checking title, company, location, and whether the role is still open. Use other job aggregators only to find leads, not as verification. Keep expired, relocated, undisclosed-advertiser, and inaccessible listings in a record of exclusions and access problems. Record bot checks and empty results as observed; they do not prove that a posting does not exist. Omit recruiter names, personal email addresses, and direct mobile numbers even when the listing publishes them. Summarize the retained jobs by site, suburb, advertiser type, and whether a salary is shown, and state how much of the ten-per-site target you could access. Provide output.csv with Job Title, Job Description, Company Name, source site, listing URL, and observation time, plus the ordered list from each site, a table matching roles to employer verification, a duplicate and disagreement log, and a short report on live roles. Do not sign in, apply, submit forms other than public search, location, and sort controls, contact anyone, bypass bot checks, collect personal contact information, or invent description text that the listing did not show.

rubric.name: Seek results collected
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows a Seek search using Western Sydney location controls and newest-first sorting. Evidence supports rows for the ten newest displayed listings, or a clearly stated complete smaller set, in displayed order. A location keyword alone, unfiltered radius results, or invented rows are not enough. If Seek is blocked, record the failed attempt and mark listing collection incomplete; the access report is judged separately and does not establish that the ten-listing target was collected.

rubric.name: Indeed results collected
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows a date-sorted search on Indeed's Australian site. Retained rows contain the ten newest displayed Western Sydney listings, or a clearly stated complete smaller set, in displayed order. Clearly out-of-area listings are recorded as exclusions rather than silently dropped. If Indeed is blocked, record the failed attempt and mark listing collection incomplete; the access report is judged separately and does not establish that the ten-listing target was collected.

rubric.name: Complete listing details
rubric.requirement: output.csv includes Job Title, Job Description, Company Name, source site, listing URL, and observation time. For every captured row, the ordered list also has title, displayed company, main listing URL, suburb, work type, salary wording, posted-date wording, advertiser type, source site, and check time. Missing information says “not listed.” Displayed wording and digits are preserved.

rubric.name: Full descriptions preserved
rubric.requirement: Each Job Description includes the full public listing text except recruiter names, personal emails, and direct mobile numbers, which must be removed. These removals do not make it incomplete. It is not a shortened excerpt with ellipses, search snippet, paraphrase, or invented replacement. not listed is used only when the description was truly inaccessible and that access problem is recorded.

rubric.name: Duplicate comparisons recorded
rubric.requirement: The duplicate and disagreement log shows comparisons across sites using company, title, location, and description matches. Duplicate listings keep both source rows and flag the earlier posting instead of being combined. A supported finding of no duplicates is acceptable; invented pairs are not.

rubric.name: Employer listings checked
rubric.requirement: The employer-verification table gives every retained role an honest status. Any claim that title, company, location, or open status was verified has support from an employer careers page or official applicant-tracking listing in the browsing record. Other aggregators do not count as confirmation. An honest unverified status is acceptable. Each retained role has a recorded employer-careers or official ATS lookup attempt, or a concrete access or identity limitation explaining why it could not be attempted. An unsupported blanket “unverified” label does not establish attempt coverage; successful confirmation is not required where unavailable.

rubric.name: Access problems and conduct recorded
rubric.requirement: The exclusion and access record includes expired, relocated, undisclosed-advertiser, and inaccessible listings with reasons. Every access wall, bot check, or empty result is recorded as an access event and not proof of absence. No sign-in, application, non-search form submission, contact, or bot-check bypass occurs. All claims about copying and checking agree with the browsing record. Ordinary public search, location, and sort controls are permitted; applications, contact, registration, and bot-check bypass remain prohibited.

rubric.name: Personal contact details removed
rubric.requirement: No delivered file or final message contains recruiter names, personal email addresses, or direct mobile numbers, including when those details occur in public job descriptions or raw listing content.

rubric.name: Consistent summary
rubric.requirement: The live-roles report and summary group the retained jobs by site, suburb, advertiser type, and salary disclosure. They state the accessible share of the ten-per-site target. Every reported number, required or volunteered, including ranges, verification totals, and duplicate counts, can be reproduced from the delivered rows, records, and verification table.

rubric.name: Supported advertiser labels
rubric.requirement: Advertiser labels do not contradict the listing's own wording. Qualified labels such as “undisclosed-advertiser / agency” are acceptable. A missing label is assessed under field completeness.

tasks.title: Pull U.S. import data for bulk bags, HTS 6305.32
tasks.instruction:
Build the official U.S. annual import-quantity series for flexible intermediate bulk containers under HTS 6305.32 using the public USITC DataWeb query tool. Select Imports: For Consumption, HTS Items, First Unit of Quantity, Actual values, Full Years, annual results, and aggregated commodities. Show India, China, and Mexico separately and include an all-countries total.

Use official HTS or DataWeb classification evidence to identify the first full calendar year in which 6305.32 is available, then collect every completed annual result through the most recent full year DataWeb offers. Do not force the code into earlier years. If an older year predates the code, label it not applicable with the supporting classification evidence rather than reporting zero. Capture every returned value for all three countries and the all-countries total. Distinguish a true null, suppressed value, reported zero, not-applicable year, and failed request.

For every country-year, record the reported quantity, unit of measure, HTS description in force, query settings, and UTC retrieval time. Check the definition of 6305.32 and any code split, statistical-suffix change, or schedule revision across the series against the official Harmonized Tariff Schedule and USITC documentation. Reconcile India, China, and Mexico with the all-countries total for every year, calculate the residual rest-of-world share, and flag any difference beyond rounding without changing the reported parts or total.

If DataWeb is under maintenance or refuses part of the period, retain everything it returns and state exactly which request or years failed. An outage is not evidence that trade did not occur. Deliver a country-year table or spreadsheet, query-parameter log, classification-change timeline, reconciliation sheet, and short explanation of how the three countries’ shares changed. Do not sign in, buy subscription data, or invent an unobserved cell.

rubric.name: Configure exact query
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows a public DataWeb query using Imports: For Consumption, HTS Items, commodity 6305.32, First Unit of Quantity, Actual values, Full Years, annual results, aggregated commodities, India, China, and Mexico separately, and an all-countries aggregate in the same or a separate run. It records the first supported full year and most recent completed offered year from official evidence, and no sign-in occurs.

rubric.name: Capture country series
rubric.requirement: The structured data contains India, China, and Mexico for every completed year in the official 6305.32 window identified by the research. Each populated value comes from an executed DataWeb query with visible extraction evidence. A year before the code existed is marked not applicable with classification evidence, and a refused or missing result remains explicitly unresolved rather than becoming zero.

rubric.name: Capture total series
rubric.requirement: The structured data contains an observed all-countries total for every completed year in the official 6305.32 window that DataWeb returns. The browsing record shows the query output supplying each total. A pre-code year is labeled not applicable with official classification evidence, while a failed aggregate request or discarded returned row remains a visible gap and does not count as an observed total.

rubric.name: Preserve reported quantities
rubric.requirement: Every reported quantity and unit exactly matches DataWeb's returned Imports: For Consumption value for the stated country and year. No unobserved cell is assigned a number or unit, and each populated cell remains attributable to the captured query output.

rubric.name: Label every cell
rubric.requirement: Every country-year cell has a source-supported status: reported quantity, reported zero, null, suppressed, not applicable, or failed request. A missing result not explained by the source remains not observed. These statuses stay distinct; null does not mean that the code was not in force. Missing, refused, or suppressed values are not converted to zero. Official classification evidence supports any not-applicable year.

rubric.name: Document HTS history
rubric.requirement: The definitional-change timeline uses official HTS or USITC material actually retrieved and records when 6305.32 and any applicable statistical suffixes, predecessor coverage, description changes, unit changes, splits, or schedule revisions appear in the evidence. It does not assume a predecessor code or effective year that the cited official material does not establish.

rubric.name: Reconcile annual totals
rubric.requirement: For every year with the necessary captured values, the reconciliation compares India plus China plus Mexico with the observed all-countries total, correctly calculates the residual rest-of-world share, and reports whether any difference exceeds the disclosed rounding rule. It changes no source figure and preserves every documented disagreement.

rubric.name: Provide all outputs
rubric.requirement: The output includes all five structured outputs: country-year table, query-parameter log, definitional-change timeline, reconciliation sheet, and short narrative. Country-year records contain quantity, unit, HTS description in force, settings or source information, and cell status, and the work reports a UTC retrieval date and time. This check concerns structure only.

rubric.name: Explain share trends
rubric.requirement: The short explanation accurately describes the collected shares’ direction and rough size. It reflects Mexico’s, China’s, and India’s collected share trends across the requested period. Every trend statement agrees with the delivered data.

rubric.name: Report limitations honestly
rubric.requirement: The work reports only cells, queries, and source checks supported by the browsing record. It does not present incomplete current-year values as full-year data. Each outage or refusal is recorded with the affected request and years, and missing results are never treated as proof of no imports. There is no sign-in or purchase of subscription data.

tasks.title: Record every FinSMEs article from one day
tasks.instruction: I need a complete record of FinSMEs articles dated October 9, 2025. Use its public archive, pagination, sitemap, date pages, and search as needed to find every article displaying that publication date. Record each route used to find articles, result order, count, overlap, and access state. For every qualifying article, record title, URL, displayed publication and update time, author when shown, company, funding or transaction type, amount and currency, investors or counterparties, headquarters, sector, a short announcement summary, and the cited original release. Record the full set for that date before combining duplicates. Keep updates, syndicated articles, and articles about the same company as separate page identities. If the archive cannot establish completeness, report an evidence-supported zero or the specific source limitations. Where available, check the company, date, round or transaction type, amount, and named investors against a public company announcement, investor page, regulatory filing, or original release, preserving conflicts. Summarize the full day's articles by type, geography, sector, disclosed amount, and verification coverage. Keep currencies separate unless a clearly explained conversion is requested. Provide the complete October 9 article table, a record of discovery and duplicate handling, a company-and-deal verification table, a list of conflicts, summaries with visible formulas, and a short daily report. Do not replace the full set with hand-picked articles, infer undisclosed deal terms, contact companies, reproduce full articles, or claim coverage of the venture market beyond FinSMEs on that date.

rubric.name: Capture all articles
rubric.requirement: When a complete public discovery route is accessible, the structured table includes every qualifying FinSMEs URL dated October 9, 2025, and excludes other dates and non-article pages. Browsing evidence establishes where the full set ends. If archive, pagination, sitemap, date, and search routes cannot establish completeness, the result records source failures and a supported partial or zero finding, without guessing or claiming completeness.

rubric.name: Accurate article data
rubric.requirement: For each row present, title, URL, publication or update time, author, company, transaction type, amount and currency, investors, headquarters, summary, and original release match displayed FinSMEs content. All investors named in the body and all disclosed amounts are kept. Undisclosed amounts are not invented, and FinSMEs is not mislabeled as the original release.

rubric.name: Document discovery paths
rubric.requirement: The discovery-and-duplicate log covers the routes actually used as needed, such as date-archive pagination, REST API, sitemap, month archive, or search. It records displayed order, counts, overlap, access state, and failures, matching browsing evidence. For routes mixing dates, total and qualifying result counts are separate.

rubric.name: Check available outside sources
rubric.requirement: For each article with an available qualifying external source, the output compares individual fields with content actually retrieved from a company announcement, investor page, filing, or original release. FinSMEs and search snippets do not count as external checks.

rubric.name: Resolve every article
rubric.requirement: Every article has a verification-table result: either checking supported by retrieved external content or its own unavailable or shortfall status supported by a visible attempt. Labels without searches or retrieved sources do not prove full coverage.

rubric.name: Keep verification honest
rubric.requirement: No verification is claimed without browsing evidence. Counts and percentages are not inflated, checked rows have retrieved support, and conflicting round labels, headquarters typos, or teaser-versus-body wording remain visible in the verification table or conflict list. Honest zero-coverage reporting is acceptable.

rubric.name: Consistent summaries
rubric.requirement: Summaries cover article type, geography, sector, disclosed amount, and verification coverage, keeping currencies separate. All counts, totals, formulas, and coverage figures agree with the article table and other outputs. The short report and formula-visible summaries use consistent amount totals, geography splits, and verified-versus-unverified counts.

rubric.name: Provide six deliverables
rubric.requirement: All six requested outputs are present and distinguishable: article table, discovery-and-duplicate log, verification table, conflict list, formula-visible summaries, and daily report. Every article row has the requested fields, with missing values explicit. An empty conflict list states that no conflicts were observed. For a documented zero-result set or an unavailable scope allowed by the instruction, header-only tables with the required fields and an explicit explanation count as present outputs. They do not by themselves prove complete discovery. Missing outputs fail this check.

rubric.name: Respect scope boundaries
rubric.requirement: The final message and daily report name only existing files and limit completeness to the documented FinSMEs October 9 pages. They do not call a hand-picked subset complete, claim unused discovery routes, invent deal terms, contact companies, claim company contact that did not happen, or reproduce full articles instead of short summaries. Raw extraction files and page text kept as working evidence are allowed.

rubric.name: Use practical formats
rubric.requirement: Summaries show formulas or arithmetic for article type, geography, sector, disclosed amount, and verification coverage and agree with the full article table. The daily report is concise. Any created category labels are defined and used consistently.

tasks.title: Build a Blue Cross Laboratories insights library
tasks.instruction: I'm building a Blue Cross Laboratories insights library so reviewers can see what is published, supported, and missing. At the task-start observation time, check every section, category, archive, page, tab, and load-more result under Medical Tips & Clinical Insights at https://www.bluecrosslabs.com/medical-tips-clinical-insights/. Record the views, their order and counts, where the results end, and whether they are accessible. For every PDF, keep the exact title, full direct PDF URL, source page, context, date or version, description, products, topics, category, and division. Mark anything inferred and leave unknowns empty. Check that every downloaded file is a PDF, and record its observation time, destination, page count, and evidence for its fields. Verify product names and clinical claims using Blue Cross product pages or labels and at least one non-Blue Cross regulator registry or bibliographic record. Keep what the site says separate from facts confirmed by other sources. Compare PDF destinations and document identities to identify duplicates, keep conflicts, and prefer PDF content over listing text and authoritative records over secondary summaries. Analyze the documents by topic, product, category, division, year, duplication, broken links, and verification status. Prioritize documents for review based on unsupported claims, outdated details, and coverage gaps without making clinical recommendations. Provide a source record, validation and verification log, coverage brief, and a downloadable attachment or link to bluecrosslabs_clinical_insights.txt. That file must contain only parseable JSON with a top-level “Clinical Insights” object containing page_url and values records with the keys name, pdf_url, description, products, topics, category, and division. If a source is blocked or missing, record the gap and continue using other public evidence; failed access does not prove absence. Do not log in, submit forms other than public archive, registry, and bibliographic search controls, contact anyone, enter personal data, or publish the document collection on a public host.

rubric.name: Document archive boundary
rubric.requirement: At the recorded task-start time, the coverage record checks every accessible section, category, archive, page, tab, and load-more result under Medical Tips & Clinical Insights. Each observed view records order, card count, first and last result or equivalent boundary evidence, and access status. Controls or views the site does not expose are not required. Blocked or incomplete coverage is explicitly reported.

rubric.name: PDF corpus capture
rubric.requirement: Every distinct PDF-linked document found while checking the whole archive has a structured record with extraction evidence. PDF-linked documents count as entries in the collection. Non-PDF archive entries are logged separately with their observed format and access result. They are not silently converted into, or counted as, retained PDF documents.

rubric.name: Capture full corpus
rubric.requirement: Structured records cover every unique PDF destination observed at task start. Each duplicate is explained or clearly noted.

rubric.name: Preserve record details
rubric.requirement: For every delivered record, titles use exact source wording and pdf_url contains a direct source URL whose returned bytes validate as PDF. A literal .pdf URL suffix is not required; an HTML page or image file must not be relabeled as PDF. It stays empty for listings observed at task start without a PDF. Source page, context, date or version, description, products, topics, category, and division have source evidence, are marked as inference, or are empty. Values are not invented or copied from another record.

rubric.name: Validate downloaded PDFs
rubric.requirement: For every item called downloaded or validated, the validation log gives a PDF check using magic bytes or content type, destination, page count, and observation time. The browsing record shows the actual download. Items not validated are clearly labeled according to the stated sampling scope.

rubric.name: Support confirmation claims
rubric.requirement: Every claim of confirmation in the verification log is backed by retrieved Blue Cross material or an independent record, includes specific identifiers where available, and matches the source shown in the browsing record. Blue Cross site observations remain separate from facts confirmed across sources.

rubric.name: Document verification coverage
rubric.requirement: Every retained PDF that names a product or makes a clinical claim has a verification record. The record gives a check against Blue Cross product pages or labels and a check against at least one independent regulator registry or bibliographic record, with the fields checked, source identifiers where available, and outcomes. Genuine access failures or missing source information are recorded as gaps, not confirmation. Non-PDF archive entries remain in a separate format and access log and are not counted as verified PDFs. Unattempted checks do not satisfy coverage.

rubric.name: Analyze corpus coverage
rubric.requirement: The coverage brief analyzes delivered documents by topic, product, category, division, year, duplication, broken links, and verification status. It prioritizes review using unsupported claims, outdated details, and coverage gaps, gives no clinical recommendations, and uses counts consistent with the declared collection and source record.

rubric.name: Provide required files
rubric.requirement: The outputs include a source record, validation and verification logs, coverage brief, and a file named exactly bluecrosslabs_clinical_insights.txt. The file contains only parseable JSON with a top-level “Clinical Insights” object, page_url, and values records containing name, pdf_url, description, products, topics, category, and division. Empty values and extra keys are allowed. The file is supplied as an accessible attachment or download link, not merely named in the response.

rubric.name: Work honestly and safely
rubric.requirement: The work does not claim checks that were not performed, use hard-coded or simulated registry data, name registries never accessed, overstate completeness, claim files that do not exist, or treat failed access as absence. It performs no login, non-search form submission, contact, personal-data entry, or publication of the collection on a public host. The public search controls named in the instruction are allowed.

tasks.title: Identify a product from an invoice line
tasks.instruction: I'm checking an invoice line that says “tubular bandage natural c 10m lf” and need to identify the actual medical product without forcing a match. Search Eastern Health's public procurement, catalogue, and product information first. Then use manufacturer catalogues and established Australian medical suppliers as needed to work out the abbreviation. Build a list of up to eight distinct products, or every plausible documented match if there are fewer, covering reasonable meanings of “natural,” size C, 10 m, and “lf.” For each candidate, record the official product name, manufacturer, product family, catalogue or supplier code, size designation and limb-size range, colour, roll length, packaging, published latex or material statement, intended use, market context, and source. Show how each word or abbreviation in the invoice agrees or conflicts with the product evidence. Distinguish an exact manufacturer-code match from a match based only on description, and compare distributor names with the manufacturer catalogue. State weights for code, size, length, colour, packaging, regional availability, and source authority, and use them to score the candidates. Recalculate the ranking after removing ambiguous invoice terms to see whether the result changes. Provide a candidate-product workbook, a table comparing invoice terms with product evidence, an evidence-quality scorecard, and a short memo naming the strongest match and what remains uncertain. If files cannot be created, provide structured tables. Do not contact suppliers or submit enquiries.

rubric.name: Eastern Health searched first
rubric.requirement: Before moving into manufacturer or supplier research, the browsing record shows a search for Eastern Health public procurement, catalogue, or product information using easternhealth.org.au pages or Eastern Health-targeted searches. Starting directly with suppliers without checking Eastern Health is not enough.

rubric.name: Evidence for the identifying terms
rubric.requirement: Opened pages, PDFs, or screenshots—not search snippets alone—provide candidate evidence used to assess natural, size C, 10 m, and LF. Any term not resolved by the inspected sources stays explicitly uncertain rather than being forced into a match.

rubric.name: Four required outputs
rubric.requirement: The output includes the candidate-product workbook, invoice-term comparison table, evidence-quality scorecard, and identification memo, as files or structured tables. Each candidate row has official name, manufacturer, family, code, size and limb range, colour, length, packaging, latex or material statement, intended use, market context, and source. Unknown is acceptable.

rubric.name: Supported product details
rubric.requirement: Every candidate value other than unknown is supported by source content actually opened. This includes codes, limb ranges, packaging, lengths, latex or material statements, ARTG numbers, market context, and source attribution. An unopened URL or information taken from clipped or blocked content does not provide support.

rubric.name: Distinct product candidates
rubric.requirement: The list contains no more than eight candidates. Each is a distinct documented product, not a repeated SKU, generic category, or catch-all placeholder.

rubric.name: Every invoice term compared
rubric.requirement: A structured table checks tubular bandage, natural, C, 10m, and LF against every candidate and marks evidence for and against a match. Every conflict found in opened sources is kept. For example, a source saying a Tubigrip candidate contains latex must be recorded as a conflict if LF is interpreted as latex-free.

rubric.name: Code and description matches separated
rubric.requirement: A candidate is called an exact manufacturer-code match only if the invoice supplies that code and an opened manufacturer source identifies the same product by that code. A code found only in a catalogue does not make a description-only invoice an exact code match. Distributor SKUs are clearly identified as distributor codes. Comparisons of distributor and manufacturer names rely only on opened sources.

rubric.name: Stated weights applied
rubric.requirement: The scorecard gives weights for all seven criteria: code, size, length, colour, packaging, regional availability, and source authority. Totals are calculated correctly, weights are applied consistently, and the ranking agrees with the memo. No evidence-based points contradict a candidate's recorded sources.

rubric.name: Ranking recalculated without ambiguous terms
rubric.requirement: The ranking is recalculated after removing only terms the research identified as ambiguous. Updated scores or order are shown, with a statement of whether the leading candidate changes. Calling the ranking robust without showing the recalculation is not enough.

rubric.name: Strongest match and uncertainty
rubric.requirement: The memo names the leading candidate supported by evidence and explains remaining uncertainty, including any unresolved code, abbreviation, or Eastern Health linkage actually found during the research. It need not invent a particular uncertainty. It does not call the identification definitive or confirmed or claim the product is an Eastern Health contract item without evidence.

rubric.name: No supplier contact
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no supplier contact, quote or enquiry submission, email, or account signup used to message a supplier. Public product and contact pages may be viewed.

tasks.title: Compare bulk-bag imports from four countries
tasks.instruction: Analyze U.S. general imports of flexible intermediate bulk containers under HTS 6305.32 from India, China, Mexico, and Vietnam for 2020–2025. Reproduce the USITC DataWeb query using HTS Items, First Unit of Quantity, Actual values, Full Years, annual aggregation, all six named years, the four countries displayed separately, and commodity 6305.32 aggregated as entered. Preserve the complete raw result table. For every observation, record year, partner, commodity description, first-unit quantity, unit label, suppression or revision markers, totals when shown, the query URL or saved specification, and UTC observation time. Record every query-builder selection, every default retained in steps 5–10, validation message, result order, export format, row count, and access failure so the grid can be reproduced. Verify the code description and reporting unit for each year against official HTS or DataWeb metadata. Record every suffix, description, unit, or comparability change without converting units. Using only comparable reported quantities, calculate country shares, year-over-year changes, six-year changes, and four-country totals. Show formulas and explain the handling of zero, missing, revised, and suppressed observations. Deliver the untouched raw export, tidy CSV, query specification, HTS and unit lineage table, formula-visible metrics workbook, two accessible trend charts, and a concise supplier-shift and limitations note. If the exact logged-out DataWeb query cannot be completed, provide a source-access report and preserve partial raw evidence instead of substituting another dataset or inventing the CSV.

rubric.name: Reproduce exact grid
rubric.requirement: While logged out, the exact query returns a grid for General Imports, HTS Items, General First Unit of Quantity, Actual values, Full Years, Annual, 2020–2025, India, China, Mexico, and Vietnam displayed separately, and commodity 6305.32 or 630532 aggregated as entered, with no unit conversion. The browsing record shows all four countries and six years through the site’s interface or its own endpoint; an equivalent row/column orientation is allowed. This criterion measures successful query completion, not whether a permitted access report was written.

rubric.name: Preserve grid values
rubric.requirement: Every reported observation matches the verified DataWeb grid for year, partner, commodity description, first-unit quantity, displayed unit label, suppression or revision markers, totals when shown, query URL or saved specification, and observation time. The code description and reporting unit are checked against official metadata for each year, and no unit or marker state is assumed in advance.

rubric.name: Preserve raw export
rubric.requirement: A server-produced output is retained exactly as received: the dataExport XLSX, its raw JSON envelope, or the raw runReport response body. A table reconstructed from the page does not count as the untouched raw export. If the exact query fails, preserve the raw evidence actually returned; a nonexistent export must not be invented or claimed as delivered.

rubric.name: Record every observation
rubric.requirement: The records include year, partner, commodity description, first-unit quantity, unit label, suppression or revision status, whether totals were shown, the full query payload or selection list, and a UTC observation time captured during the work. If the query fails, the partial record still includes the specification, time, and explicit N/A values for fields without results.

rubric.name: Log query reproduction
rubric.requirement: The log accurately records every query-builder selection, defaults retained in steps 5–10, every validation message, result order, export format, row count, and access failure. On the fallback path, it records attempted selections, observed defaults, validation messages, and all failures, with explicit N/A for result order, row count, and export format.

rubric.name: Verify annual lineage
rubric.requirement: Official annual HTS editions, tariff database files, or DataWeb metadata are retrieved for every year from 2020 through 2025. The lineage table records whether the suffix, description, unit, or comparability changed and supports the finding that none changed if that is what the sources show. No unit conversion occurs. If the exact query cannot be completed, the permitted access report states which annual checks were and were not performed instead of claiming an unsupported lineage table.

rubric.name: Calculate metrics correctly
rubric.requirement: Country shares, year-over-year changes, six-year changes, and four-country totals use only the retrieved grid values and match them within reasonable numeric tolerance. Formulas are visible, and the workbook states how it handles zeros, missing values, revisions, and suppression even if those cases do not occur. This check requires a successfully retrieved grid.

rubric.name: Provide required outputs
rubric.requirement: On the full path, the output location contains a tidy CSV with one country-year per row, a formula-visible metrics workbook, two trend charts with alt text or companion data, and a concise supplier-shift and limitations note. On the fallback path, it instead contains a source-access report and preserved partial raw evidence; empty templates are not required.

rubric.name: Report only supported results
rubric.requirement: The deliverables and final result make no unsupported claim about quantities, shares, trends, units, verification, or access. They contain no substitute dataset, fabricated or representative numbers, invented chart series or timestamps, unsupported annual verification, or unsupported claim that login is required. A directly observed sign-in gate may be described for that attempted path without claiming all public paths require login. Any statement that no data was fabricated must be true.

tasks.title: Price half-year Hertz rentals near Springfield, Illinois
tasks.instruction: My car will be off the road for months, and I want to compare Hertz's actual prices for a half-year rental from a neighborhood counter rather than an airport. Use ordinary web search and Hertz's public location pages to find all non-airport neighborhood and Local Edition counters within a six-hour drive of Springfield, Illinois 62704, excluding anything in or around Atlantic City, New Jersey. Search the whole area rather than stopping after a few branches. Combine duplicate street-address and Hertz-location-code records, but keep distinct counters in the same building separate. Type each verified street address into the pick-up field in Hertz.com's standard reservation search; do not select it from the map finder. Use a pick-up date fourteen days after the task starts and returns exactly six and eight months later. For each branch and duration, record the dates accepted, cheapest car class and cheapest SUV quoted, base rate, taxes and fees, total cost, and any mileage or long-term restrictions displayed. If the form rejects a rental that long, find and record the longest term it accepts, state the limit, and mark the six- or eight-month price as not quotable. Do not estimate it from a monthly rate. Record when you retrieved every quote. Keep conflicting prices from the location page and quote screen visible rather than averaging them, and write "not shown" for undisclosed figures. Rank every branch-duration-class combination that can be quoted. Name the cheapest overall and cheapest SUV, and flag caveats. Do not sign in, enter personal or payment details, hold a reservation, or book anything. Before discovery, declare a reproducible geographic and public-source search boundary covering the requested area, then document the results and observable endpoints within that boundary. Do not claim coverage outside it.

rubric.name: Initial branch set
rubric.requirement: The output has structured rows for every verified non-airport Hertz neighborhood or Local Edition branch within the stated six-hour boundary. Each row has branch name, street address, and the Hertz location code when published, supported by a Hertz source in the browsing record. An unpublished code is marked not shown, not invented. Airport and FBO counters are excluded.

rubric.name: Broad branch coverage
rubric.requirement: The record defines a reproducible geographic and public-source discovery boundary covering the requested area, then documents traversal of the relevant source results to their observable end. Every plausible counter discovered within that boundary is retained or has a supported exclusion. A small verified subset, a broad-search claim, or an unattempted area does not establish complete discovery. Evidence-backed partial coverage and blocks are recorded separately from complete-coverage credit.

rubric.name: Accurate branch records
rubric.requirement: Every address and location-code pair matches its cited source. Codes are not invented or inferred from map markers. Eligible rows exclude airport, FBO, and truck-only counters, although a truck counter may appear as a separate counter at the same location. Address-code pairs are not duplicated, distinct counters in one building remain separate, all entries fit a reasonable six-hour boundary, and none is in Atlantic City.

rubric.name: Correct quote process
rubric.requirement: Each branch with quote data was searched in Hertz.com's standard reservation form by typing its verified street address into the pick-up field and selecting autocomplete. Pick-up is fourteen days after research began, with returns exactly six and eight calendar months later. Code-based API requests and constructed vehicle-search URLs do not qualify.

rubric.name: First complete quotes
rubric.requirement: Both durations were attempted for every verified branch, with browsing support. Each attempt has either a results screen with the cheapest car and SUV data or a documented refusal and longest accepted return date. Accepted dates are recorded, and each quote has its retrieval time.

rubric.name: Duration limits documented
rubric.requirement: When a requested duration is rejected, the record establishes the longest term accepted by the form, records the accepted dates and evidence of the limit, and marks the requested six- or eight-month price as not quotable. It distinguishes a duration limit from a closed-day, unavailable-location, or technical error. If both durations are accepted, this conditional limit-finding requirement is not triggered.

rubric.name: Accurate quote details
rubric.requirement: Each car or SUV class, base rate, tax and fee amount, total, mileage term, and long-term restriction matches the visible quote for that branch, duration, and retrieval time. Undisclosed values say "not shown." Differing location-page and quote-screen prices stay visible, without averaging or silently choosing one.

rubric.name: Honest reporting
rubric.requirement: No prices, taxes, fees, or totals are estimated, extrapolated, or invented. Monthly rates are not multiplied, and regional taxes are not guessed. Duration limits match evidence; a closed-day failure is not called a term limit. Refused durations remain not quotable. Claims about typed addresses, branch searches, and saved files agree with the browsing record.

rubric.name: Complete price ranking
rubric.requirement: The ranking includes every quotable branch-duration-class combination recorded. It names the cheapest overall and cheapest SUV combinations and flags restrictions, changed dates, refusals, and other caveats. The ranking agrees with the reported figures.

rubric.name: No transaction actions
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in, personal or payment details, or submitted or confirmed reservation. Viewing quote, add-on, or checkout screens is allowed when none of those prohibited actions occurs.

tasks.title: List newly licensed San Diego businesses
tasks.instruction: I'm building an outreach list of newly licensed San Diego businesses and need all the underlying records, not a sample from a page. Start with the city open-data portal's business tax certificate dataset and find the structured source behind it, such as CSV, JSON, Socrata, or ArcGIS. Before showing records, state its endpoint, actual format, and the issue, application, effective, or equivalent start-date field you will use. Return every certificate dated 2026-05-15 through 2026-06-14 under that rule, continuing past pagination and row limits until all are covered. Give counts found, returned, and omitted, with reasons, and put later-dated rows under Future Effective Records. For every record, keep certificate and license numbers as literal text and include record ID, business, legal and DBA names, owner, business and mailing addresses, category, NAICS, all dates, and status. Add San Diego, CA, the dataset URL, and record type business_tax_certificate to every row. Use public searches to look up each returned business's phone, email, official site, Google profile with rating and review count, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Yelp, and owner name. Give a source URL for every added value and never use details from a similarly named business. Mark No only when a search found nothing and Unknown otherwise. Make names and addresses consistent, use YYYY-MM-DD dates, combine duplicates by certificate identity, and record when the search ran. State a weighting formula and score every lead from 1–100, favoring recent, active businesses with reachable contacts, limited web presence, and local trades, and lowering scores for expired, chain, or unreachable businesses. Give each lead an offer angle and a confidence of High, Medium, Low, or Unknown. Provide the complete CSV-ready table in batches or a file, a source summary, a top-25 shortlist, separate records of fields missing from the original source and still missing after searches, and a blockers log. If an export cannot be loaded, use the best public substitute and label it. Do not log in, purchase, submit anything other than public search or dataset queries, contact these businesses, or include individuals' personal details beyond the required public owner names.

rubric.name: Structured source identified
rubric.requirement: The result names every structured source actually downloaded, using its portal endpoint or a portal download link that resolves to it. It gives the actual format and states the date field and date-range rule before the records. A landing page alone is insufficient.

rubric.name: Complete date population
rubric.requirement: Every certificate meeting the stated date rule has a structured delivered row, with evidence of scans of complete source files. Reference counts are checked through full-file scans, allowing for changes between search dates. Samples, mock rows, and partial-file totals are incomplete. Any complete-source-file scan requirement in this item can instead be met by complete traversal of an allowed paginated API or endpoint, with reported totals or terminal-boundary evidence, continuation beyond row limits, and deduplication accounting. A capped or partial endpoint response is not complete traversal.

rubric.name: Counts and sections
rubric.requirement: Counts found, returned, and omitted agree with the date rule, delivered rows, and recorded source scans. Every omission category has a reason. Later-dated rows appear under Future Effective Records with the interpretation stated, or the result says none were found. Combining duplicates by certificate identity is stated, the duplicate count is given, and the search time is recorded.

rubric.name: Complete record fields
rubric.requirement: Each row has record ID; certificate and license identifiers; business, legal, and DBA names; owner; business and mailing addresses; category; NAICS; all source dates; and status. It also contains San Diego, CA, the dataset URL, and record_type business_tax_certificate. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Fields absent from the source remain as columns with explicit null or Unknown values.

rubric.name: Faithful source values
rubric.requirement: Government fields in every delivered row match the source, regardless of total coverage. This includes identifiers kept as literal text with exact digits, addresses, NAICS, status, and dates. Displayed addresses preserve the source city. Missing fields are marked: account_key is not silently renamed a certificate or license number, owner is not silently used as legal name, and no values are invented.

rubric.name: Top leads enriched
rubric.requirement: The top-25 shortlist comes from the returned records. Every shortlisted lead shows attempted research across all requested fields: phone, email, official site, Google profile with rating and review count, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Yelp, and owner name. Added values have adjacent source URLs, missing values use No or Unknown correctly, and the research record shows the searches.

rubric.name: Broad business research
rubric.requirement: Every business in the complete returned group has a documented public-source research attempt for the requested enrichment fields, or a documented access or identity gap. Sources, queries, and outcomes identify the business checked; missing fields remain explicit. A 100-business milestone may be reported as partial progress but does not replace full-group research-attempt coverage. Unattempted rows, a blanket unknown label without a search, and research limited to a shortlist do not satisfy full coverage.

rubric.name: Reliable enrichment
rubric.requirement: Every added value matches its cited source and the correct business. No information is borrowed from similarly named firms. Directory, social, or news pages are not called official sites, and phones, emails, or contact patterns are not malformed or guessed. No is used only after a documented empty search. This check does not apply if there are no added values and no No markers.

rubric.name: Supporting outputs delivered
rubric.requirement: The result provides a complete CSV-ready main table as a file or clearly divided complete batches, a source summary, a record of fields absent from the source, a record of fields still missing after searches, and a blockers or limitations log. Both missing-field records agree with the table and its Unknown and No values.

rubric.name: Truthful work claims
rubric.requirement: Claims about downloads, complete scans, date partitions, source checks, and searches match the saved evidence. Partial work and unknown values are described as limits, not completed research. No invented, mock, or missing rows are claimed as extracted records, and a business’s operating status is not called verified from an assumption. There is no login, purchase, non-search submission, or business contact. Public search and dataset queries are allowed. The only permitted personal information is the public owner names expressly requested; other individual contact details are excluded. Honest limitations are not fabrication, but do not make incomplete work complete.

rubric.name: Published lead scoring
rubric.requirement: Every returned lead has a score from 1–100 calculated using stated weights. Scores favor recency, active status, reachable contacts, limited web presence, and local trades, and penalize expired status, chains, and unreachable leads. Each lead has exactly one offer angle and one confidence value: High, Medium, Low, or Unknown.

tasks.title: Review Vision3K as a retail partner
tasks.instruction: We're considering Vision3K as a premium-eyewear retail partner and need an evidence-based review of how it presents and sells products, rather than a technical data scrape. Assess the homepage, main navigation, representative category pages showing multiple brands and a single brand, 20 product pages across at least four prominent brands, and public shipping, returns, warranty, help, and contact information. Before inspecting pages, define observable examples of what each score means for visual consistency, image quality, clarity of product information, ease of finding products and information, restraint in promotions, separation of brands, and storytelling. Score each sampled page on all seven criteria, giving short reasons, page links, and page-level evidence for every rating. Record the brands and product categories you find, how filters and stock messages are shown, and whether important policy claims are easy to find. Where the public catalogue allows, choose the 20 products across different prices, product types, stock states, and positions on brand pages. Trace five representative logged-out browsing paths from navigation or a category page to product and policy information, recording where each path is difficult. Compare Vision3K with official brand presentation materials and three established premium-eyewear retailers. Compare equivalent product-presentation and shopping features rather than requiring identical products, and use official brand material only for claims about brand presentation. Clearly distinguish direct observations from comparisons. Record and explain inconsistent prices, availability, or policies across pages. End with prioritized strengths, risks, and five concrete improvements, separating quick fixes from larger structural work. Attempt all 20 products, four brands, and three retailers. If a named Vision3K category, product, policy, brand, or comparison page shows no substantive content while logged out, report the smaller set you directly inspected and the exact access failures. Do not score uninspected pages, rely on snippets or empty page shells, or call fewer than 20 products, four brands, or three retailers a complete review. Provide a workbook with findings for each page, the scoring guide, a table comparing retailers and brand presentation, a map of browsing paths and difficulties, a disagreement log, and a prioritized product-presentation brief. Do not begin checkout, submit forms other than public product-search or filter controls, or contact the retailer.

rubric.name: Site sections covered
rubric.requirement: The report has linked observations supported by browsing evidence for the homepage, main navigation, at least one multi-brand category page, and at least one single-brand category page. It records encountered brands and product categories and explains how filters appear on an inspected category page.

rubric.name: Policies inspected
rubric.requirement: The report has linked, supported observations about public shipping or delivery, returns, warranty, help, and contact information wherever published. It explains whether key policy claims are easy to find. Warranty is handled according to available evidence. Quoted return windows, free-shipping thresholds, and contact details agree with the inspected pages.

rubric.name: Initial product sample
rubric.requirement: Every sampled Vision3K product page has a link and source-supported records of its displayed price and stock message. If an inspected page omits a field, the row identifies that field as not shown. An absent field does not exempt the whole row from evidence checking, and an empty or blocked page is not a completed product inspection.

rubric.name: Full product sample
rubric.requirement: The sample contains 20 distinct Vision3K product pages across at least four brands. Every row is supported and agrees with its source. Where the catalogue allows, the documented sample spans different price bands, product types, stock states, and positions on brand pages. Unsupported or contradicted rows are individually identified.

rubric.name: Consistent page scores
rubric.requirement: The scoring guide defines observable examples for each of the seven criteria. Every page described as scored has all seven scores, a short reason for each, and a page link. Factual statements in the reasons agree with browsing evidence. The chosen scores are accepted as the reviewer's reasoned judgments. The initial scoring guide is recorded before page assessment, with evidence of that ordering. The full inspected sample, not a self-selected scored subset, determines score completeness.

rubric.name: Supported comparisons
rubric.requirement: The comparison table covers Vision3K and three other retailers using equivalent product-presentation and shopping capabilities. Official brand material supports only brand-presentation claims. Every retailer and brand claim has support from an inspected page, and direct observations are distinguished from comparisons. Empty page shells, access-error pages, and simple availability indicators support only what they visibly show.

rubric.name: Five browsing paths traced
rubric.requirement: The browsing-path map includes five real logged-out paths that start in navigation or a category and continue to product and policy information. Each records its steps. Every reported difficulty links to pages shown in the browsing record.

rubric.name: Disagreements and improvements
rubric.requirement: The disagreement log addresses every price, availability, or policy inconsistency found in the report's own evidence. Prioritized strengths, risks and exactly five concrete improvements, separated into quick fixes and structural work, are reported.

rubric.name: Honest scope reporting
rubric.requirement: The report never presents an uninspected page as inspected or scored, claims outputs it has not delivered, or calls fewer than 20 products, four brands, three retailers, or five browsing paths a complete review. Each shortfall names the affected page and exact observed access failure.

rubric.name: Prohibited actions avoided
rubric.requirement: The complete browsing record shows no checkout started, no form submitted except public product-search or filter controls, and no retailer contact.

rubric.name: Reasonable review choices
rubric.requirement: The three comparison retailers are plausibly established premium-eyewear retailers, the chosen brands are plausibly prominent, and scoring examples describe observable features rather than defining a score using itself. The six requested outputs are recognizable in reasonable formats: workbook, scoring guide, comparison table, browsing-path difficulty map, disagreement log, and brief.

tasks.title: Find CAD laptops a Slovenian retailer stocks
tasks.instruction:
I’m choosing a CAD and 3D-modelling laptop for a small Slovenian studio and need to know what mimovrste.com currently stocks. Search the retailer’s own site for the exact queries "workstation laptop" and "prenosnik za CAD." Also use its laptop-category filters for NVIDIA graphics and at least 32 GB of memory. Traverse every results page or lazy-loaded batch to the end. Report each query’s hit count and listing boundary.

Keep every machine with at least 32 GB of installed RAM and a discrete NVIDIA GPU. For each, record the model designation exactly as the shop presents it, article code, CPU, installed RAM and upgrade headroom, storage, GPU and VRAM, screen size, resolution, any colour-gamut claim, weight, EUR price including struck-through or promotional amounts, VAT basis, verbatim stock or delivery wording, and product link. Write "absent" when the page omits a field rather than estimating it.

Merge duplicates by article code, not title. Keep near-identical ASUS ProArt P16, Lenovo ThinkPad P1 Gen 7, Dell Precision 5690, and HP ZBook Studio G11 configurations separate when their article codes differ. Document duplicates collapsed across searches.

Check every retained model’s GPU, memory ceiling, and display specification against an official manufacturer product or datasheet page. Show retailer and manufacturer values side by side when they disagree. State one local Slovenian observation time for price and stock. Log failed queries and pages and continue; an unreachable page does not show that a product is unavailable.

Finish with a ranking for viewport-heavy CAD work based on GPU class, memory headroom, colour accuracy, and price tier, plus a list of questions that require calling the store. Do not create an account, sign in, use the cart, order, or contact the retailer.

rubric.name: Both searches completed
rubric.requirement: For each exact retailer search, "workstation laptop" and "prenosnik za CAD," the result reports the captured hit count, what the results contained, and the pagination or lazy-load endpoint. These details match the browsing record. A first-screen review cannot be described as a full sweep.

rubric.name: Filtered catalogue completed
rubric.requirement: The retailer’s laptop category was filtered for NVIDIA graphics and at least 32 GB of memory, with the filter state stated. The full filtered set was traversed to its recorded endpoint. Every retained machine has at least 32 GB installed RAM and a discrete NVIDIA GPU in the retailer evidence; conflicting rows are flagged or excluded.

rubric.name: Article-code deduplication
rubric.requirement: One article-code key is applied consistently across the retained set. No two rows share that key, configurations with similar names remain separate when their codes differ, and duplicate listings collapsed across queries are documented.

rubric.name: Complete laptop records
rubric.requirement: Every retained row includes the exact retailer model designation, article code, CPU, installed RAM, upgrade headroom, storage, GPU and VRAM, panel size, resolution, colour-gamut claim, weight, EUR price and any crossed-out or promotional figure, VAT basis, verbatim stock or delivery wording, and the captured product-page link. Missing page fields say "absent," and all other values match captured retailer evidence.

rubric.name: Entire qualifying set
rubric.requirement: The delivered rows cover the complete qualifying population produced by the declared searches and category filters after every result page or lazy-loaded batch is traversed to the end. Every retained machine has at least 32 GB of installed RAM and a discrete NVIDIA GPU supported by the cited page. A shortlist, brand-only subset, or first-page sample is not complete coverage.

rubric.name: Complete vendor checking
rubric.requirement: For every retained machine, the record shows an official manufacturer product-page or datasheet check for GPU, memory ceiling, and display specification. Each requested field has a supported value or an explicit missing-information or failed-access outcome. Unattempted models do not satisfy check coverage, and a failed check is not labeled successful verification.

rubric.name: Supported vendor claims
rubric.requirement: Every manufacturer-attributed specification, correction, confirmation, PSREF statement, or access failure is backed by visible manufacturer-source evidence. Retailer and manufacturer disagreements are shown side by side instead of silently reconciled. Rows without a completed manufacturer check are marked unverified.

rubric.name: Honest stock reporting
rubric.requirement: The result states one Slovenian local read time consistent with the browsing record. Missing fields, including VAT details, are marked absent rather than estimated. Failed or unreachable searches and pages are logged as attempts and are not treated as proof that a model is not stocked. Completeness and verification claims do not exceed the evidence.

rubric.name: CAD suitability ranking
rubric.requirement: The ranking uses only the retained data and addresses GPU class, memory headroom, colour accuracy, and price tier for viewport-heavy CAD work. It also gives an explicit list of unresolved points that would require a call to the store.

rubric.name: No shopping actions
rubric.requirement: The browsing record contains no account creation, sign-in, cart, checkout, order, or retailer-contact action and no claim that one occurred. Adding products to a comparison widget is allowed, but clicking "V košarico" is not.

tasks.title: Build a GCSE History revision pack
tasks.instruction: I'm preparing a GCSE History revision and question-writing pack for the current AQA 8145 specification. Put together a clearly named collection of the current specification, exam structure and mark allocations, assessment objectives, option and route rules, and official teaching or assessment guidance needed to establish what can be assessed. List every publicly available official past paper, mark scheme, and examiner report from the five most recent completed exam series under the current specification, or all available series if there are fewer. For each paper and question family, record the component, option, wording pattern without unnecessarily reproducing protected text, mark value, assessment objectives, command words, expected evidence, mark-scheme features, and recurring mistakes identified by examiners. Give page or section citations. Explain changes in paper structure or guidance across series and keep current material separate from specimen papers, older specifications, and withdrawn documents. Use the evidence to show which specification areas and question formats are well covered and which are underrepresented. Write 24 original practice questions spread across the current papers and mark bands. For every source- or interpretation-based question, include usable original or properly attributed material for the student to work from. For each question, give brief answer-planning guidance and explain how it follows the official pattern without copying it. Provide the official reference collection, a workbook connecting specification content to assessment, a table of examiner evidence, the coverage map, and the original 24-question practice pack. If you cannot create files, provide the same information in structured form.

rubric.name: Official reference collection
rubric.requirement: Only outputs identified as the reference collection count here. They contain or link official AQA material covering the current specification, exam structure and marks, assessment objectives, option and route rules, and relevant teaching or assessment guidance. Retrieval or official catalogue-link evidence is visible for the required materials; no fixed minimum number of distinct documents is imposed. A qualifying guidance document is named with its AQA URL and was retrieved or visibly linked from a retrieved AQA page. Statements do not contradict established hours, marks, SPaG placement, AO percentages, question families, option titles or codes, or the rule requiring one option from each section. Availability claims are checked with the inventory.

rubric.name: Correct series window
rubric.requirement: The analysis uses the five most recent completed exam series under the current specification at the observation date, or all available completed series if fewer than five are publicly listed. Official AQA catalogue evidence identifies them. Specimen, older-specification, and withdrawn materials remain outside that window.

rubric.name: Complete document inventory
rubric.requirement: The inventory includes one record for every publicly catalogued paper, mark scheme, and examiner report in the five-series window, including every question-paper and mark-scheme variant exposed by the official catalogue. Each gives series, component or option identity, document type, and URL or equivalent catalogue identifier. The official listing process is visible. Missing document types are established from the checked catalogue, not an old fixed count. Component templates with substitution notes and silent omissions are insufficient.

rubric.name: All question families
rubric.requirement: For each in-scope paper and its question families, identified from official specification and paper evidence, the workbook or table gives component, option scope, wording pattern, marks, assessment objectives, command words, expected evidence, and mark-scheme features. These agree with the specification and come from retrieved specifications, papers, and mark schemes with page or section citations. Generic unsupported templates are insufficient.

rubric.name: Examiner findings supported
rubric.requirement: Recurring mistakes are grouped by question family or paper and come from retrieved and inspected examiner reports within the window. Each finding names its report and page or section. Findings are not attributed to unread reports, page references are not invented, and standard boilerplate is not called an examiner finding. Fewer reports may be used if that limited scope is stated.

rubric.name: Materials clearly separated
rubric.requirement: Changes in paper structure or guidance across the studied series are explained using inspected evidence. Current material is separate from Sample sets, older-specification or legacy material identified by official evidence, and withdrawn or superseded documents. Specimen material is outside the five-series window, and distinct official series are not combined.

rubric.name: Meaningful coverage map
rubric.requirement: The coverage map uses inventoried and inspected evidence to show well-represented and underrepresented specification areas, including option parts, and question formats. Coverage calculations use suitable totals as their basis. A table that only counts resource records by option is insufficient.

rubric.name: Original practice questions
rubric.requirement: The pack has exactly 24 original questions spread across the current papers and mark bands established from the retrieved official materials. Every question has short planning guidance and an explanation of how it follows the official pattern without copying it. Retrieved specifications and mark schemes allow this to be checked. Fewer questions, concentrating on one paper, or copying questions is insufficient.

rubric.name: Usable source material
rubric.requirement: Every source- or interpretation-based practice question includes material the student can actually use. This material is original or properly attributed. Telling a teacher to find or supply a source later is insufficient.

rubric.name: Honest research record
rubric.requirement: Claims in delivered files and the final response about retrieval, inventory scope, examiner findings, citations, and completion have cited official support; interim notes do not count. There are no unsupported retrieval claims or findings and citations attributed to documents whose contents were not established. Official values, such as historic-environment lists or appearances by series, are not invented beyond retrieved text. Complete coverage is not claimed while standard catalogue records are silently missing. Calculations from retrieved data are allowed. Misclassified content from genuinely extracted documents belongs to its content check; modified or large-print omissions belong to inventory completeness. Honest limitations, timeouts, labeled partial work, rounding, summary wording, and harmless descriptions of extraction methods do not fail this check.

tasks.title: Collect Hunter Health plans for an ACT quote
tasks.instruction: I need the plans shown by Hunter Health Insurance's public quote flow for a generic applicant in ACT. Open https://hunterhi.com.au/start and select ACT, under 30, and Single cover. Continue only where the flow accepts generic choices without identity or contact information. Record every selected input, the displayed income label, quote state, result count, displayed order, and observation time. For each plan shown, record provider, product, hospital or extras type and tier, premium and payment frequency, excess, co-payment, included, restricted and excluded services, waiting periods, rebate or loading basis, promotions, and public product or quote link. Use “not shown” for fields absent from the quote flow, and keep quote values separate from public product-document values. Record every consent, contact, identity, membership, login, application, or submission boundary encountered. If Hunter results are missing, explain the shortfall instead of replacing them with government comparison results. Where a current public product summary or insurer document is available, check each plan's tier, excess, clinical categories, waiting periods, and eligibility against it, keeping conflicts visible. Compare the displayed plans by premium basis, hospital tier, excess, restrictions, waiting periods, and missing fields, using visible formulas or a table of values. Treat the generic quote as nonbinding and give no personal advice. Provide the complete Hunter result list, selected-input record, a table matching quotes to product documents, conflict and access log, comparison with visible formulas or values, and a short plan brief. Do not enter a name, birth date, email, phone number, Medicare information, address, payment data, or other identifying information. Do not request contact, submit an application, sign in, or buy cover.

rubric.name: Inputs accurately recorded
rubric.requirement: The selected-input record matches the logged-out browsing evidence: ACT, under 30, Single cover, and the result-page state actually read, including displayed income label, premium frequency, and excess. It records the observation time and does not describe another applicant profile.

rubric.name: Complete Hunter results
rubric.requirement: The result list includes every Hunter plan displayed for the recorded inputs, in displayed order with the observed count. Each plan records the requested product type, tier, premium, frequency, excess, co-payment, service coverage, waiting periods, rebate or loading basis, promotion, and public link when shown. Optional states are labeled. Missing Hunter results are not replaced by a government comparison group, and no outcome is assumed beforehand.

rubric.name: Faithful quote values
rubric.requirement: Every recorded quote value matches visible evidence, including premium and frequency, rebate or loading basis for each price, excess, displayed income label, clinical-category status, and promotions when shown. If two price displays are observed, both remain separate with their stated bases.

rubric.name: All quote fields
