rubric.requirement: Every result entry has provider, product, type and tier, premium and frequency, excess, co-payment, included, restricted and excluded services, waiting periods, rebate or loading basis, promotion, and public link. Quote omissions are explicitly marked "not shown". All requested columns are present, and document values are not placed in quote columns.

rubric.name: Product document matching table
rubric.requirement: Each displayed product is checked against a current public product summary or insurer document with extracted evidence, or has a documented search or failed-access attempt and is explicitly marked no document found. Quote and document values stay separate. Document details include all shown waiting periods, tier, excess, clinical categories, and eligibility. Conflicts stay visible.

rubric.name: Supported observation times
rubric.requirement: Every exact timestamp has browsing evidence for the specific quote state it describes. Clearly labeled broader time windows are acceptable. The result does not invent timestamp precision or reuse one state's time for another.

rubric.name: Boundaries and conflicts
rubric.requirement: The log records each boundary encountered and the action taken, including any start-page consent notice, Send-my-quote contact modal, Apply identity page, Member Login, or callback prompt shown. It keeps any income-label conflict when both relevant pages were visited and any conflicting price displays when both were seen.

rubric.name: Transparent plan comparison
rubric.requirement: The comparison covers premium basis, hospital tier, excess, restrictions, waiting periods, and missing fields using only result-list or cited-document values. Each premium is labeled gross, rebated, or another stated basis. Different price displays are not mixed without labeling both. Missingness either names each plan's absent fields or gives a correct count using a field set defined in the same output. Tier, excess, restrictions, and waiting periods appear in formulas, defined counts, or a table of values; prose alone is insufficient. This check assesses coverage, stated price bases, and internal consistency. A3–A5 assess source accuracy.

rubric.name: Consistent nonbinding brief
rubric.requirement: The complete result list, selected-input record, quote-to-document table, conflict and access log, comparison, and short brief are all present. The brief agrees with the results and comparison. It does not claim a difference between plans that the data contradicts or omit a significant recorded difference from an absolute statement. It explicitly treats the quote as nonbinding and makes no personal recommendation.

rubric.name: Privacy boundaries respected
rubric.requirement: No name, birth date, email, phone number, Medicare information, payment details, address, or other identifying value is entered. No application is submitted, and no quote-email request, callback booking, sign-in, or purchase is initiated. Viewing boundary pages without submitting is allowed.

tasks.title: Cost out AquaTru water purifiers
tasks.instruction: I'm comparing countertop water purifiers and want to understand AquaTru's full ownership cost before choosing a model. Build a spreadsheet of every current purifier, bundle, filter, accessory, and replacement part in AquaTru's public U.S. catalogue. Include model compatibility, capacity, filtration claims, certifications, list and sale prices, subscription options, shipping terms, warranty, and product link. Use the published filter-replacement schedule to calculate filter costs for years one through five for each purifier. Clearly separate assumptions from published facts, and do not make health claims beyond what the certification evidence supports. For comparison, choose one currently sold countertop reverse-osmosis system from each of five different established brands. Choose the closest products in form and rated capacity to AquaTru's base countertop model; break ties by lower public list price and then brand name. Collect the same information for competitors and put capacity and ownership costs on a comparable basis where possible. For every AquaTru purifier and retained competitor, model filter-replacement timing, dependence on subscriptions, published capacity, warranty period, and how costs change with household water use. Check contaminant-reduction claims for each individual model and filter against its applicable public certification listing. Do not assume one product's certification applies to the whole brand. Make a table linking purifiers, bundles, compatible filters, and replacement parts so components are not counted twice. Flag bundles that repeat separately listed components and promotions requiring a subscription or code. Report gaps in public catalogue, certification, or competitor information rather than guessing missing products or claims. State your criteria for comparing total cost over time, independently certified contaminant-reduction coverage, space required, and capacity. Provide the AquaTru catalogue and compatibility workbook, a table of certification claims and evidence, a five-year ownership-cost model with visible formulas covering purchase price, filter costs, and other applicable ownership costs, and recommendations for low total cost, strongest documented certification coverage, compact size, and high throughput. Include observation dates. Do not subscribe, enter a promo code, or purchase anything.

rubric.name: Complete AquaTru catalogue
rubric.requirement: The structured catalogue includes every item shown in the dated public U.S. catalogue collection: purifiers, bundles, filters, accessories, and replacement parts. Every row has a link. No product is invented.

rubric.name: Accurate AquaTru details
rubric.requirement: For each catalogue row, model compatibility, capacity, filtration claims, certifications, list and sale prices, subscription options, shipping terms, warranty, and product link agree with cited public evidence. Unsupported fields remain gaps. Assumptions are separate from published facts, and health claims stay within the certification evidence.

rubric.name: Five-year cost model
rubric.requirement: An ownership-cost model with visible formulas includes purchase price, filter costs, and other applicable ownership costs for years one through five for every AquaTru purifier retained from the complete current catalogue. It uses each model's published replacement schedule and states whether replacements depend on time, water capacity based on stated household use, or whichever comes first. It shows how household use affects the result and labels every assumption and unsupported input.

rubric.name: Certification checked per model
rubric.requirement: For each AquaTru model and filter and each retained competitor, certification and contaminant-reduction claims are checked against the applicable public certification listing. Product performance sheets may provide supporting detail, but do not replace independently verified certification coverage. The record links the exact model or filter to its evidence, distinguishes manufacturer claims from independently confirmed claims, and records missing evidence as a gap. A listing for one product does not establish certification for the whole brand.

rubric.name: Competitors from five brands
rubric.requirement: The comparison has one currently sold countertop reverse-osmosis system from each of five different established brands other than AquaTru, with evidence each is currently sold. The selection rules for form, rated capacity, list price, and brand name are stated and applied to the documented eligible products. Proof that the choices are the best possible worldwide is not required. Fewer than five is an explicitly labeled, evidence-supported shortfall, not completion of the five-brand requirement.

rubric.name: Accurate competitor details
rubric.requirement: For each retained competitor, even if fewer than five were included, the report gives the same fields as AquaTru plus replacement timing, subscription dependence, published capacity, warranty, and comparable capacity and year-one-through-five ownership-cost figures with visible formulas for purchase, filters, and other applicable costs. The model shows how household water use affects replacement timing and cost. Each value has cited evidence or is clearly labeled as an assumption or gap.

rubric.name: Components linked without double-counting
rubric.requirement: The component table links every purifier to compatible filters, parts, and bundles. It flags combination packs or other bundles that repeat separately listed components and identifies promotions requiring a subscription or code. The ownership model never counts a component both in a bundle and as a separate item.

rubric.name: Four clear recommendations
rubric.requirement: The result states clear criteria for total cost over time, independently certified contaminant-reduction coverage, space required, and capacity. It provides all four recommendations: lowest cumulative cost, strongest documented certification coverage, compact footprint, and high throughput. Each follows from the report's own data.

rubric.name: Assumptions and missing information
rubric.requirement: All outputs distinguish assumptions from published facts. Missing catalogue, certification, and competitor information is reported as a gap rather than guessed. Health claims do not exceed cited certification evidence. Failed source lookups are not described as verification.

rubric.name: Dates and action limits
rubric.requirement: The data has observation dates by output or source; a date on every row is not required. No subscription, promo or discount code entry, or purchase occurs. Cart previews and shipping calculators without checkout are allowed.

tasks.title: Build a directory of U.S. public retirement agencies
tasks.instruction:
I’m building a verified directory of U.S. public retirement agencies from the Public Plans Data retirement-system list. Capture every displayed record in the complete public source list before deduplication. Preserve the source identifier, displayed system name, public profile URL, state or national scope, and every plan or agency relationship exposed by the source.

Treat administrative agencies, retirement systems, and individual plans as distinct but related entities. Preserve mergers, renames, closures, parent-child uncertainty, and the row counts before and after resolution. For every resolved agency, record the official entity name, government level, jurisdiction, stated plan types and covered populations, verified official website, and the evidence connecting that first-party site to the source record.

When the source provides membership or asset figures, retain the value, unit, population definition, as-of date, and profile link. Do not describe an undated or older value as current. Record redirects, inaccessible sites, conflicting official-site evidence, missing fields, and limitations in the source list. Do not claim that the result covers every U.S. public plan.

Summarize agency and plan counts and disclosed assets by government level and state only when definitions and dates are compatible. Identify states with multiple independently administered systems. Deliver the complete pre-deduplication source capture, agency-plan relationship table, official-site verification table, status-change and conflict log, summary workbook, and coverage-methodology note. Do not collect staff contacts or member information, sign in, or contact any agency.

rubric.name: Complete source capture
rubric.requirement: The delivered pre-deduplication capture contains every retirement-system record displayed at collection time as structured entries. Every row includes system_id, displayed system name, public profile URL, and state or national scope.

rubric.name: Faithful source capture
rubric.requirement: Every captured identifier, name, and profile URL matches the displayed source. No row is invented or accidentally repeated during capture. If the source itself repeats a record, retain that raw occurrence and identify it during the separate duplicate-resolution step.

rubric.name: Complete agency resolution
rubric.requirement: The relationship table treats agencies, retirement systems, and plans as distinct related entities. Every captured system is connected to all relationships exposed by the source. Each resolved agency includes official name, government level, jurisdiction, and any source-stated plan types or covered populations. Raw and resolved row counts are stated. Unresolved identities remain explicitly unresolved with their evidence and attempted checks; they are not silently copied as confirmed agencies. Genuine missing fields do not require invented values.

rubric.name: Accurate entity relationships
rubric.requirement: Every value in the resolved layers has source support. No system or plan is attached to another jurisdiction’s agency or domain, and null or orphan records are not filled by inference. Mergers, renames, and closures appear only when shown by the source or cited first-party evidence and are attached to the correct records.

rubric.name: Reliable site verification
rubric.requirement: No website is marked verified without first-party evidence connecting it to the correct entity. Generic parent-government portals are not enough by themselves, blank URLs cannot be verified, and stated verification totals agree with the table’s rows.

rubric.name: Official-site coverage for every agency
rubric.requirement: Every resolved agency receives a documented status such as verified, redirected, inaccessible, conflicting, or missing. The official-site verification table shows the underlying website checks and evidence for those statuses.

rubric.name: All agencies checked
rubric.requirement: Every resolved agency receives a documented verification or access status supported by a probe. The delivered status-change and conflict log records all resulting redirects, inaccessible sites, official-site conflicts, and missing fields.

rubric.name: Figures fully dated
rubric.requirement: Every reported membership or asset figure includes its value, unit, population definition, fiscal-year or other as-of date, and profile link. If the source omits a date or definition, record it as not given. No undated figure or older figure is presented as current.

rubric.name: Summary and methodology
rubric.requirement: The summary workbook reports agency and plan counts and disclosed assets by government level and state, combining values only when their definitions and dates are compatible. It also identifies states with multiple independently administered systems. A coverage-methodology note clearly explains the limitations of the Public Plans Data source list.

rubric.name: Honesty and privacy
rubric.requirement: The result never claims to contain every U.S. public plan or claims completeness or verification contradicted by its own evidence. No staff contact details or member information are collected, no account is accessed, and no agency is contacted.

tasks.title: Get a Huawei trade-in price
tasks.instruction: My Huawei P40 Pro is spotless and fully working, and I want to know what Huawei's own store would pay before I use a buyback site. Use Huawei's official worldwide storefront list and try every country storefront reachable while logged out, checking its trade-in estimator. Quote the P40 Pro at the best condition grade offered for every storage tier and every variant the device picker distinguishes, rather than stopping at the first result. For each quote, record the storefront, currency, exact listed model, Huawei's name for the condition grade, base value, any bonus and what qualifies for it, whether payment is cash or store credit toward a new phone, stated validity, and observation time. Check each quote against that estimator's terms, FAQ, and partner disclosures. Cover condition definitions, functional checks, device-lock and IMEI requirements, return shipping, and rights to change the valuation after inspection. Keep disagreements between the calculator and written terms visible. Mark information the pages do not state as unstated; do not borrow terms from another market. Convert values to one currency using a single published exchange-rate table, naming its source and date, and identify storefronts that send trade-ins to a named third-party recycler. Rank only storefronts with captured quotes to show which pay best for an excellent-condition P40 Pro after considering bonuses, cash versus credit restrictions, and revaluation risk. Explain whether Huawei's trade-in route is worthwhile. Provide a workbook with every quote, a record of quote-versus-terms conflicts, and a log of every storefront tried, including those hiding or blocking the tool. Record access barriers and leave those values undetermined; an inaccessible page reveals nothing about its prices. Do not sign in, submit an IMEI, serial number, address, or contact details, start a trade-in, or buy anything.

rubric.name: Three complete outputs
rubric.requirement: Three distinct structured outputs exist: quote workbook, quote-versus-terms conflict record, and storefront-attempt log. Each quote gives storefront, currency, exact model, grade, base value, bonus and trigger, cash or credit status, validity, and observation time, using unstated, undetermined, or null where appropriate. Each attempt gives storefront and outcome or barrier. An empty quote or conflict table includes the required columns and an evidence-supported explanation; it does not imply that untested markets have no offers.

rubric.name: Storefront access attempts
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows a source listing storefronts, such as Huawei's worldwide selector or sitemap, and actual access attempts for every country storefront reachable while logged out. Each tested storefront and its outcome appear in the attempt log.

rubric.name: Every storefront checked
rubric.requirement: Every storefront in that source has a logged outcome or barrier supported by evidence. Listing a storefront as untried does not count as trying it.

rubric.name: Accurate quote fields
rubric.requirement: Each quote has visible estimator evidence. Currency, amounts, model label, condition-grade name, base and bonus treatment, payment form, validity, and observation time match the source or are marked unstated.

rubric.name: All picker variants
rubric.requirement: At every storefront with a working picker, every P40 Pro variant and storage tier is quoted at the best offered grade, or the barrier to that option is recorded. Stopping at one tier or skipping the best grade without a barrier is insufficient.

rubric.name: Terms fully checked
rubric.requirement: For each storefront with a captured quote, the output records findings from that market's terms, FAQ, and partner disclosures where publicly available, with documented attempts or gaps for each source type. It covers condition definitions, functional checks, device-lock or IMEI requirements, return shipping, and revaluation after inspection. Genuinely missing points are marked unstated. The terms record also identifies any market-specific third-party recycler or partner, its role, and the source naming it, or a documented “unstated” marker when inspected sources do not identify one.

rubric.name: Accurate terms conflicts
rubric.requirement: Every terms statement and conflict entry matches extracted content from the correct storefront. Conflicts show both the calculator's claim and the written clause. Unstated is used only when inspected material omits the point. Terms are never borrowed from another market.

rubric.name: Consistent currency conversion
rubric.requirement: All currency conversions use one published exchange-rate table, with its source and date named. Calculations are correct within the allowed rounding tolerance. Naming a source such as IMF or OANDA without visiting it is insufficient.

rubric.name: Grounded ranking and verdict
rubric.requirement: Only storefronts with captured quotes are ranked. The output gives a clear judgment on whether the route is worthwhile, considering bonuses, cash-versus-credit limits, and revaluation risk from recorded quotes and terms. Undetermined values are not ranked.

rubric.name: No sensitive submissions
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows no sign-in or submission of an IMEI, serial number, address, or contact information. No trade-in order is started and nothing is purchased.

rubric.name: Honest storefront coverage
rubric.requirement: Every coverage and status claim agrees with the browsing record. The work does not claim more storefronts or locales checked than documented, count seeing a search result as a storefront visit, assign zero value or no offer to an unreached tool, falsely claim no submission happened, or claim unsupported completion.

tasks.title: Reconcile Root, Inc. financials, 2022 to 2025
tasks.instruction: I need to compare and reconcile Root, Inc.'s financial reporting for fiscal years 2022 through 2025 using SEC EDGAR filings and first-party annual reports. List every 10-K and amended 10-K in fiscal-year and filing-date order. Record accession number, filing date, reporting period, form, SEC document link, first-party report link when available, and reported revenue, net income or loss, total assets, and cash and cash equivalents, with units and exact page citations. Keep restatements, corrections, amendments, missing first-party reports, and conflicting values visible rather than silently choosing one. Use SEC filings as the main evidence, record when you checked the information, and do not replace filed figures with investor-relations summaries. For every year, trace each figure through the main financial statements, relevant notes, and SEC inline-XBRL facts. Record the exact concept, period, unit, scale or decimals, and page, fact link, or context identifier. Show which filings amend earlier ones and distinguish an amended document from a restated value. If annual-report presentation differs from EDGAR, keep both versions and explain whether the difference concerns format, rounding, taxonomy, period, or substance. Calculate year-over-year changes only after reconciling the bases of the reported figures. Provide a filing and amendment list, a financial workbook with page citations, a record matching XBRL tags and values to the statements, a table explaining year-over-year changes, and a short report on filing quality naming every unresolved conflict.

rubric.name: Complete filing index
rubric.requirement: The filing and amendment list includes every in-scope 10-K, each with correct accession number, filing date, reporting period, form, and working SEC link to that filing. The result states whether any 10-K/A exists, supported by a visible SEC form check.

rubric.name: First-party reports linked
rubric.requirement: For each fiscal year from 2022–2025, the result provides a first-party annual-report link found during research when available, or records where it searched and marks the report missing. An investor-relations static-file PDF or EDGAR ARS document is acceptable. Shareholder letters and investor-relations summaries are not substitutes.

rubric.name: Complete financial workbook
rubric.requirement: The workbook contains all 16 year-and-metric records: revenue, net income or loss, total assets, and cash and cash equivalents for FY2022–FY2025. Each structured record has a value, unit or scale, and specific page citation for that figure. Prose summaries and general citations do not replace those records.

rubric.name: Faithful financial values
rubric.requirement: Every financial value, metric, unit, scale, and page citation in the workbook or final answer matches the filed document. Each cited page contains the stated figure. This applies to all delivered entries even if fewer than all 16 are present.

rubric.name: Exact XBRL reconciliation
rubric.requirement: The XBRL record covers all 16 year-and-metric pairs. Each gives the exact concept, duration or instant period, unit, scale or decimals, and fact link or context identifier, and connects the fact to the reported value. SEC filing or API extraction supports each entry. For each year and metric, the record also traces the figure to the main statement and relevant notes, with citations, or explains why no note adds relevant detail. No placeholder contexts, invented anchors, wrong concepts, quarterly facts labeled annual, or conflicting scale details are included.

rubric.name: Correct correction lineage
rubric.requirement: The filing history shows every observed amendment relationship for in-scope annual filings and distinguishes an amended document from a restated or corrected value. Restatements, corrections, missing first-party reports, and conflicts remain visible with sources. No fixed count of originals or amendments is assumed.

rubric.name: Accurate yearly bridge
rubric.requirement: The year-over-year table gives changes in revenue, net income or loss, total assets, and cash and cash equivalents for FY2022→2023, FY2023→2024, and FY2024→2025. Calculations use the reconciled reported bases correctly and explicitly handle any transition from loss to income when it occurs.

rubric.name: Conflicts clearly named
rubric.requirement: A filing-quality brief is delivered. It names every unresolved conflict or retained pair of differing values appearing elsewhere and does not say there are no conflicts when another output records one. For every available first-party annual report, differences from EDGAR are compared and classified as format, rounding, taxonomy, period, or substance where the evidence permits; unresolved differences remain named. The results include an explicit retrieval or check date.

rubric.name: Honest verification claims
rubric.requirement: The outputs and final answer do not claim comparisons or checks absent from the research record. They do not say first-party figures match without opening a first-party report or claim every figure was traced through notes and inline XBRL without those extractions. Honest limitations in extracting an applicable first-party report are acceptable. A4 and A5 assess numeric accuracy; A1 and A6 assess specific filing and correction claims.

rubric.name: Clear presentation
rubric.requirement: The filing list consistently uses one direction for fiscal-year and filing-date ordering. Outputs are clearly named and recognizable, units are understandable, and citations use a consistent usable format. This check assesses presentation, not the financial content.

tasks.title: Choose a used 2022 Toyota RAV4 trim
tasks.instruction: I'm considering a used 2022 Toyota RAV4 and want to know which trim suits different ownership needs and what to inspect on a particular vehicle. Build a workbook of every U.S.-market trim from Toyota's official specifications. Keep gasoline, hybrid, and plug-in-hybrid variants separate. Record body style, seating, doors, powertrain, fuel type, drivetrain, official fuel economy, cargo space, towing capacity, wheel and tire details, ground clearance, and major standard or optional features. Add J.D. Power's currently published overall, quality and reliability, driving-experience, and resale scores, with the rating year and methodology. Do not assign scores for the whole model to individual trims. Compare NHTSA and IIHS safety results according to the exact configuration tested. List every NHTSA recall campaign applicable to the model year, including component, consequence, remedy, and the build dates or configurations affected. Compare current used-price and retained-value ranges from two established valuation sources by trim and mileage band where publicly available. Keep each source's condition assumptions and dates. Use explicit weights to recommend trims for value, fuel economy, winter driving, and towing, then show how the choice changes when purchase price, drivetrain, or towing need takes priority. Provide the complete trim workbook, a safety and recall record, a valuation-range table, and a short report covering the four ownership uses with an inspection checklist for an individual vehicle. Use structured tables if files cannot be created.

rubric.name: Complete trim list
rubric.requirement: The workbook includes every U.S.-market model-year 2022 Toyota RAV4 trim identified by Toyota's official sources. Each has the correct powertrain category and drivetrain. No trim from another model year is added.

rubric.name: Complete trim details
rubric.requirement: Every row includes body style, seating, doors, powertrain, fuel type, drivetrain, official fuel economy, cargo space, towing, wheel and tire details, ground clearance, and major features. Standard and optional features are clearly distinguished.

rubric.name: Accurate specifications
rubric.requirement: Each recorded specification, including fuel economy, agrees with the cited official source for that value. Toyota's official specifications establish the requested vehicle details. Figures for different drivetrains remain separate. Every value other than null has source evidence.

rubric.name: J.D. Power scores
rubric.requirement: The report gives the currently published J.D. Power overall, quality and reliability, driving-experience, and resale scores as model-level values, with rating year and methodology. It does not assign a model-level score to a particular trim.

rubric.name: Safety results compared correctly
rubric.requirement: NHTSA and IIHS results are organized by the configuration tested. NHTSA configurations and ratings cover each RAV4 and RAV4 Prime configuration. IIHS results distinguish the RAV4 and RAV4 Prime pages and report each page's tested configurations, and stated applicability. All values agree with saved source content. A configuration without published test results is marked unavailable or not tested; the comparison does not invent a rating or require an unpublished test.

rubric.name: Complete recall list
rubric.requirement: The recall record includes every applicable NHTSA campaign for gasoline, hybrid, and Prime models, with complete and correct model applicability. Each has component, consequence, remedy, affected build dates or configurations, and correct model applicability supported by sources, with unpublished details explicitly marked. No campaign is invented or attributed to the wrong model.

rubric.name: Values from two sources
rubric.requirement: The valuation table compares used-price and retained-value ranges where publicly available from two established sources, by trim and by mileage band where the source publishes one. Every number has source support. Each source's condition assumptions and valuation date are kept. Unavailable values remain unavailable instead of being filled in.

rubric.name: Recommendations can be recalculated
rubric.requirement: The four recommendations cover value, fuel economy, winter driving, and towing. They include explicit weights, scoring inputs for each trim, and a method that lets the winners be recalculated. Three sensitivity cases show what happens when purchase price, drivetrain, or towing need takes priority. The particular choice of weights is not scored.

rubric.name: All required outputs
rubric.requirement: All four outputs are present as files or structured tables: the trim workbook, safety-and-recall record, valuation-range table, and short report on the four ownership uses. The report includes an inspection checklist for an individual vehicle. This check covers presence and organization; other checks assess content.

rubric.name: Honest source reporting
rubric.requirement: The outputs and final response claim only what the browsing record supports. Failed or missing source collections are not called complete or verified. Unsupported facts are not labeled confirmed or verified.

tasks.title: Map FernUniversität teacher-exam options
tasks.instruction: I’m considering a distance-learning route to a German Erstes Staatsexamen and want to know exactly what FernUniversität in Hagen currently offers. Use only FernUniversität’s official public site to define the core population. Identify every current program explicitly leading to an Erstes Staatsexamen, and preserve the exact program title, field, degree outcome, study modes, official listing URL, and evidence that the catalogue search is complete. For every match, record admission requirements, enrollment periods, standard duration, required in-person components, curriculum phases, examination structure, fees, applicable regulations, document dates, and transition rules. Clearly distinguish program-specific fields from student-dependent ones. Reconcile the A-to-Z catalogue, degree filters, faculty pages, admissions information, examination regulations, and state-examination materials. Keep an exclusion record for bachelor’s, master’s, certificate, preparatory, and near-match programs, explaining why each does not qualify. Compare the verified pathway with official state-examination requirements. Also compare it with up to three German public universities, but only when they offer a materially comparable flexible or part-time route under a criterion published before selection. Present prerequisite, enrollment, study, attendance, examination, federal-state, and prior-education dependencies as a staged pathway. Separate general requirements from conditional ones and list unresolved public-information questions. Deliver the complete program register, requirement-to-regulation matrix, exclusion table, comparator table, dependency-aware timeline, and unresolved-question brief. Do not apply, enroll, contact a university, submit forms other than public catalogue and search controls, infer a particular person’s eligibility, or replace official evidence with third-party program claims.

rubric.name: Correct program identity
rubric.requirement: The register identifies every current qualifying program found on FernUniversität’s official pages. Its entry contains the exact official program title, field, state-examination degree outcome as shown by the source, study modes, and an official fernuni-hagen.de listing URL that the browsing record shows was visited.

rubric.name: Complete catalogue search
rubric.requirement: The deliverable and browsing record show a complete catalogue search. They enumerate the catalogue’s degree-type categories and relevant state-examination category pages, then use the displayed contents to determine which programs qualify without assuming the population in advance. Search snippets or unsupported review counts are insufficient.

rubric.name: Complete program details
rubric.requirement: The register addresses admission requirements, enrollment periods, standard duration, fees, study modes, in-person requirements, and curriculum phases. Every reported value is supported by an official page or document authorized by the task and shown as read. Unknown values remain explicit, and precise values are not supplied without evidence.

rubric.name: Supported regulation matrix
rubric.requirement: The matrix connects requirements to named regulations and document dates. It covers the applicable FernUniversität regulations and official state-examination requirements established by the retrieved sources. Claims about paragraphs, examination counts or weights, transition rules, and dates are supported by opened text. A relevant official page may support stated preconditions; an unopened PDF cannot support paragraph contents.

rubric.name: Complete exclusion table
rubric.requirement: The exclusion table addresses all five requested categories: bachelor’s, master’s, certificate, preparatory or Akademiestudium, and near-match programs. Every entry names a program shown on a FernUniversität source and explains why it does not qualify. It does not use invented or malformed URLs or present programs from another domain as FernUniversität offerings.

rubric.name: Valid comparator group
rubric.requirement: The comparator table states its comparability criterion before selection and contains zero to three German public universities. Each included university is supported by its own official pages as offering a materially comparable flexible or part-time route matching the verified FernUniversität pathway, with a direct comparison to FernUniversität. An honestly empty table passes when the screening is documented; snippets do not establish a verified comparator.

rubric.name: Dependency-aware pathway
rubric.requirement: A staged pathway covers prerequisite, enrollment, study, attendance, examination, federal-state, and prior-education dependencies. It distinguishes general requirements from conditional ones. Every substantive stage is supported by the browsing record or explicitly marked unresolved.

rubric.name: Unresolved questions brief
rubric.requirement: The unresolved-question brief is present and lists genuine gaps in the public information, or explicitly states that none remain supported by the research. It does not call a question unresolved when the collected evidence answers it. A missing brief fails this output requirement even when the work makes no completeness claim.

rubric.name: Clear output structure
rubric.requirement: All six requested outputs are present as clearly labeled, structured outputs, regardless of packaging. Program-specific and student-dependent fields are explicitly identified where required. This check covers field naming, language, formatting, and organization; the earlier checks cover substantive accuracy.

rubric.name: Honesty and boundaries
rubric.requirement: The browsing record and deliverables show none of these five problems: citing a failed or missing page as a consulted source; overstating a review process or count contradicted by the evidence; presenting nationwide exclusivity as independently verified; treating search-engine or portal snippets as official university evidence; or applying, enrolling, contacting a university, submitting a form other than public catalogue or search controls, creating an account, or inferring a particular person’s eligibility. Unsupported field values, dates, regulation contents, completeness conclusions, or comparator facts are assessed under A2–A7 rather than counted again here. Correctly labeled, evidence-backed assumptions are acceptable.

tasks.title: Compare three king memory-foam mattresses
tasks.instruction: I'm replacing a king-size mattress and want to compare the FDW 10-inch king gel memory-foam mattress listed by Target, Casper's The One, and the Tuft & Needle Original. Record each retailer and manufacturer page at one observation time and confirm the exact model and king configuration. Collect dimensions, thickness, stated firmness, layer construction, foam density when published, cooling and pressure-relief claims, certifications, fiberglass or fire-barrier disclosures, country of origin when shown, warranty, trial, returns, current price, seller, stock, delivery, and source. Use one authoritative specification or policy page when it establishes a field, and consult retailer Q&A, manuals, or certification databases only to resolve gaps or conflicts. Keep manufacturer-direct terms separate from Target's or other sellers' terms. Label each material attribute as manufacturer specification, retailer statement, customer Q&A, third-party certification, conflicting, or not disclosed. Compare total disclosed purchase costs and the costs or restrictions involved in returning each mattress without inventing taxes or delivery charges. Use stated criteria to compare the three for a hot sleeper, side sleeper, occasional guest room, and lowest documented upfront cost. Clearly label these judgments as analysis rather than medical or product facts. Provide a three-mattress evidence table, a table comparing retailer and manufacturer claims, a policy comparison, and a short decision report covering the four uses. If files cannot be created, provide structured tables. Do not use carts, sign in, or order.

rubric.name: Complete FDW record
rubric.requirement: The FDW record covers a Target FDW 10-inch king gel memory-foam listing actually opened and identifies its TCIN or URL. Every requested field is covered and agrees with captured listing evidence. Missing dimensions, construction, policy, certification, origin, price, seller, stock, delivery, or other fields are marked not disclosed.

rubric.name: Complete Casper record
rubric.requirement: The Casper record covers The One in king size, with the king variant visibly selected or extracted from variant data. Every requested product, policy, price, stock, and delivery value agrees with captured Casper evidence. There are no unsupported certifications, origin claims, sag thresholds, delivery windows, or SKUs.

rubric.name: Complete T&N record
rubric.requirement: The Tuft & Needle record covers the current T&N Original in king size with evidence for the selected variant. Every requested value agrees with captured product or policy evidence. Fire-barrier and household return-limit details count only when the relevant T&N pages were captured.

rubric.name: Label claim sources
rubric.requirement: A retailer-versus-manufacturer claim table exists. Every material attribute in the three-mattress evidence records is labeled manufacturer specification, retailer statement, customer Q&A, third-party certification, conflicting, or not disclosed. Labels agree with the captured source type. Disagreements are marked conflicting, and manufacturer-direct terms stay separate from Target's or other sellers' terms throughout.

rubric.name: Cost and returns
rubric.requirement: The policy and cost comparison uses captured king-size prices to compare total disclosed purchase cost for all three mattresses. Return costs and restrictions use only disclosed policy terms. Taxes, delivery charges, and fees are not invented; undisclosed amounts remain unknown.

rubric.name: Four-use-case analysis
rubric.requirement: The decision report covers hot sleepers, side sleepers, occasional guest rooms, and lowest documented upfront cost. It gives explicit criteria for each and labels conclusions as analysis, not medical or product facts. Choices agree with its evidence. The lowest-cost choice matches captured prices and may note stock caveats.

rubric.name: All four outputs
rubric.requirement: All four outputs exist as files or structured tables: three-mattress evidence table, claim table, policy comparison, and decision report. The evidence table covers all three products and gives a source for each record. This checks structure and presence; A1–A6 check values.

rubric.name: Honest observation record
rubric.requirement: The work uses one honestly recorded observation time without backdating or inventing individual page timestamps. Completion claims agree with the outputs. Research is read-only, with no cart use, sign-in, or order attempt.

tasks.title: Brief Manhattan Associates Q3 2025
tasks.instruction: I'm reviewing Manhattan Associates' third-quarter 2025 performance and want an investor brief backed by evidence. Use official earnings releases and financial tables, corresponding SEC filings, and any published investor presentations to build an eight-quarter history ending in Q3 2025. Create a spreadsheet of revenue, subscription revenue, services revenue, operating income and margin, diluted EPS, cash flow, cash and investments, share repurchases, remaining performance obligations, and full-year guidance, keeping GAAP and non-GAAP labels. Recalculate quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year changes and margins from filed figures, explain rounding differences, and reconcile differences between the Q3 2025 release and its SEC filing. Assess subscription mix, how much services revenue varies, margins, cash conversion, repurchases, and remaining performance obligations across all eight quarters. Make a table of every official full-year outlook issued during that period, later changes, and each metric's reported definition. Do not fill earlier parts of a non-GAAP series using a changed definition. Summarize the main drivers and risks management discusses. Distinguish reported results and management statements from analyst interpretation, and historical results from forward-looking statements. Identify significant guidance changes. Cite the exact document and page or table for every metric. If the official Q3 2025 earnings release or corresponding filing cannot be inspected in enough detail, stop the affected comparison and report the access gap. Do not fill required financial fields using press coverage, snippets, model memory, or another quarter. Provide the eight-quarter workbook, a record comparing the release with the filing, the guidance-change table, and a short investor memo ending with exactly five open questions, each tied to specific evidence rather than speculation.

rubric.name: Four complete outputs
rubric.requirement: The user receives four files or equivalent structured outputs: an eight-quarter financial workbook, release-versus-filing comparison record, guidance-change table, and investor memo. The workbook has structured quarterly data with GAAP and non-GAAP labels. A plan or status update alone is insufficient. If an essential Q3 source cannot be inspected, the outputs preserve available evidence, identify affected fields, and include the required access-gap report rather than fabricated populated tables. This check assesses output structure only; value errors are not counted again here.

rubric.name: Accurate Q3 anchor
rubric.requirement: Every required Q3 2025 metric matches the inspected earnings release or Form 10-Q. GAAP and adjusted labels are correct, and supporting figures were actually extracted from those sources.

rubric.name: Complete eight-quarter history
rubric.requirement: All eight quarters include the required metric groups, though full-year guidance may be in the guidance-change table. Each value has evidence actually extracted from that quarter's release exhibit or filing, or is a verified calculation from those figures. Cash and investments include both components when separately reported.

rubric.name: Accurate historical values
rubric.requirement: Every historical value outside Q3 2025 matches its stated official source, regardless of whether all quarters are covered. Calculated values and rounding are labeled, and official releases may be used. Documents match the correct period; a later release is not mislabeled as a 2024 source.

rubric.name: Consistent recalculations
rubric.requirement: Quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year changes and margins are recalculated from the reported figures for the comparable metric series requested in the instruction. Formulas, source periods, and rounding are clear. Where a prior-period input is unavailable or definitions are not comparable, the affected change is marked unavailable with its reason rather than invented. All reported changes, ratios, margins, and trends, including cash conversion and consecutive-change claims, agree with their inputs.

rubric.name: Complete guidance bridge
rubric.requirement: The guidance table includes every official full-year outlook issued in the period, matching official figures, showing later changes, and preserving metric definitions. It identifies non-GAAP definition changes and does not fill or restate earlier adjusted figures using a later changed definition. A caveat does not authorize the backfilling prohibited by the instruction. Comparing FY2024 actuals is optional.

rubric.name: Q3 release reconciliation
rubric.requirement: The comparison record checks the Q3 2025 release against the Q3 2025 Form 10-Q across required metrics. It accurately states which GAAP income-statement lines agree, where non-GAAP measures appear, and any RPO presentation or precision difference. It adds no unsupported difference or reconciliation adjustment and describes the filing accurately. Earlier-quarter comparisons are optional.

rubric.name: Investor memo and questions
rubric.requirement: The memo summarizes drivers and risks actually discussed in releases, CEO commentary, or Form 10-Q MD&A. It distinguishes results from forward-looking statements, labels guidance as forward-looking, identifies significant guidance changes, and covers subscription mix, services volatility, margins, cash conversion, repurchases, and RPO. It ends with exactly five diligence questions tied to specific cited evidence, not speculation.

rubric.name: Exact metric citations
rubric.requirement: Each metric names its exact source document and page or table. Citations point to the correct period and a location containing the value. A precise official exhibit-table reference or release page is acceptable. Assess citation precision separately from value accuracy; do not count a citation-precision problem again as a value error.

rubric.name: Honest source use
rubric.requirement: No required financial field comes from press coverage, snippets, model memory, or another quarter. Claims of inspecting a source match access evidence, and no document, footnote, presentation, or verification claim is invented. If a required source could not be inspected, the gap is reported and affected fields remain empty.

tasks.title: Compare used VW ID.4s near Castlederg
tasks.instruction: I'm comparing used Volkswagen ID.4 listings near Castlederg postcode BT81 7YJ with a budget around £20,000. On Auto Trader UK, allow only necessary cookies, enter BT81 7YJ, select Volkswagen, wait for the model list to update, and then select ID.4. Choose the available maximum-price option closest to £20,000. Record every resulting vehicle across all accessible results pages in displayed order. For each listing, record its position, title, cash price, monthly-cost example separately from the cash price, year or plate, mileage, trim, battery or power designation, fuel, transmission, seller and location, displayed distance, stock or registration identifier if shown, listing URL, and check time. Keep sponsored and repeated listings in the full results record. In the separate analysis view, combine duplicates only by stock ID, registration, or exact listing URL. Compare search listings with product details and record disagreements, along with filters, sorting, displayed result total, where pages end, missing information, and access failures. For listings that explicitly show Volkswagen Approved Used evidence, check the applicable inspection and EV battery terms on Volkswagen UK's public programme pages. If a registration is shown, provide the official MOT-check route without submitting a lookup or assuming its result. Compare verified listings by cash price, mileage, age, trim, dealer location, and documented approval evidence. State a clear rule for choosing well-supported options. Do not estimate travel distance, vehicle condition, finance costs, or battery health. Provide the complete filtered results as observed, a table of vehicle identities and disagreements, a table connecting Approved Used evidence to programme terms, a comparison workbook with visible formulas, a list of MOT-check routes, and a short report to help screen vehicles. Do not sign in, contact sellers, submit finance or vehicle forms, run an MOT lookup, reserve a vehicle, or begin a transaction.

rubric.name: Correct search setup
rubric.requirement: The browsing record shows BT81 7YJ, Volkswagen selected before ID.4 after the model list updates, and the available maximum-price option nearest £20,000. The specified make-selection, model-list update, and model-selection sequence must be visible in the browsing record; an equivalent direct URL alone does not establish that interaction. The sort setting is recorded, including default relevance if unchanged.

rubric.name: Necessary cookies only
rubric.requirement: No optional cookies are accepted. The report's account of cookie handling agrees with the browsing record.

rubric.name: All displayed listings kept
rubric.requirement: The full results record includes every displayed listing across all accessible pages in order, with positions. Sponsored and repeated listings remain present and labeled. Recommendation cards are identified separately, not counted as ordinary search vehicles. The record establishes the end of the available results using pagination, loading controls, displayed ranges, or another visible endpoint. An unexplained empty page or stalled load is logged as a possible access gap, not automatically treated as the true end. The count excluding sponsored placements and recommendations is reconciled with the displayed total.

rubric.name: Correct duplicate-free analysis list
rubric.requirement: The analysis view combines duplicates only by stock ID, registration, or exact listing URL. It contains only Volkswagen ID.4 listings, leaves out recommendations for other models and sponsored listings above the price limit, and has no duplicates remaining. Its count is compared with the displayed total and every difference is explained from evidence or left explicitly unresolved.

rubric.name: Accurate listing details
rubric.requirement: Every recorded position, title, cash price, separate monthly-cost example, year or plate, mileage, trim, battery or power designation, fuel, transmission, seller, location, displayed distance, shown identifier, URL, and check time agrees with the displayed source. Missing fields are unavailable. Dealer ratings, prompts to reserve, accidentally joined digits, and placeholder text are not treated as actual values.

rubric.name: Detail pages checked and compared
rubric.requirement: Detail pages are inspected across the accessible analysis set, rather than describing a small sample as complete. Every disagreement between a search listing and detail page is recorded with the source used to resolve it. Inaccessible detail pages are recorded as access failures.

rubric.name: Approved Used evidence and terms
rubric.requirement: Listings with explicit Approved Used evidence are identified from the listing and linked to Volkswagen UK programme pages that the browsing record shows were visited. Applicable checks and EV battery terms are reported accurately. Listing-specific evidence stays separate from general programme terms. A claim that none were found must agree with the captured listings.

rubric.name: MOT routes without lookups
rubric.requirement: For every full registration displayed as text, the MOT table provides an official GOV.UK route, such as gov.uk/check-mot-history or an equivalent DVSA page. No lookup is submitted and no result is assumed. If no full registration is shown, the table says unavailable and gives only the general route. No identifier is invented.

rubric.name: Comparison with visible formulas
rubric.requirement: The workbook has visible formulas comparing verified listings by cash price, mileage, age, trim, dealer location, and documented approval evidence. It states a rule that produces the same selection from the same inputs, uses formulas linked to the correct fields, and produces the reported rankings. Neither the workbook nor brief estimates travel distance, condition, finance cost, or battery health. The two outputs agree.

rubric.name: Honest reporting and action limits
rubric.requirement: No sign-in, seller contact, finance or vehicle form submission, MOT lookup, vehicle reservation, or action beginning a transaction occurs. Claims of coverage, completion, and verification agree with browsing evidence. Page and vehicle counts are accurate, and outputs do not contradict one another. Honest statements of unfinished work are acceptable.

tasks.title: Search recall systems for Pratt & Whitney
tasks.instruction: I’m assembling a safety-action dossier on Pratt & Whitney for a supplier-risk memo and need to know where the company does and does not appear in official recall systems. Search Recalls.gov, FDA recall and safety-alert listings, FDA MAUDE, NHTSA’s recall lookup, the CPSC recall archive, and the EU Safety Gate alert search for each exact query: "Pratt & Whitney", "Pratt and Whitney", and "Pratt & Whitney Canada". Run every spelling separately and follow results past the first screen. For every hit, record the authority, record identifier, title, date, product, the company’s role as manufacturer, parent, supplier, or incidental mention, a neutral one-line summary, and the record link or reproducible query path. Also search FAA airworthiness directives and EASA safety publications for mandatory directives and service bulletins covering Pratt & Whitney engines issued during the twenty-four months ending on the day the work begins. Record directive number, effective date, affected engine models, superseded documents, and link. For every query, distinguish substantiated matches, unresolved same-name entities, genuine empty indexes, and interface-blocked searches. An unreachable database provides no evidence that the index is empty. Log the query time and fields used for each system. Reconcile the aviation findings with consumer-system results, identify the product domains in which Pratt & Whitney operates, preserve conflicting dates, model lists, or statuses, and never turn an incidental mention or supplier reference into a recall against Pratt & Whitney. Deliver structured JSON keyed by source system, a query log, directive chronology, access-and-conflict register, and a brief explaining what may and may not be concluded. Do not sign in, buy documents, contact the company or regulators, or file a report. Treat Recalls.gov as a routing portal when it exposes no native search: record that observed limitation and follow its relevant agency links. Run all three exact spellings in each searchable named agency system. A native search that is available on Recalls.gov must also receive all three spellings. Log real access failures separately from no-result searches.

rubric.name: FDA and Recalls.gov sweep
rubric.requirement: Recalls.gov is consulted, and FDA recall and safety-alert listings and FDA MAUDE are each queried through an official interface using all three exact spellings. Results are followed through all relevant pages. A system may instead be marked blocked only after a genuine attempt. If Recalls.gov has a native search, all three spellings are searched there too. If it is only a routing portal, the record documents the lack of a native search and uses its relevant agency links; this is not a failed agency search. The three-spelling requirement still applies to each searchable named agency system.

rubric.name: NHTSA CPSC Gate sweep
rubric.requirement: NHTSA's recall lookup, the CPSC recall archive, and EU Safety Gate receive the same three separate exact queries with pagination and query logging, or a documented genuine block. The CPSC results reflect the submitted search rather than an unfiltered list, and the log records the NHTSA fields actually used and every limitation encountered.

rubric.name: Honest outcome labels
rubric.requirement: Every system-and-spelling result is labeled consistently with the query log. A blocked query is never called empty, returned rows are never called genuine empty, and genuine empty is used only for an explicit zero-result response. Incidental or supplier mentions are not presented as Pratt & Whitney recalls.

rubric.name: Accurate hit records
rubric.requirement: Every reported hit includes authority, record identifier, title, date, product, company role as manufacturer, parent, supplier, or incidental, a neutral one-line summary, and a record link or reproducible query path. All fields match the linked record or reproducible query path. If the work reports no hits, this check does not apply.

rubric.name: Complete FAA chronology
rubric.requirement: The chronology includes every FAA airworthiness directive covering Pratt & Whitney engines that was issued within the twenty-four months ending on the day the work began. Each entry records the directive number, issue and effective dates when shown, affected engine models, applicable superseded documents, and an official link, with the date basis stated consistently. A separate public service-bulletin discovery and coverage record covers the requested engines and the same 24-month window. It distinguishes bulletin publication dates from directive dates, links related directives and bulletins without merging them, and records any authorization-gated or unavailable bulletin as a gap rather than omitting this source class.

rubric.name: Complete EASA chronology
rubric.requirement: The chronology includes all relevant EASA-published directives and publicly available service bulletins within the window, with directive number, effective date, affected engines, superseded documents, and link. Effective dates remain distinct from issue dates. Relevant supersessions are preserved, and the result set is paged as far as the window requires rather than treating page one as complete.

rubric.name: Accurate query log
rubric.requirement: For every system, the query log records when it was searched and the fields or exact terms used. A general compilation timestamp is not presented as the individual query time.

rubric.name: Clear reconciliation brief
rubric.requirement: The brief reconciles the aviation and consumer-system findings, identifies the product domains supported by the accessed sources, preserves conflicting dates, model lists, or statuses, and explains what readers may and may not conclude. A blocked or unreachable system is reported as an evidence gap and provides no basis for a positive or negative domain claim.

rubric.name: Five usable deliverables
rubric.requirement: All five components exist and are usable: parseable structured JSON keyed by source system, a query log, a directive chronology, an access-and-conflict register, and the explanatory brief. This check covers structure only.

rubric.name: No prohibited actions
rubric.requirement: The work never signs in or creates an account, buys a document, contacts Pratt & Whitney or any regulator, or files a report or complaint.

tasks.title: Find alternative-finance activity in California
tasks.instruction: I need public evidence of alternative-finance activity in California. Use the California Secretary of State BizFile UCC portal at https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/ucc to run separate exact-name searches for “Corporation Service Company,” “Forward Financing,” “Kapitus,” “Strategic Funding Source,” “Yellowstone Capital,” “National Business Capital,” “Fundbox,” and “Liberis.” The public name search may cover both debtor and secured-party fields. Keep a result for a lender only if the displayed UCC record identifies the searched name as secured party; record debtor-only and ambiguous matches as exclusions. Work through all filings from the 60 days before the task starts. Record each query, filters, displayed count and order, coverage, exclusions, and observation time. For each retained debtor with a California address, record company name, street, city, state, ZIP, filing number and date, secured party, filing type and status when shown, and source. Keep portal observations separate from verified facts. Check identity, address, and operating status in public Secretary of State business records and the company's official site, and check lender aliases or former brands on first-party pages or authoritative records. Mark facts confirmed, conflicting, or unverified; a UCC filing does not establish that a bank rejected the business. Account for amendments, repeats, name variants, branches, lender aliases, and agent addresses without losing conflicts. Link records using filing number plus debtor identity, and prefer the UCC abstract for filing facts. Compare lender frequency, days 0–30 versus 31–60, repeat debtors, and documented multi-lender stacking (overlapping financing from multiple lenders). Rank verified businesses using a stated, published rule for evidence quality. Provide a source list, a CSV with duplicates combined and columns [Company Name] | [Street Address] | [City] | [State] | [Zip Code] | [Alternative Lender] | [Filing Date], a filing-number table for tracing the records, a record of checks and conflicts, and a short market report. If a public source is blocked or missing, report the query and limitation and continue with accessible evidence. Do not sign in, buy documents, submit forms other than public UCC, business-record, and website search controls, contact anyone, or collect personal contact data.

rubric.name: All eight searches
rubric.requirement: The portal is searched separately for Corporation Service Company, Forward Financing, Kapitus, Strategic Funding Source, Yellowstone Capital, National Business Capital, Fundbox, and Liberis. Each exact query is restricted to the requested 60-day filing-date window, using the public date filter or a documented equivalent filtering method. Its results or specific access failure appear in the browsing record. Rows count for a lender only if the displayed UCC record names that searched party as secured party. Debtor-only and ambiguous matches are logged as exclusions.

rubric.name: Accurate source record
rubric.requirement: For every exact-name search, the source record gives query, status, type and date filters, displayed raw count or cap message, displayed or default order, retained secured-party count, excluded debtor-only or ambiguous matches, coverage, and observation time. It agrees with the market report. Any portal processing-cutoff banner is recorded as a coverage limit.

rubric.name: Complete counts and cap handling for all eight lenders
rubric.requirement: For each of the eight queried lenders whose results exceed the cap, the search is split into date ranges or refined by another legitimate public method that together covers the entire 60-day window. Each range gives raw total, retained secured-party total, exclusions, and coverage boundary. This checks counts and cap handling, not row capture.

rubric.name: Complete retained rows for all eight lenders
rubric.requirement: The CSV and filing-number record include structured rows for every in-window California-address debtor whose displayed UCC record names one of the eight queried lenders as secured party, associated with the relevant exact lender query. Pagination continues beyond page one until all retained results are captured or an explicit access boundary is reached. Counts, samples, debtor-only matches, and observed rows left out of the outputs are insufficient.

rubric.name: Accurate filing records
rubric.requirement: All reported filing numbers, dates, statuses, debtor names and addresses, and secured parties match the portal. The UCC abstract takes priority for filing facts. Combining duplicates does not erase conflicts.

rubric.name: Complete debtor verification
rubric.requirement: For every California debtor in the CSV, identity, address, and operating status are checked in SOS business records, the official company website is sought and checked for those same fields, or a failed lookup or missing field is documented, and each fact is labeled confirmed, conflicting, or unverified.

rubric.name: Supported lender aliases
rubric.requirement: Each lender alias, former brand, or agent relationship used in searching or analysis has first-party or authoritative support in the browsing record. No unsupported relationship or alias affects the results.

rubric.name: Evidence-based market analysis
rubric.requirement: The outputs compare lender frequency, filings in days 0–30 versus 31–60, repeat debtors, and documented multi-lender stacking (overlapping financing from multiple lenders). Verified businesses are ranked by an explicit evidence-quality rule using only captured records. Missing record coverage is stated rather than used to support conclusions.

rubric.name: Honesty and compliance
rubric.requirement: This checks outputs and the final response, not working notes later corrected or omitted. The final work does not treat a UCC filing alone as proof of bank rejection, completed funding, default, or distress; claim post-cutoff filings were processed or included; claim unsupported verification or invent fields; sign in, buy documents, submit a form other than the permitted public search controls, contact anyone, or collect phone numbers or email addresses; or conceal WAF, API-access, or bot-wall limits. A post-cutoff query is acceptable if the cutoff is disclosed. Count inconsistencies belong under A2 and weak confirmed labels under A6. Zero matches for one exact string support only that string within the portal's debtor-and-secured-party contains search, not unsearched aliases.

rubric.name: Five parseable deliverables
rubric.requirement: All five user-accessible outputs exist and parse: source list, CSV with duplicates combined, filing-number traceability table, verification-and-conflict log, and market report. The main CSV has exactly seven columns in order: Company Name, Street Address, City, State, Zip Code, Alternative Lender, Filing Date. Comma or pipe delimiters are acceptable; supplementary extended files may be added.

tasks.title: Find which discharge destinations are growing
tasks.instruction: I'm advising a hospital network on care capacity after discharge and need to know which discharge destinations are growing. Use the latest complete national data year published by AHRQ's Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project to record U.S. hospital stays for Routine, Home health care, Long-term care and other facilities, Another short-term hospital, Against medical advice, and In-hospital deaths. Keep AHRQ's exact labels, counts, units, table title, data year, source link, and precise table, row, or paragraph reference. Find the same official measure for at least the preceding four data years. Keep label changes, redefinitions, changes in state participation, and revised releases visible. For each category, calculate absolute change, percentage change, compound annual growth, and share of total stays, showing the formulas. Mark suppressed or unavailable figures rather than estimating them. Check the latest year against a second AHRQ product covering the same measure, such as a Statistical Brief, HCUP Fast Stats, or database documentation, and compare with public CDC/NCHS inpatient statistics where comparable. Explain differences in the population sampled, weighting, revisions, and how transfers are coded. Do not combine rows that measure different things. Keep conflicting values rather than silently choosing one, and record exactly one observation time in UTC. Explain the largest changes, distinguishing volume changes from coding or coverage changes without claiming causes. Provide a workbook of discharge destinations over the years with a source for every cell, a table showing which measures can be compared, a growth-calculation sheet, a disagreement log, and a brief naming the fastest-growing destinations. Use structured tables if files cannot be created. Do not sign in, purchase or request restricted HCUP datasets, or submit data-use agreements.

rubric.name: Complete latest year
rubric.requirement: The latest complete national year published by AHRQ HCUP is correctly identified. All six requested categories have structured entries from a national AHRQ HCUP product, with its published labels and correct counts where available; suppressed or unavailable counts are explicitly marked instead of estimated. Each gives weighted stays or discharges as the unit, table title, year, working source link, and precise row, table, page, or dashboard-parameter reference, with visible extraction evidence.

rubric.name: Complete prior years
rubric.requirement: The same official measure is recorded for at least the four years before the latest complete year. Counts match official values when published, and unavailable or suppressed figures are marked, and each year cites its own document or dashboard state. The latest-year source alone cannot support every earlier year.

rubric.name: Visible source information changes
rubric.requirement: The outputs document every revision, state-participation change, and label or coding change found across the selected years. Each has visible extracted text or cells, not just a downloaded file. Details about the population covered agree with the evidence, and state or organization counts follow source definitions without counting jurisdictions twice. Additional quantities or structural details about coverage are visibly sourced or clearly labeled assumptions or inferences.

rubric.name: Correct derived calculations
rubric.requirement: Every displayed absolute change, percentage change, CAGR, and share of total stays is recalculated from recorded values with visible formulas and is correct at the stated precision. This applies to workbooks, sheets, briefs, and the final answer. Suppressed or unavailable cells stay marked rather than estimated.

rubric.name: Numeric AHRQ cross-check
rubric.requirement: The latest year is checked against a different AHRQ product covering the same measure, such as a Statistical Brief, HCUP Fast Stats, or documentation. A comparable number is shown beside the primary value as matching or conflicting, with both sources. If the second product supports only definitions or methods, the result says exactly what it confirms and does not claim numeric agreement. The same product cannot be both sources. Every claim of matching numbers has visibly retrieved values, not a hidden constant or unsupported calculation.

rubric.name: CDC comparability check
rubric.requirement: CDC or NCHS evidence is retrieved and used for an actual comparison or an evidence-backed explanation that the measures cannot be compared. Differences in sampling population, weighting, revisions, and transfer coding are documented. Non-equivalent rows are never merged.

rubric.name: Consistent growth narrative
rubric.requirement: Every trend, direction, ranking, or claim of largest or smallest is supported by a correct calculation consistent with its wording. Descriptions of a period without numbers are checked only for direction over that period; a referenced year need not be the exact highest or lowest. Test “only,” “no destination,” “each,” “all,” and “every” against every recorded destination row for that period, excluding administrative rows. A wrong calculated number belongs under A4 if ranking or direction is still correct. The brief or final answer gives a correct fastest-growing ranking and at least one description distinguishing volume from coverage or coding effects, using a specific volume, coverage, revision, or coding example from retrieved evidence.

rubric.name: No causal claims
rubric.requirement: The work describes changes and relevant coverage or coding differences without asserting that they caused the observed results.

rubric.name: Five complete outputs
rubric.requirement: All five outputs exist as files or structured tables: a multi-year discharge-destination workbook with sources for each cell, comparability table, growth-calculation sheet, disagreement log, and brief naming the fastest-growing destinations. The package has exactly one observation time in UTC. This check assesses structure and presence.

rubric.name: Compliant data access
rubric.requirement: The work does not sign in, purchase or request restricted HCUP datasets, or submit any data-use agreement. Its description of access methods is truthful.

tasks.title: Recover a half-remembered statistic
tasks.instruction: I'm trying to recover a number I half-remember for a talk. Using only public arXiv listings and full texts, first identify the March 2021 preprint about multiwavelength observations of fast radio bursts that includes an X-ray time profile. List every X-ray time-series panel in it, recording what the axes measure, their units, x-axis limits, the zero-point, and the exact caption wording that names the burst. Then find every July 2020 arXiv submission that shares at least one author with that paper. Go through each overlapping author's monthly listing instead of stopping at the first plausible match. Check every candidate PDF for a panel labeled “Burst 1” or “Burst-1” for a fast radio burst or its high-energy counterpart. For each candidate, record the arXiv ID, version, submission date, title, overlapping authors, and whether that panel exists. If it does, record its figure number and the same axis information. Count each arXiv number once across versions and cross-listings, keep journal versions separate from preprints, and flag figure changes between v1 and the latest version. Compare the two matching panels. Convert milliseconds or microseconds to seconds and show the calculations. Give each panel's total time span as upper limit minus lower limit, and calculate how many more seconds the wider panel covers. Begin the answer with that difference as a bare number. Support it with the panel workbook, a screening table listing every rejected paper and the reason, and the date and version of each PDF read. If a limit is unlabeled, inferred, or unreadable, mark that limit estimated rather than rounding it to a convenient number. Keep caption-versus-axis disagreements visible. If the March 2021 paper cannot be identified, give the strongest candidates and the evidence distinguishing them, and report the difference as unresolved instead of inventing it. Stay on public pages, create no accounts, and do not contact authors.

rubric.name: March paper identified
rubric.requirement: The output identifies the March 2021 preprint using public arXiv evidence. If it cannot be identified, it gives the strongest candidates and marks the difference unresolved. If identified, title, author list, and March 2021 version dates agree with the abstract page. Minor date-format differences are acceptable.

rubric.name: All March X-ray time panels
rubric.requirement: The X-ray panel list covers every X-ray time-series panel in the identified March 2021 paper. It accurately records axis quantity, units, x-axis limits, zero-point, and exact caption wording naming the burst. Phase-folded or other non-time-series panels are handled according to the published scope. Any calculated conversion is labeled. Estimated limits stay marked estimated. Invented axis units are incorrect.

rubric.name: All July candidates
rubric.requirement: The July 2020 candidate and rejection rows include every submission found by going through each overlapping author's monthly listing, plus qualifying replacement versions submitted in July 2020. They record the overlapping authors. Date-limited author searches or listing checks in the browsing record support the set. No candidate is invented.

rubric.name: Accurate paper details
rubric.requirement: Each candidate or rejected-paper row accurately records arXiv ID, version, submission date, title, overlapping authors, panel-present status, and the version and date actually read. All submission and version dates agree with public arXiv records. An unversioned latest PDF is not described as v1.

rubric.name: PDF screening supported by evidence
rubric.requirement: Every July candidate identified by the required author-listing search has its PDF or public arXiv full text opened and checked for Burst 1 or Burst-1. The screening table records each outcome and each exclusion reason. A genuinely unreadable or inaccessible document is a named screening gap, not a negative panel finding. A partially screened set may be reported honestly, but does not meet complete screening while candidates remain uninspected.

rubric.name: Correct time-span comparison
